target.title: feat: advertise realtime voice provider voices in talk.catalog
target.body:
Closes #106020

AI assisted with Claude Opus 4.8 and Fable 5

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Talk clients could not learn which voices the active realtime voice provider supports. `talk.catalog` realtime entries carried no voice list, so the web and iOS Talk voice pickers fall back to a hard-coded OpenAI-only list. With any other active realtime provider (e.g. Google Live), none of the offered voice ids are valid, and picking a working voice requires hand-editing config outside the app. In the same projection, transcription and realtime provider entries silently dropped plugin-declared `models`, so clients could never render a model picker from them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirrors the existing speech-provider seam: `RealtimeVoiceProviderPlugin` gains an optional `voices?: readonly string[]` that core projects into `talk.catalog` realtime entries — the projection lives in core, so plugins cannot add catalog fields themselves. Catalog pick-lists now go through one shared helper: speech, transcription, and realtime entries advertise `models`/`aliases`/`voices` only when non-empty, which also fixes the dropped `models`. The wire schema (`TalkCatalogProviderSchema`) already allowed all these fields, so the change is additive. The OpenAI plugin advertises its canonical voice list (the same set its config validation accepts); the Google plugin deliberately advertises none because the Live API's valid voice set differs per model and Google publishes no Live-specific enumeration. Migrating client pickers to consume the catalog is named follow-up work, marked at the web UI site.

## User Impact

Talk clients can now read provider-specific voice and model lists from `talk.catalog` instead of hard-coding them, and realtime voice provider plugin authors can advertise voices/models with a single registration field. Shipped client UIs are unchanged until the picker follow-up lands (web/iOS still render their hard-coded lists).

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/talk.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts` (local Linux, Node 24; no remote Testbox/Crabbox available in this environment): 92 + 65 tests passed. Covers voices/models projection, empty-list omission on both speech and realtime entries, transcription `models` projection, and pins the advertised OpenAI voice set to the list documented in `docs/nodes/talk.md`.
- tsgo typecheck lanes clean: core, extensions, core-test, extensions-test, ui.
- oxfmt/oxlint clean on changed files.
- `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK on the rebased head — the new optional SDK field does not shift the API baseline (type aliases are recorded by name), verified by regenerating before and after.

target.title: fix: deliver completed replies when post-turn compaction fails
target.body:
Closes #94688

Related: #94928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could lose a completed channel reply when post-turn transcript compaction failed or the gateway restarted during compaction. The reply could already be present in the local transcript and Control UI while never reaching the originating channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

The turn owner now records the canonical, user-visible pending final before optional post-turn compaction. An ordinary compaction failure remains visible in logs but no longer blocks delivery when a genuinely sendable final exists; restart and stale-lifecycle aborts still fail closed so the old run cannot double-send.

The pending marker follows provider and successful-compaction session successors, and cleanup uses exact session ownership checks so an unrelated later rotation cannot clear another run's state. Silent, reasoning-only, heartbeat-only, and outbound-suppressed relay payloads do not manufacture pending-delivery state.

This is intentionally implemented on current `main` rather than by updating #94928: the older branch is conflicting and only catches the compaction exception. It does not make the completed final durable before compaction, so it leaves the restart window and successor-session cleanup unresolved.

## User Impact

Users can expect a completed reply to be delivered even if optional post-turn compaction times out or otherwise fails. If the process restarts in that window, restart recovery has a durable text marker instead of relying only on the local transcript.

No configuration surface or timeout default changes. Empty or intentionally suppressed replies still treat compaction failure as fatal, and successful compaction behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs `listTaskRecords` — a full cloned-and-sorted snapshot of all task records plus in-process generated-media activity. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless
- ClawSweeper confirmed the shape: "one canonical bulk pending-generated-media session-key snapshot that combines active in-process work with nonterminal persisted requester and owner keys"

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6: `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` covers empty set, in-process activity, requesterSessionKey, ownerKey, terminal exclusion, non-generated-media exclusion, combined snapshot)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests pass (mock updated to use `buildPendingSet`; two pending-media tests now verify correct sessionKey membership)
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests pass (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +131 −7 lines
  - `src/tasks/generated-media-task-activity.ts` — new `getAllActiveGeneratedMediaSessionKeys` export
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.ts` — new `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` helper
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — one snapshot call before the loop, `Set.has()` per row
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.test.ts` — 6 new tests
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — mock updated for new function
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `listTaskRecords`, `getActiveGeneratedMediaTasks`, `isTerminalTaskStatus`
- **Process-level proof:** directly exercised the real `sweepCronRunSessions` function with `vi.spyOn` on `listTaskRecords` to count per-sweep calls. The reaper was seeded with realistic cron continuation sessions and pending generated-media tasks, then called with `force: true`:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/_proof-session-reaper-batch.test.ts --reporter verbose

 ✓ calls listTaskRecords exactly once per sweep regardless of session count
   (100 sessions with continuations + 5 persisted tasks → 1 listTaskRecords call)
 ✓ preserves sessions with pending generated-media work, prunes expired ones without
   (protected key has pending media → preserved; expired + no media → pruned)
 ✓ captures both requesterSessionKey and ownerKey from persisted tasks
   (both requester and owner session keys included in snapshot → both preserved)
 ✓ excludes terminal generated-media tasks from pending snapshot
   (succeeded task excluded → not pending → expired session pruned)
 ✓ makes 1 listTaskRecords call with 500 sessions (old code: up to 250)

   [scale] S=500 sessions, T=10 tasks, listTaskRecords calls: 1, sweep elapsed: 2ms
   [scale] old path would have called listTaskRecords up to 250 times (once per continuation row)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- **Key findings:**
  - `listTaskRecords` (full cloned-and-sorted task snapshot) is called exactly **once** per sweep regardless of S=500 sessions — old code would have called it up to 250 times (once per continuation row)
  - All retention decisions match the old per-row contract: pending media keys preserved, terminal tasks excluded, both `requesterSessionKey` and `ownerKey` captured
  - Sweep elapsed time is ~2ms for 500 sessions (old path: O(S×T) repeated clones and sorts)

target.title: fix(ai): avoid websocket cache clobber on stale reused release
target.body:
Closes #105434

## What Problem This Solves
Releasing a reused ChatGPT Responses WebSocket deleted `websocketSessionCache` by session id without checking whether a newer same-session connection already owned that slot. A stale release could close/evict a valid replacement connection.

## Why This Change Was Made
The new-connection release path already guarded deletion with an identity check (`cache.get(sessionId) === entry`). The reused-lease release path and idle-expiry callback did not, so a replacement-before-release race could clobber the newer socket. This extends the same ownership guard to those async teardown paths.

## User Impact
Cached WebSocket sessions are less likely to drop a healthy replacement connection when an older reused lease later releases or expires. No config or API changes.

## Evidence
- Source: `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` reused `release` + `scheduleSessionWebSocketExpiry` now delete only when the cache still references the captured entry (mirrors the existing new-connection release guard).
- Test: added replacement-before-release coverage in `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`.
- Proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts` — 33 passed (Testbox warmup unavailable; local Vitest fallback).

When Slack auth.test fails at boot, or channels.slack.botToken is actually a user token (xoxp without bot_id), Socket Mode can still connect and previously published healthState: "healthy". target.title: fix(channels): progress drafts only for long tasks, with the model's own preamble as the status headline
target.body:
Closes #105872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord (and other progress-mode channels) showed an AI-written "working" status even for tasks that finish in a few seconds. The progress-draft start gate promised a 5-second delay but started immediately on the second work event, which nearly every tool-using turn triggers; the utility-model narrator additionally burned a paid completion on every small turn even when the draft never rendered. Separately, the narrated status was fully synthetic even though the model already narrates its own work in typed pre-tool preamble events.

## Why This Change Was Made

Small tasks should get just the answer; only genuinely long turns should show a working status, and that status should prefer the model's own words. The gate is now purely time-based (explicit immediate-start paths such as approvals and patches are unchanged), the narrator defers all utility-model calls until the draft is actually visible, and in progress mode the draft's status line is now the model's freshest typed preamble - always on, no new config - with utility narration only as filler when the model has been quiet for ~20s or emits no preamble. Preambles never start the draft early, so the time gate still owns the small-vs-big decision. The opt-in `streaming.progress.commentary` lane and its receipt counters are unchanged. LOC-ratchet compliance is paid for with real splits (`progress-draft-status-text.ts`, Telegram `progress-draft-preview.ts`, and small ownership moves) plus lower-only baseline updates.

## User Impact

- Small/fast tasks on Discord and Telegram no longer flash a status draft or an activity receipt; they get a plain answer.
- Long tasks show a status headline written by the model itself ("Reading the gateway config, then restarting agents.") refreshed as work progresses, with cheap-model narration covering silences; the final answer still carries the `-#` activity receipt and the draft is deleted.
- Operators stop paying for narration completions that were never rendered.

## Evidence

- Gate fast-path root cause: `createChannelProgressDraftGate.noteWork()` started on `workEvents > 1` (src/channels/streaming.ts); default delay `DEFAULT_PROGRESS_DRAFT_INITIAL_DELAY_MS = 5000` almost never applied.
- Eager narrator: first tool note always passed `shouldRunNow` (src/auto-reply/reply/progress-narrator.ts) regardless of draft visibility.
- Typed preamble lane (no string inference): embedded commentary normalization and CLI `onCommentaryText` both emit `kind: "preamble"` item events (src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts).
- Validation on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox (leases `tbx_01kxcm7g262wveq2pqqgr1yst5`, `tbx_01kxcrd3xm285wg71xz0sn4kmf`, `tbx_01kxcrwtc2ampzrvvrj5at85c6`): `pnpm test:changed` (auto-reply/discord/telegram/matrix/msteams/slack/compositor/narrator suites green after fixes), `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (freshness constant kept off the SDK barrels), `pnpm build` green (plugin-sdk DTS budget respected), LOC ratchet: this branch removes 2 violations vs origin/main and adds 0 (diff proof against stashed clean main on the same box).
- Known pre-existing failures on latest origin/main, unrelated to this diff and reproduced on a clean stashed tree on the same Testbox: LOC-ratchet drift on ~50 files (locales, embedded runner, cli-output, etc.) that cannot be baseline-raised by design, plus flaky broad-shard timeouts (live-network Telegram polling, ui custom-element re-registration); shard-level base-vs-branch comparison output retained in the session logs.

target.title: fix(chat): preserve explicit current-source sends in Control UI history
target.body:
Related: #104544
Related: #83494

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent could explicitly send a successful `message` tool reply to the exact current source conversation, while Control UI history omitted that delivered reply and showed only a later, different assistant final.

This PR addresses the explicit current-source `message` send slice of #104544. It does not address missing subagent lifecycle announcements, which are tracked separately in #105517.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit routes were excluded from message-tool history projection even when the resolved channel, account, target, and thread matched the current source conversation. The change adds a structured current-source route marker at the outbound owner and permits marker-backed successful explicit sends in the history projector.

Dry-run, suppressed, and explicit `ok: false` results remain excluded. Existing transcript delivery mirrors remain authoritative and are deduplicated.

## User Impact

Users who receive an explicit agent reply in the current Telegram/Slack source conversation can now see the same reply in Control UI session history. Later assistant output no longer replaces that delivered message in the dashboard.

Cross-channel, cross-account, cross-target, and cross-thread sends remain excluded from the current session history.

## Evidence

- Exact patch head: `8e1a56699c15d27847cf45065bb1305fa4868a11`
- Exact-head Control UI proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29226510248
- Proof artifact: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29226510248/artifacts/8269975305
- Patch CI: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29226510257
- Exact-base upstream comparison: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29226570970

The exact-head proof runs focused gateway/outbound regressions, projects a confirmed current-source tool result through the production history projector, and renders the resulting history in the real Control UI with Playwright. The uploaded screenshot shows the Telegram-delivered reply before a later, distinct final; the JSON artifact records rendered order `sourceIndex=0`, `laterIndex=1`.

Patch-specific checks pass, including formatting, lint, production types, test types, LOC guard, Control UI history proof, gateway, agent tools, embedded agent, and the focused outbound regressions. The full matrix currently has two failures: the exact-base branch already contains a stale dead-export baseline, and the locale-sensitive Control UI approval timestamp test remains flaky. The linked exact-base comparison is included to classify those failures independently of this patch.

## Risk And Rollback

Risk is limited to read-time history projection and the structured result metadata used to prove an exact current-source route. The marker is emitted only after trusted channel/account/target/thread resolution, and projection continues to reject existing non-success indicators.

Rollback is a straight revert of this PR. No config, schema, transcript migration, or persisted data rewrite is introduced.

## Documentation

No documentation change is needed. This restores consistency between an existing channel delivery path and the existing Control UI history surface without changing configuration or user-facing commands.

target.title: fix(cli): stop rewriteUpdateFlagArgv from corrupting positional --update values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`rewriteUpdateFlagArgv` rewrites any occurrence of `--update` to `update`, even when `--update` appears:
- After the `--` end-of-options marker (where it's a positional value)
- After a subcommand like `config set` (where it's a value, not a root flag)

This corrupts user input and can silently change values passed to commands like `openclaw config set`. Fixes #105923.

## Why This Change Was Made

The function is meant to support the old root-level `--update` spelling (equivalent to the `update` subcommand). The fix constrains rewriting to only when `--update` is used as a root-level command — before any subcommand and before `--`.

The fix:
1. Finds the `--` end-of-options marker and only searches for `--update` before it
2. Checks for a subcommand (first non-flag, non-flag-value word) before `--update`; if one exists, `--update` is a positional argument, not a root command
3. Skips long-flag value pairs (`--flag value`) when scanning for subcommands

## Evidence

```
$ npx vitest run src/cli/run-main.test.ts --no-coverage -t "rewriteUpdateFlagArgv"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed | 36 skipped (43)
```

All 7 tests pass (4 existing + 3 new regression tests):
- `--update` after `--` is not rewritten
- `--update` as a positional value for a subcommand is not rewritten
- `--update` after a subcommand is not rewritten

## Merge Risk

Low. The change only affects the `rewriteUpdateFlagArgv` function used during CLI startup. Existing behavior for root-level `--update` is preserved. The only behavioral change is that `--update` used as a positional value (after `--` or after a subcommand) is no longer incorrectly rewritten.

target.title: fix(config): warn on JSON5 comment loss after successful config write
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105683

Fixes silent JSON5 comment loss when `openclaw.json` and its `$include`-referenced files are written back to disk. OpenClaw parses user configurations with JSON5 (supporting `//` and `/* */` comments), but the canonical write path serializes with `JSON.stringify`, which irreversibly strips all user-authored comments, documentation, and commented-out settings on every automatic config mutation.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Previous attempt (#105727) added a regex-based detector with a pre-commit warning. ClawSweeper review identified three defects:

1. **Incomplete JSON5 line continuation handling** — regex only recognized LF/CR/CRLF, missing U+2028/U+2029
2. **Warning emitted before write commit** — rejected writes still alarmed users
3. **[P1] Uncovered `$include` writer** — `writeRootBoundJsonFile` (single-file `$include` path) also stripped comments silently

This fix:
- Replaces the regex with a **character-by-character lexical scanner** covering all JSON5 escape sequences including U+2028/U+2029
- Warning fires only from `logConfigOverwrite()` (post-`replaceFileAtomic`)
- `onCommitted` callback in `writeRootBoundJsonFile` extends coverage to included files
- Recovery guidance points to the pre-write `.bak` backup

#### User Impact

- Users with comments in `openclaw.json` or included files (`plugins.json5`, etc.) see a post-commit warning
- Warning tells users to diff against the pre-write backup to recover comments
- False positives eliminated: URLs, `//` in strings, all JSON5 line-continued strings correctly ignored
- Plain JSON configs produce no warning

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Tests:**
  - `io.parse.test.ts` — 11 tests (+9: lexical scanner)
  - `io.write-config.test.ts` — 103 tests (no regression)
  - `io.audit.test.ts` — all tests (no regression)
  - `mutate.test.ts` — 46 tests (+1: include-file comment-loss warning)
- **Change scope:** 4 files, +230 lines
  - `src/config/io.ts` — +68: `hasJSON5Comments()` scanner + warning in `logConfigOverwrite` (root writer)
  - `src/config/mutate.ts` — +18: `onCommitted` callback in `writeRootBoundJsonFile` (include writer)
  - `src/config/io.parse.test.ts` — +57: 9 focused scanner tests
  - `src/config/mutate.test.ts` — +85: 1 focused include-writer test
  - No new dependencies, no config/CLI/SDK/docs/changelog surface
- **Both write paths covered:**
  - Root writer (`replaceFileAtomic`): warning in `logConfigOverwrite` post-commit
  - Include writer (`writeRootBoundJsonFile`): warning via `onCommitted` callback
- **Real behavior proof** — actual `writeConfigFile` call against a JSON5-commented config on real filesystem:

```

====================================================================

Fixes an issue where agents inspecting omitted image content through live tool

enforcement. Already-projected images without data retain their existing

target.title: fix(node-pairing): require operator.admin to approve fs.listDir nodes (#105936)
target.body:
Closes #105936


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with only `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` scopes (without `operator.admin`) could approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`, even though invoking `fs.listDir` via `node.invoke` already correctly requires `operator.admin`. This is the same class of approval-versus-invoke scope mismatch previously fixed for `browser.proxy` in #104491.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval-scope resolver in `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` determines which operator scopes are required to approve a pending node pairing. It maintains an admin-level command list (`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`) that dictates which declared commands demand `operator.admin` at approval time. `fs.listDir` was added to the invoke-time admin gate in #105114 but was never included in the approval-time admin list, creating an asymmetry: the approval gate was weaker than the execution gate.

This change adds `NODE_FS_LIST_DIR_COMMAND` to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`, making the approval-time scope requirement match the existing invoke-time requirement. The approach is identical to the `browser.proxy` fix in #104491.

## User Impact

Operators with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` can no longer approve a node pairing that declares `fs.listDir`. Such approvals now require `operator.admin`, consistent with the existing invoke-time authorization. Existing approved pairings are unaffected.

## Evidence

- **Unit test**: `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes(["fs.listDir"])` now returns `["operator.pairing", "operator.admin"]`

```

```

- **Integration test**: Full `node.pair.approve` RPC flow via gateway — 12 existing tests continue to pass, confirming no regression to `system.run`, `browser.proxy`, or non-admin command approval paths.

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  12 passed (12)
```

- **Type check**: `tsgo:core` passes without errors.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an `operator.write` (non-admin) operator can approve a node advertising the `fs.listDir` capability, whereas invoking `fs.listDir` requires `operator.admin`; the fix makes approval require `operator.admin` too.

Real environment tested: drove the real `approveNodePairing` reducer through its on-disk paired-device store in a fresh temp directory — the real `requestDevicePairing`, `approveDevicePairing`, `requestNodePairing`, `approveNodePairing`, and `resolveMissingRequestedScope` all ran against the real SQLite store, with nothing stubbed (the store was seeded through the real pairing request/approve functions).

target.title: fix(agents): bound compaction planning worker payloads
target.body:
Addresses #100635

## What Problem This Solves

Compaction planning sanitizes private fields before worker handoff, but previously still sent full model-visible tool-result text and base64 image data through `workerData`. Large browser/command results or multimodal transcripts could therefore force multi-megabyte structured-clone work before summary-prompt truncation had a chance to help.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a planning-only projection before worker handoff:

- oversized tool-result text/content keeps a bounded UTF-16-safe sample plus omitted-character accounting;
- image blocks in user, custom, and tool-result content keep their type/MIME metadata but omit base64 bytes;
- token-pressure accounting remains conservative, so chunking and pruning decisions still reflect the original payload;
- local fallback behavior and private-field sanitization remain unchanged.

Image bytes are not used by compaction's text serializer, while image token pressure is a fixed per-block estimate. Omitting only `data` therefore reduces worker cloning without changing summary text or planning pressure. The pure projection helper is split from worker orchestration so both implementation files remain below the repository's 500-line guard (476 and 109 lines).

## User Impact

Long or multimodal sessions should spend less time and memory cloning redundant payloads into the compaction planning worker, reducing event-loop stall and OOM risk without changing compaction decisions or generated summary text.

## Evidence

- Final `upstream/main` rebase: `26210c16003f16768b02e989af773e536b15d6f2`; branch HEAD: `0899710631f6350c8fe34e238a9d12049415b0b9`.

target.title: fix(gateway): preserve accumulatedText on replace:true with empty text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where media-only upstream responses (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) silently erase accumulated assistant text in OpenResponses streaming. The fallback chain degrades to `"No response from OpenClaw."` — users see a wrong error message even though the assistant had already streamed valid text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText`. The sibling delta-emission path at the same function already guarded with a truthy check (`text &&`); but applying a broad truthy guard to the accumulated-text assignment risks masking a potential "clear buffer" signal from a non‑media empty-text replacement.

Following ClawSweeper review (P2), this change scopes the preservation to **media‑only** replacement events by checking `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media‑content signal used by `server-chat.ts:1101`. A `replace:true, text:""` event that also carries a media signal is a proven media‑only update and must not erase previously streamed text. Without the media signal, the existing "clear" behavior is preserved.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with `"No response from OpenClaw."` when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: When an upstream provider sends a media-only replace event (`replace: true, text: ""`, with `mediaUrls` or `mediaUrl`), the old `typeof text === "string"` guard unconditionally resets `accumulatedText = ""`, erasing all previously streamed assistant text. The lifecycle end fallback then outputs "No response from OpenClaw." instead of the actual assistant reply.

**Evidence**: See sub-sections below for redacted live provider streaming output, end-to-end SSE gateway transcript, shipped code evidence, and integration test results.

### Redacted live provider output

Real streaming response from ZTE Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct (multimodal vision model) processing an image + text query through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` SSE endpoint:

```
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":...,
        "choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":""},...}]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"L"},...}]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"ime"},...}]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":" green"},...}]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":""},
        "finish_reason":"stop"},...]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":87,...}}
data: [DONE]
```

The provider successfully streams deltas (`"L"`, `"ime"`, `" green"`) for a multimodal request. These deltas flow through the agent runtime's `emitSplitResultAsBlockReply` path (`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450`) where `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that the fix targets.

### End-to-end SSE stream proof

Terminal output from a local gateway instance started with the fixed code, sending a real HTTP request to `/v1/responses` and capturing the full SSE event stream:

```
=== SSE Event Stream ===
  [SSE] response.created
  [SSE] response.in_progress
  [SSE] response.output_item.added
  [SSE] response.content_part.added
  [SSE] response.output_text.delta → delta: "Hello "
  [SSE] response.output_text.delta → delta: "world"
  [SSE] response.output_text.done
  [SSE] response.content_part.done
  [SSE] response.output_item.done
  [SSE] response.completed → output text: "Hello world"
  [SSE] DONE

=== Verification ===
  Deltas combined:        "Hello world"
  Completed output text:  "Hello world"

  ✅ PASS: Accumulated text PRESERVED after media-only replace event.
```

The event sequence injected after the two text deltas (`text: ""`, `delta: ""`, `replace: true`, `mediaUrls: [...]`) mirrors the exact shape produced by the production agent runtime at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText`. The `response.completed` output text remains `"Hello world"` — the media-only replace event did not erase the accumulated text.

Test run across all three gateway configurations (gateway-core, gateway-server, gateway-client):

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Shipped code evidence

The event contract and guard pattern are already recognized in two existing shipped code paths:

1. **Producer-side guard** (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`). The agent runtime already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check:
   ```
   evt.data.replace === true && snapshotText
     ? snapshotText
     : ...
   ```
   This confirms the producer never treats empty `text` as valid replacement content — it has always skipped empty-text replace events.

2. **Chat-path media signal** (`server-chat.ts:1101-1102`). The existing chat SSE coalesce logic already identifies media-only assistant events via `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl`:
   ```
   !(Array.isArray(evt.data.mediaUrls) && evt.data.mediaUrls.length > 0) &&
   typeof evt.data.mediaUrl !== "string" &&
   ```
   This fix applies the same media-content signal to the OpenResponses path, narrowing preservation to the proven media-only case.

### Integration test

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts -t "preserves accumulated text on media-only replace"
```

```
 ✓ |gateway-server| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-client| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  2 passed | 64 skipped (66)
```

The test sends a media-only replace event (`replace: true, text: "", mediaUrls: [url]`) after two assistant deltas and verifies that `response.completed` still contains the accumulated "Hello world" text.

**What was not tested**: Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Non‑media empty-text replacement semantics (no known producer emits such events, and the existing shipped agent-runner guard already skips them).

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(ios): block omitted share attachments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103363.

The iOS Share Extension accepted at most three image attachments and ignored videos, files, PDFs, and unknown attachment providers while still moving toward the normal send flow. That let a user share partial content without any visible explanation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the current gateway media contract unchanged: the share route still sends image attachments only, and it does not attempt to add video/PDF/file transport in this PR.

Instead, extraction now records selected image count, accepted image count, and unsupported attachment classes. If the extension would omit selected content, the compose card enters the existing blocked state with a concrete recovery message, so send stays disabled until the user removes omitted items and shares again.

## User Impact

- Sharing 6 images now shows: `Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.`
- Sharing a video, PDF/file, or unknown attachment now shows an unsupported-item message instead of silently sending only text or the first accepted images.
- Normal shares with up to 3 images are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused local proof:

```text
SHARE_ATTACHMENT_SUMMARY_PROOF=PASS
Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.
OpenClaw Share cannot send 1 video(s), 2 file(s), 1 unsupported item(s) yet. Remove omitted items and share again.
```

Validation run:

```text
swiftc /tmp/.../ShareAttachmentSummary.swift /tmp/.../main.swift -o /tmp/.../share-proof && /tmp/.../share-proof
git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check
```

### Real proof

Exact-head native simulator proof for `5dda9040ac66350805428609bca660dd5373e6f6`.

Environment: iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.2 (`23C54`), Xcode 27.0. The installed app's `OpenClawGitCommit` is the exact PR head above. Both scenarios used the real Photos → Share Sheet → OpenClaw Share Extension path.

#### Six-image omission path

- Selected 6 photos in Photos.
- The extension rendered: `Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.`
- Send was disabled.
- After entering `Compare all six images`, Send remained disabled.
- XCTest result: **Passed** (`39.91s`).

![Six selected images show the omission warning with Send disabled](https://files.catbox.moe/91crio.png)

#### Normal one-image control

- Selected 1 photo in Photos.
- After entering `Describe this image`, Send enabled normally.
- XCTest result: **Passed** (`27.65s`).

![A normal one-image share enables Send after draft text is entered](https://files.catbox.moe/1vcxn8.png)

Focused commands:

target.title: feat(ui): render streaming chat markdown live instead of plain text
target.body:
Closes #106053

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where assistant replies streaming into the Control UI chat (web UI) showed the in-flight portion as raw plain text — `**bold**` markers, bare `| table |` rows, and unstyled code — until the whole message finished, then the message snapped into formatted markdown. The streaming renderer only formatted text up to the last blank line outside a code fence, so single paragraphs, lists, tables, and open fenced code blocks stayed unformatted for their entire streaming lifetime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Streamed replies are the primary reading surface in web chat; raw markdown markers plus the end-of-run reflow made them noticeably harder to read than the final render. The stable-prefix pipeline (markdown-it + DOMPurify with repo-specific rules for file links, sanitize hooks, copy buttons, and task lists) is kept as-is; only the tail handling changes:

- The streaming tail is repaired with `remend` (Vercel's zero-dependency `string -> string` incomplete-markdown fixer extracted from Streamdown, Apache-2.0) and then rendered through the same sanitized markdown-it pipeline. Unclosed `**` / `*` / `` ` `` / `~~` close instead of flashing literal markers, half-written links render as text-only, and math completion is disabled since this pipeline does not render KaTeX.
- Inside an open code fence, repair is skipped and markdown-it auto-closes the fence at end of input (CommonMark), so code streams as a live-highlighted code block instead of escaped text.
- Refactor while in the area: the uncached render core is extracted (`renderSanitizedMarkdown`) so per-delta tail renders stop churning the LRU markdown cache, and the now-unused `toStreamingPlainTextHtml` path plus its tests/mocks are deleted. Net −7 non-test LOC.

Alternatives (Streamdown itself is React-only; smd/Incremark/stream-markdown-parser replace the whole pipeline) are covered in #106053.

## User Impact

Everyone using the Control UI / web chat sees streamed replies render as formatted markdown while they arrive: headings, bold/italic, lists, tables, links, and code blocks with live syntax highlighting. No more raw markers or full-message reflow when a reply completes. Completed-message rendering is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/markdown.test.ts` — 104 passed, including new coverage: tail bold closes while streaming, half-written links render text-only, tables render before the closing row, `$$50` prose is left alone, open fences (top-level, in lists, in blockquotes) stream as highlighted code blocks, and the stable prefix still renders exactly once across deltas (cache reuse asserted via `md.render` spy).
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.ts` — 91 passed (streaming rows keep routing through `toStreamingMarkdownHtml`).
- `tsgo` ui + test-ui lanes green; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean on touched files.
- `remend@1.3.0` inspected from the npm tarball before adoption (zero runtime deps, Apache-2.0, Vercel); lockfile integrity matches the registry (`sha512-iIhggPkhW3hF…`); remaining lockfile diff is pnpm sort normalization only.
- Local test/typecheck fallback was used because Blacksmith Testbox warmup was failing (backend `context deadline exceeded`); hosted CI on this PR is the remote gate.

target.title: gateway: fs.listDir node pairing can be approved without operator.admin
target.body:
## Summary
A caller with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write`, but without `operator.admin`, can approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`. The same command is explicitly admin-gated when it is invoked, so the pairing trust decision is weaker than the command's execution boundary.

## Environment
- Commit: a674ce5e0d1ab0774546086fa7b2730516eca176 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: Gateway node pairing authorization and node-host filesystem directory browsing

## Steps to reproduce
1. Register a pending node pairing request whose declared commands are `["fs.listDir"]`.
2. Call `node.pair.approve` with an operator session containing `operator.pairing` and `operator.write`, but not `operator.admin`.
3. Observe that the pairing is accepted and persists `fs.listDir` on the node surface.

## Expected
Approving a node surface that declares `fs.listDir` should require `operator.admin`, matching the existing invoke-time authorization for that command.

## Actual
The approval-scope resolver classifies `fs.listDir` as a generic non-exec command and requires only `operator.pairing` plus `operator.write`. The accepted surface is then persisted by the real pairing approval path.

## Root cause
`src/infra/node-pairing-authz.ts:11` defines the commands that need admin approval:

```ts
const ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS = [...NODE_SYSTEM_RUN_COMMANDS, NODE_BROWSER_PROXY_COMMAND];
```

`fs.listDir` was added in #105114 and is included in `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS` in `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts:115`, but it was never added to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`. `approveNodePairing` calls `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` before it persists the node surface, so every `node.pair.approve` path uses the weaker mapping.

## Sibling surfaces
#104491 fixed the same approval-versus-invocation scope mismatch for `browser.proxy` by adding that command to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`. This report concerns the separate `fs.listDir` command introduced later in #105114. The command is live: it is advertised by the node command policy, accepted by the node host runtime, and dispatched by the `fs.listDir` gateway handler. This is not an unreachable or dead declaration.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram diagnostics and membership audits could keep waiting after the Bot API returned response headers but then stalled or only trickled the response body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram Bot API diagnostic body reads now use a Telegram-local bounded reader with the existing byte cap, a per-chunk idle timeout, and an overall body deadline. The change covers `getMe`, best-effort `getWebhookInfo`, and membership-audit `getChatMember` reads without changing fetch/header timeout or webhook best-effort semantics.

## User Impact

Telegram setup checks and membership audits now fail or degrade on a bounded deadline instead of appearing to spin forever on a stuck response body.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/response-body-timeout.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/probe.response-body-timeout.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/probe.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/audit.test.ts` (22 tests passed)

Command:

HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost node_modules/.bin/tsx scratchpad/telegram-diagnostic-exact-head-proof.mts

It called production `probeTelegram()` and `auditTelegramGroupMembership()` through the production Telegram undici transport, routing only the Bot API root to a loopback `node:http` server. It used a redacted fake token, no mocked adapter, no real Telegram traffic, and no credentials.

Redacted transcript:

```text

exact-head: f174acb7b443a366fed7048448884d226dab886f
apiRoot: http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>

server: client closed getMe

probe: mode=normal ok=true error=none webhook=none elapsed=6ms
server: accepted getMe mode=webhook-body-stall
server: accepted getWebhookInfo mode=webhook-body-stall
probe: mode=webhook-body-stall ok=true error=none webhook=none elapsed=156ms
server: client closed getWebhookInfo
server: accepted getChatMember mode=audit-body-stall

target.title: feat: advertise realtime voice provider voices in talk.catalog
target.body:
Closes #106020

AI assisted with Claude Opus 4.8 and Fable 5

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Talk clients could not learn which voices the active realtime voice provider supports. `talk.catalog` realtime entries carried no voice list, so the web and iOS Talk voice pickers fall back to a hard-coded OpenAI-only list. With any other active realtime provider (e.g. Google Live), none of the offered voice ids are valid, and picking a working voice requires hand-editing config outside the app. In the same projection, transcription and realtime provider entries silently dropped plugin-declared `models`, so clients could never render a model picker from them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirrors the existing speech-provider seam: `RealtimeVoiceProviderPlugin` gains an optional `voices?: readonly string[]` that core projects into `talk.catalog` realtime entries — the projection lives in core, so plugins cannot add catalog fields themselves. Catalog pick-lists now go through one shared helper: speech, transcription, and realtime entries advertise `models`/`aliases`/`voices` only when non-empty, which also fixes the dropped `models`. The wire schema (`TalkCatalogProviderSchema`) already allowed all these fields, so the change is additive. The OpenAI plugin advertises its canonical voice list (the same set its config validation accepts); the Google plugin deliberately advertises none because the Live API's valid voice set differs per model and Google publishes no Live-specific enumeration. Migrating client pickers to consume the catalog is named follow-up work, marked at the web UI site.

## User Impact

Talk clients can now read provider-specific voice and model lists from `talk.catalog` instead of hard-coding them, and realtime voice provider plugin authors can advertise voices/models with a single registration field. Shipped client UIs are unchanged until the picker follow-up lands (web/iOS still render their hard-coded lists).

## Evidence

Covers voices/models projection, empty-list omission on both speech and realtime entries, transcription `models` projection, and pins the advertised OpenAI voice set to the list documented in `docs/nodes/talk.md`.

target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks that were already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. This happens because the session is removed from the shutdown tracker synchronously before the hook fires asynchronously via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation`, and the direct-stop path (`handleStopAfterServerClose`) exits the process without waiting for these continuations to settle. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

The existing shutdown drain (`drainActiveSessionsForShutdown`) only covers sessions still in the active-session tracker when shutdown begins. Sessions already finalized by reset/delete/compaction are deliberately excluded to avoid double-firing. Their `session_end` hooks already run as tracked gateway root work continuations — the only gap is that the direct-stop path never waits for the root work set to drain before exiting.

Instead of changing the `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` signature (which would alter latency on every normal finalization path), this fix adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root work set to the direct-stop path.

#### User Impact

No visible impact under normal operation. On graceful gateway stop, pending `session_end` hooks now have up to 2 seconds to complete before the process exits, reducing the chance of lost plugin finalization writes. The wait is bounded and the force-exit watchdog remains armed, so a stuck hook cannot block shutdown past the supervisor stop timeout.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Tests:**
  - `gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 17 tests pass (+4: `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` success / timeout / immediate zero-count / poll-and-release)
  - `run-loop.test.ts` — 45 tests pass (+2: direct-stop drains root work before exit; warns and still exits on drain timeout; mock fix for new exports)
  - `drain-active-sessions-for-shutdown.test.ts` — 28 tests pass (no regression)
  - **Total: 90 tests pass across 3 suites**
- **Change scope:** 2 source files + 2 test files
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts` — new `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` helper
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — drain call in `handleStopAfterServerClose` before `exitProcess(0)`
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`

- **Real production behavior proof** — exercises the exact `handleStopAfterServerClose` code path using real `gateway-work-admission` functions (no mock):

```
====================================================================
  Gateway handleStopAfterServerClose — Real Drain Proof
====================================================================

┌─ Case 1: Session_end hook completes → drain succeeds ─┐
  ✓ root admission acquired
  [0.357s] session_end hook: starting DB write (400ms)...
  ✓ only hook continuation remains
  [0.358s] SIGTERM received → handleStopAfterServerClose:
  [0.358s]   getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount() = 1
  [0.358s]   gatewayLog.info("waiting for 1 gateway root work continuation(s) before stop")
  [0.359s]   → waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(2000ms)...
  [0.758s] session_end hook: DB write complete
  [0.763s]   waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain → true (404ms)
  [0.763s]   releaseLockIfHeld()
  [0.763s]   exitProcess(0)
  ✓ 1 root work continuation pending at SIGTERM
  ✓ no remaining root work after drain

┌─ Case 2: Stuck hook → drain timeout → warn + exit ─┐
  ✓ 1 stuck continuation
  [0.764s] SIGTERM received → handleStopAfterServerClose:
  [0.764s]   getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount() = 1
  [0.764s]   gatewayLog.info("waiting for 1 gateway root work continuation(s) before stop")
  [0.764s]   → waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(200ms)...
  [0.966s]   waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain → false (201ms)
  [0.966s]   gatewayLog.warn("stop drain timed out with 1 root work continuation(s) still pending")
  ✓ stuck work still tracked
  [0.966s]   releaseLockIfHeld()
  [0.966s]   exitProcess(0)
  ✓ process would exit despite stuck hook

┌─ Case 3: No pending work → fast path (no drain log) ─┐
  [0.966s] SIGTERM received → handleStopAfterServerClose:
  [0.966s]   getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount() = 0
  [0.966s]   (no drain needed — fast path)
  [0.966s]   releaseLockIfHeld()
  [0.966s]   exitProcess(0)
  ✓ zero root work → immediate exit (zero-cost fast path)

====================================================================
  Passed: 8  |  Failed: 0
====================================================================

✅ Proof confirms:
  • handleStopAfterServerClose checks getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount()
  • When > 0: logs info + calls waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(2000)
  • Drain returns true when hooks complete before timeout
  • Drain returns false on timeout → logs warn → still exitProcess(0)
  • When = 0: zero-cost fast path (no drain, immediate exit)
  • 2s drain budget fits within 25s supervisor stop timeout
```

The proof script exercises the exact production code path that runs on SIGTERM:
1. Imported `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`, `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain`, `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation` directly from source — **zero mocks for the drain logic itself**
2. Created a real `session_end` hook continuation via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation` (the same function `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` uses)
3. Released the parent root (session handler returns, session removed from shutdown tracker)
4. Called `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount()` → `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(2000)` (exactly what `handleStopAfterServerClose` does)
5. Verified: hook completes before timeout → drain returns true; stuck hook → timeout → returns false → process still exits

The `gatewayLog.info("waiting for N gateway root work continuation(s) before stop")` and `gatewayLog.warn("stop drain timed out...")` messages shown above are the exact strings compiled into `dist/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.js`.

target.title: improve(ui): restyle composer send button as filled accent circle
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The composer send button rendered as an outline ghost: transparent background, 1px accent border, and an outlined paper-plane glyph. Every other primary action in the Control UI uses the solid `.btn.primary` accent fill, so the single most important action on the chat surface looked like a secondary control, and the border-around-an-outlined-icon read as double-stroked and wireframe-y next to the rest of the design.

## Why This Change Was Made

Send is the primary action of the whole surface and should carry the same visual weight as `.btn.primary`. The redesign makes the button a solid accent circle with a white arrow-up glyph (the shape/glyph convention users already know from other chat products), keeps a muted fill while there is nothing to send, and drops borders from the stop/voice variants so the whole control family escalates via fill strength instead of outline strength.

## User Impact

- Send button in the chat composer and new-session start screen is now a filled accent circle with an arrow-up glyph; hover uses the accent-hover color plus the same glow as `.btn.primary`.
- Disabled state is a quiet muted fill instead of a ghost outline, so the accent fill itself signals "ready to send".
- Stop generating keeps its soft danger fill, now borderless.
- Voice idle/live states escalate via fill strength (10% -> 18% -> live meter + breathing glow) instead of border strength; behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Filled send (chat composer):
![chat filled send](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/composer-send-button/chat-filled-send.png)

Empty composer (voice idle tint):
![chat empty voice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/composer-send-button/chat-empty-voice.png)

Start screen (disabled muted fill):

target.title: fix(cli): rewriteUpdateFlagArgv corrupts positional values containing --update
target.body:
Fixes #105923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw --update` was rewritten to `openclaw update` even when `--update` appeared after the `--` terminator or as a positional value for another command (for example, `openclaw config set some.key --update`). This silently corrupted user input.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteUpdateFlagArgv` used `argv.indexOf("--update")`, which matches `--update` anywhere in the argument list. The intended behavior is to preserve the legacy root-level `--update` spelling only when `--update` is the first non-root-option token and appears before `--`. The fix scans past root options (`--profile`, `--log-level`, `--container`, `--dev`, `--no-color`), stops at `--`, and only rewrites the first matching `--update`.

## User Impact

Users can now safely pass `--update` as a literal value to CLI commands or after `--` without it being rewritten to the `update` subcommand. Root-level `openclaw --update` and `openclaw --profile p --update` continue to work as before.

## Evidence

### Real CLI behavior (after fix)

Using an isolated state dir on the PR branch (`08abe64`):

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof pnpm openclaw --update --help
OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (08abe64) — All your chats, one OpenClaw.

Usage: openclaw update [options] [command]

Update OpenClaw and inspect update channel status
```

Root-level `--update` is still routed to the `update` subcommand.

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof pnpm openclaw config set env.vars.TEST -- --update
Updated env.vars.TEST. Restart the gateway to apply.

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof pnpm openclaw config get env.vars.TEST
--update

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof cat /tmp/openclaw-proof/openclaw.json
{
  "env": {
    "vars": {
      "TEST": "--update"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "lastTouchedVersion": "2026.7.2",
    "lastTouchedAt": "2026-07-13T05:44:33.088Z"
  }
}
```

`--update` passed after `--` is preserved as the literal string value instead of being rewritten to `update`.

### Automated tests

Focused tests added to `src/cli/run-main.test.ts`:

- `does not rewrite --update after the -- terminator`
- `does not rewrite --update when it is a positional value for another command`

Before the fix:

```ts
rewriteUpdateFlagArgv(["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "foo", "--", "--update"]);
// => ["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "foo", "--", "update"]

rewriteUpdateFlagArgv(["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "update.channel", "--update"]);
// => ["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "update.channel", "update"]
```

After the fix:

```ts
// both leave --update unchanged
```

### Validation run

- `pnpm test src/cli/run-main.test.ts --run` → 38/38 passed
- `pnpm test src/cli --run` → 157 files, 2924 tests passed
- `pnpm format:check src/cli/run-main-policy.ts src/cli/run-main.test.ts` → clean
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cli/run-main-policy.ts src/cli/run-main.test.ts` → 0 warnings, 0 errors

target.title: refactor: canonicalize binary operation results
target.body:
Closes #106047

AI-assisted with Codex. Maintainer-requested refactor; transcript intentionally omitted at maintainer request.

## What Problem This Solves

Internal binary operations used multiple weak `{ ok: boolean }` shapes, so TypeScript could not reliably narrow success payloads from errors. The repository already had a sound discriminated `Result`, but it was buried inside the agent-core harness and unavailable to core callers; agent-core also duplicated unknown-error coercion.

## Why This Change Was Made

This promotes the tiny `Result<TValue, TError>` type plus `ok()` and `err()` to `@openclaw/normalization-core/result`, keeps the shipped agent-core exports compatible, and routes agent-core error coercion through normalization-core. Fitting internal operations now use discriminated results; public plugin SDK contracts, memory-host SDK contracts, and domain-rich outcomes remain unchanged. Package dist entries now derive from package exports so new subpaths cannot silently miss the build.

## User Impact

No CLI, config, or end-user behavior changes. Maintainers get compile-time narrowing for binary failures, structured error metadata survives agent-core coercion, and new fallible-operation results have one documented owner.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `578e0aecea65e6e9fbd168f186bc08c5bab060dd`.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcwmyzqkhy5atp4fzcye77y` ([run 29224666598](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29224666598)): `pnpm build`; 556 focused tests passed with 24 macOS-only skips; Plugin SDK API baseline passed; expected normalization-core `result`/`expect` dist artifacts present.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcx20hsyr4kqfwzrfb2qxjn` ([run 29224926865](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29224926865)): `pnpm tsgo:all` and `pnpm lint:scripts` passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: no actionable findings; patch correct at 0.88 confidence.
- `pnpm check:changed` reaches the repository-wide TypeScript LOC ratchet, which is already red on the exact base SHA for unrelated growth. Every touched over-baseline file shrinks relative to its baseline; the same base failure was reproduced before running the successful scoped/full gates above.

### Deliberate exclusions

- No combinator library; no current `map`/`andThen`/`unwrap` demand.
- No mass rename of domain result payloads.
- No change to `ChannelSendRawResult`, memory-host SDK result contracts, status flags, callbacks, or multi-arm outcomes.

## What Problem This Solves

The Devices page lived as a top-level workspace destination even though it is fleet/system configuration, and its layout had accumulated visual debt: three header buttons at three different heights, a redundant card title repeating the page title, a manual Refresh button on a page that already receives live presence events, plain-text rows with no visual anchor, and low-contrast "muted div" section separators that made pending approvals easy to miss.

Sections (Pending approval, Paired, Connected without pairing) use proper labels, header actions are two equal-height buttons (stale cleanup + pair), and the static card subtitle became a live "N of M connected · K awaiting approval" summary. The manual Refresh button is gone: the page already refreshes via presence/pairing gateway events plus a 30s poll, so the button was redundant surface.

## User Impact

Devices now lives where users expect fleet management (Settings → Devices, searchable from settings search), pending pairing requests stand out, every device row is scannable at a glance by device type and status, and there is no confusing manual Refresh button — the list stays current on its own. target.title: fix(subagents): credit requester-consumed descendant completions
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a lifecycle/delivery accounting gap for background and cron-owned subagent trees: when a requester actually consumes completed descendant subagent output, the descendant run is now durably credited as delivered instead of later being finalized as failed/suspended solely because no separate visible delivery event occurred.

## What Problem This Solves

Requester-owned subagent trees can legitimately consume descendant output without sending a separate descendant-visible delivery event. This is common for cron/background flows where a parent/requester gathers frozen child output, composes its own result, and then delivers that requester result outward. Before this PR, the descendant completion could remain delivery-unproven even though its output had already been consumed by the requester. Later cleanup/finalization could then classify that descendant as failed or suspended, producing delivery state that did not match real behavior. This PR gives the registry an explicit durable signal for that case: requester consumption is delivery evidence only for the exact descendant runs that were consumed, under the matching requester session/run-start window, when the requester path adopts descendant fallback output, so the consumed descendant rows do not later announce or finalize as pending just because the final outward send fails.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

This PR keeps the delivery model explicit:
- if a descendant result was visibly delivered, it is delivered;
- if a requester consumed the descendant output because cron adopted it as the requester result, the descendant is delivered by requester consumption;
- if neither happened, failure/suspension handling still applies.

## Linked Context

- Related issue: #92433 — subagent completion can be silently dropped when an announce handoff reaches a requester transcript but the requester run ends before consuming it. This PR addresses the adjacent durable-accounting problem for completions that *are* consumed by a requester.
- Related issue: #67777 — subagent completion delivery can be lost on direct-announce timeout, drain, or orphan prune. This PR does not implement the full durable inbox/spool requested there, but it narrows one delivery-accounting gap by recording proven requester consumption.
- Related issue: #86537 — suspended final delivery can expire and discard a pending subagent completion. This PR keeps requester-consumed completions from remaining indistinguishable from undelivered completions in finalization state.
- Related issue: #90299 — subagent lifecycle state can report lost active execution context while still surfacing child output. This PR contributes to lifecycle/state consistency when descendant output is actually consumed.
- Related PR: #92934 — required assistant acknowledgement for completion wake handoffs, so transcript commit alone is not treated as requester consumption. This PR complements that by adding durable credit for explicit consumed descendant run IDs.
- Related PR: #35080 — deterministic subagent announce delivery with descendant gating. This PR builds on that direction by making consumed descendant accounting durable.
- Related PR: #44205 — stale descendant cron fallback summaries. This PR keeps the same stale-vs-current discipline for requester-consumed descendant credit.
- Related PR: #95604 — Discord subagent progress feedback. This PR is not a Discord UI change, but accurate delivered/failed lifecycle state is useful to progress/failure-marker consumers.
No exact existing issue/PR was found for `markDescendantCompletionConsumedByRequester` or this exact requester-consumed credit mechanism, so this PR should stand as the focused implementation thread for that behavior.

## What Changes

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

## Implementation Notes

Core registry/runtime changes:
- Adds requester-consumed delivery metadata to subagent registry/delivery state.
- Adds a registry operation for marking descendant completions consumed by requester.
- Persists/restores the new delivery fields.
- Exposes the new runtime operation through the existing registry runtime shims.
Main files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.ts`
  - Implements durable requester-consumption credit.
  - Matches by requester session, explicit run IDs, and run-start window.
  - Records requester-consumption metadata and persists the updated run state.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.types.ts`
  - Adds delivery/requester-consumption state fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.ts`
  - Persists and restores the new delivery fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.registry.runtime.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-subagent-registry.runtime.ts`
  - Wires the new registry operation through runtime boundaries.
Requester-consumption paths:
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts`
  - Reads completed descendant fallback replies and returns both formatted fallback text and the consumed descendant run IDs.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts`
  - Applies cron fallback consumption credit when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output, before the final outbound send.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`
  - Credits nested/direct child completions when their output is included in the requester-consumed announcement/wake result.
  - Uses the same latest-child dedupe input for rendering and consumed-run credit so stale child rows are not credited.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce-output.ts`
  - Keeps latest-child dedupe reusable while preserving caller-specific fields such as `runId`.

## Tests / Verification

Coverage added or extended for:
- positive requester-consumed descendant credit;
- no credit for mismatched requester session;
- no credit outside the requester run-start window;
- no credit without explicit consumed run IDs;
- persisted/restored requester-consumption delivery fields;
- cron fallback credit only after successful outbound delivery;
- cleanup/finalize treating `delivery.status === "delivered"` as proof;
- nested/direct child announcement credit;
- stale-vs-current child dedupe, including a negative assertion that stale child run IDs are not credited when stale output is not rendered.
Primary test files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-completion.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.test.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts`

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `604bc96e3bc716e545455c9ebaa81ef147a344f1`

target.title: feat(goal-driver): completion contracts, wait barriers, and an optional completion judge
target.body:
# feat(goal-driver): completion contracts, wait barriers, and an optional completion judge

> **Stacked on #102261** (`feat/interactive-parity`) — only the last **3 commits** are new here
> (`82879720c8`, `21792a1a3f`, `67c5600a13`). Merge the parity PR first; this one then reduces to
> a small, purely-additive goal-driver series.

## What

Three opt-in upgrades to the experimental goal driver that make long goal runs **converge**
instead of firing continuations until the no-progress ceiling trips. 

### 1. Completion contracts (`82879720c8`)

`SessionGoal` gains an optional structured contract — `outcome / verification / constraints[] /
boundaries[] / stopWhen` — settable at goal-create time or later via the new **`set_goal_contract`**
tool. The driver folds the contract block into **every continuation prompt**, so each nudge restates
what "done" means and which constraints bound the work, instead of re-sending a bare objective.

- Absent or all-empty contracts are dropped on normalize → a free-form goal's prompt is
  **byte-for-byte unchanged**.
- Also fixes a pre-existing broken `completeQueuedChatTurn(2-arg)` call in
  `driver.integration-probe.test.ts` that left `tsgo:test` red on the base branch.

### 2. Wait barriers — gate g5 (`21792a1a3f`)

Goals can now **park** instead of burning continuation turns on async waits. `SessionGoal` gains an
optional barrier (`waitingUntil` epoch **or** `waitingOnSessionKey`), surfaced via the new
**`set_goal_wait`** tool (`seconds` backoff | `session_key` watch). New driver gate **g5**:

- While a barrier is set and unsatisfied → re-arm at the floor, do **not** fire, and do **not**
  consume a no-progress turn from the ceiling.
- A satisfied barrier (deadline passed / watched session's run ended) clears itself; the next wake
  resumes normal gating. Barriers auto-drop on any goal status change.

This is the "waiting on CI / waiting on a subagent" primitive: the goal stays alive without the
driver nudging a session that has nothing to do yet.

### 3. Optional LLM completion judge (`67c5600a13`)

Config-gated via **`tools.experimental.goalDriver.judge.enabled` (default: off)**. After a goal turn
completes and gates g1–g5 pass — and before a continuation fires — a bounded judge call classifies
the run: **`done`** → mark the goal complete (no continuation), **`wait`** → park behind the g5
barrier, **`continue`** → fire exactly as before.

- **No new provider plumbing.** The judge reuses the existing simple-completion utility-model seam
  (`prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` + `completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel`) — the same
  seam `conversation-label-generator` uses. `judge.modelRef` overrides the model if desired.
- **Fail-open by construction.** Unavailable model, transport error, empty/unparseable output, or a
  thrown judge all resolve to a normal continuation — a broken judge can never wedge progress; the
  no-progress ceiling remains the backstop.
- **No async-gap races.** The judge await re-checks the pre-fire gates before firing
  (queue-nonempty → re-arm; goal deactivated mid-judge → safe no-op), so a user message landing
  during judge deliberation behaves exactly like the sync path.

## What Problem This Solves

Today the goal driver fires continuations blindly until the no-progress ceiling trips: a goal whose
work is actually finished keeps getting nudged, a goal waiting on CI or a subagent burns its
continuation budget on "still waiting" turns, and each nudge re-sends a bare objective with no
definition of done. With contracts + barriers + judge enabled, a goal run converges instead: every
continuation restates the verification surface (contract) → async waits park instead of spinning
(barrier) → the driver notices verifiable completion instead of nudging a finished session until the
ceiling trips (judge). Each piece is independently useful and independently off by default.

## Behavior when you change nothing

None. No contract → identical prompts. No barrier → g5 passes trivially. No judge config → the
driver fires continuations exactly as on main. All config additions are `.strict()` zod objects with
help + labels wired.

## Example

```jsonc
// openclaw.jsonc
{
  "tools": {
    "experimental": {
      "goalDriver": {
        "enabled": true,
        "judge": { "enabled": true } // optional; uses the agent's utility model
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```text
agent → set_goal_contract { outcome: "PR #42 merged", verification: "gh pr view 42 → MERGED",
                            stopWhen: "CI green and merged" }
agent → set_goal_wait     { seconds: 300 }        // parked: waiting on CI
driver: [g5] barrier unsatisfied → re-arm (no ceiling turn consumed)
driver: barrier cleared → gates pass → judge → { verdict: "done", reason: "PR is merged" }
driver: goal marked complete — no further continuations
```

## Evidence

- **40** passing in the focused goal-driver suite (`node scripts/test-projects.mjs
  src/agents/goal-driver/`) plus **27** in `src/config/sessions/goals.test.ts`, including new
  suites: contract prompt folding, g5 barrier gating (fire/park/clear/auto-drop), judge branching
  (done/continue/wait), judge fail-open (undefined/throw), mid-judge race regressions
  (queue-flip / run-flip / goal-deactivated), and the atomic `requireActiveStatus` store guard.
  The race regressions were proven fail-without/pass-with: the pre-fix judge path fired/mutated
  unconditionally after the await.
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean (test-side was red on the base branch before commit 1;
  commit 1 fixes the broken `completeQueuedChatTurn` call in `driver.integration-probe.test.ts`).
