target.title: fix(agents): decouple MCP retirement from browser cleanup
target.body:
Related: #76233
Related: #101830

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a completed run-mode subagent waits for sequential browser-tab cleanup before retiring its bundle MCP runtime and starting completion delivery. A browser close request can wait up to the browser service timeout per tab, so one run with several tabs can delay MCP retirement, the completion announcement, and the next same-session turn.

The concrete sequential browser-cleanup delay is separate from the MCP lease-disposal race covered by #76233 and the related #101830 work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser cleanup is dispatched as independent owner-scoped work, while MCP retirement and completion announcement proceed after the existing generation and lease-safety checks. Browser operations hold a per-session access gate for their full request; cleanup takes the exclusive gate, so a successor browser turn waits safely instead of racing an already-issued close request.

The browser registry tracks the opaque run owner and an ordered ownership claim. Successor reuse transfers ownership; late predecessor callbacks cannot reclaim or remove the successor tab. Failed non-ignorable closes remain tracked for a later cleanup, and legacy unowned tabs remain eligible for cleanup.

`runId` remains an additive, optional Plugin SDK context field. It is host-issued, stable for the active run, opaque, and absent outside an active run. Plugins may use it only to key ephemeral plugin-owned resources and cleanup; they must not parse it, persist it as application data, expose it to users, or use it as an authentication or authorization boundary. The contract is documented in `docs/plugins/building-plugins.md` and covered at the `defineToolPlugin` factory boundary in `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`; the existing agent-context test covers runtime propagation.

## User Impact

Run-mode subagent completion no longer waits for the browser service to close every tracked tab before MCP retirement and completion delivery begin. A successor turn can start its non-browser work immediately and its browser work is admitted after the old cleanup gate releases, preserving tab safety. App-view MCP leases continue to defer retirement until their release path completes.

## Evidence

Branch-attributable CI repair:

- `check-test-types` previously failed at `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts(345,18)` because the successor fixture read optional `entry.startedAt`. The fixture now uses deterministic timestamps (`1_001`), and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-core-test.tsbuildinfo` exits 0.
- The previous `checks-node-compact-large-1` failure is `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`, which is unchanged by this branch. The same file failed in current-main run [29217990227](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29217990227/job/86717742399) at a separate assertion.
- The previous `checks-node-compact-small-2` failure is `test/scripts/apple-app-i18n.test.ts`, caused by the unchanged `apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabSections.swift`. Running that exact test in a disposable checkout of the PR base (`2f756c70a65ca345df10618b2900809936012028`) reproduced the same 2 failed / 11 passed result. No UI or iOS file is changed here.

Focused branch validation:

- `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts`: 88/88 passed.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`: 6/6 passed.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.test.ts`: 20/20 passed.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/session-tab-registry.test.ts`: 13/13 passed.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts`: 91/91 passed.
- `src/browser-lifecycle-cleanup.test.ts`: 4/4 passed.
- `oxfmt --check`, targeted `run-oxlint.mjs`, docs formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh Codex autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` reports the same pre-existing budget failure on base and branch (`public deprecated exports 3284 > 3279`, `conversation-runtime 4 > 0`, `channel-pairing 1 > 0`); this change does not alter the inventory.

Redacted runtime fallback evidence (local in-process runtime, no secrets or transcript):

```text
[runtime-proof/lifecycle] {"provider":"local-runtime-fallback","run":"old","session":"agent:…:child","events":["browser-cleanup-blocked","mcp-retirement-started","completion-announcement-started","completion-returned-before-browser-release","browser-cleanup-released"]}
[runtime-proof/browser] {"provider":"local-runtime-fallback","session":"agent:…:child","events":["browser-close-blocked","browser-close-released","successor-browser-access-resumed"]}
```

These are complementary deterministic barriers through the actual lifecycle controller and browser session registry, with the close/announce seams blocked inside the tests. The first proves completion proceeds before browser release; the second proves successor browser access resumes only after the exclusive cleanup gate releases. Identifiers are redacted. A browser-capable remote lease was not retained because the available DigitalOcean provider is SSH-only and its bootstrap was slower than the local fallback; AWS and Hetzner browser lanes were unavailable in this environment. The DigitalOcean attempt used provider `digitalocean`, lease `cbx_16823554cf26`, and was aborted before any runtime command; authenticated lease listing was empty afterward.

The remaining proof gap is a remote user-path run with a real browser service and captured completion/successor-turn timestamps. The source-level barriers and focused regression tests are present, but this environment could not produce that remote artifact without a slower or unavailable provider.

target.title: fix(ci): make TypeScript LOC growth reviewable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The TypeScript maximum-LOC ratchet introduced by #105894 had no legal path for legitimate growth: a changed file above the threshold, or a new oversized file, could not raise or add its checked-in baseline entry because CI compared that entry with the base ref. Snapshot baseline repairs therefore re-broke as `main` moved.

#105991 already excluded generated locale bundles. #106042 tolerates inherited drift, but intentionally still rejects changed-path growth, so it does not provide the missing approval path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make the checked-in baseline diff the explicit review artifact, matching the repository's other ratchets:

- The normal check still requires every tracked entry to equal the file's current physical LOC.
- Reductions still require lowering or removing the baseline entry.
- `check:loc:update` may record legitimate growth or a new oversized file for reviewer approval.
- The unshipped versioned-comparison machinery and `--base-ref` CI argument are removed.

This is the owner-approved enforcement boundary: CI proves the baseline matches reality; code review approves any increase.

## User Impact

Fresh repo-wide guard runs stop deadlocking on legitimate, reviewed TypeScript growth. The 500-line target and downward ratchet remain enforced.

## Evidence

- AWS Crabbox `run_bf68e8843b92`: `pnpm check:changed` passed on the refreshed patch.
- AWS Crabbox `run_54670c223a72`: focused LOC tests passed 8/8; current `pnpm check:loc` passed.
- Red/green approval proof: a temporary baseline entry lowered by one line failed with `grew`; `--write-baseline` regenerated it; the normal check then passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcydvj62pj0acv44q4qxmae`: `pnpm check:workflows`, scripts/root-test tsgo, formatting, and focused tests passed.
- Two fresh Codex autoreviews: no findings; patch correct.

Refs #105894, #105991, #106042.

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

## What Problem This Solves

Rewritten HTML uses a bounded four-entry compression cache; HTML, public files, and configured roots retain `no-cache`, and configured `.br`/`.gz` files remain directly accessible.

The bundled Control UI transfers substantially fewer bytes on cold loads, avoids request-time compression CPU for large static assets, and reuses fingerprinted assets without revalidation on repeat loads. Existing configured UI roots retain their current behavior.

target.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw does not currently have an official installable MXC sandbox backend for Windows hosts that can run sandboxed commands through Microsoft eXecution Containers. This leaves MXC-capable Windows environments without a first-party plugin path for ProcessContainer-backed execution and filesystem bridge operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an official OpenShell-style external `mxc` sandbox plugin package (`@openclaw/mxc-sandbox`) with Windows-only readiness checks, plugin-owned MXC SDK dependency ownership, ProcessContainer payload construction, a plugin-side launcher, host-backed filesystem bridge support, sandbox policy loading, and targeted tests.

The plugin source lives under `extensions/mxc`, but it is packaged as an installable plugin (`bundledDist: false`) so the MXC SDK/native dependency is owned by the plugin package instead of an unshipped bundled `node_modules` tree. The backend uses the current MXC `0.7.0-alpha` schema and keeps sandbox defaults conservative: strict plugin config, read-only isolated workspaces for `none`, a distinct read-only agent workspace for `ro`, writable agent workspaces for `rw`, fail-closed protected-skill overlap handling, guarded fs-safe host mutations, required explicit policy files/paths, and host-derived Windows baseline roots.

The MXC read-only skill mount resolver remains plugin-local instead of adding a plugin-specific public sandbox SDK export. The only new shared SDK surface is the narrow generic fs-safe recursive-remove seam requested by review because the sandbox bridge contract includes `recursive`/`force` behavior that the pinned fs-safe `Root.remove` API does not expose.

## User Impact

Users on MXC-capable Windows hosts can install the official MXC sandbox plugin, restart the Gateway, configure `sandbox.backend: "mxc"`, and run OpenClaw sandboxed commands through MXC. Non-Windows or unsupported Windows hosts remain unaffected because the plugin stays dormant when readiness probes fail.

Install command:

```bash
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/mxc-sandbox
```

## Evidence

Related: https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/626

target.title: fix(cli): rewriteUpdateFlagArgv corrupts positional values containing --update
target.body:
Fixes #105923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw --update` was rewritten to `openclaw update` even when `--update` appeared after the `--` terminator or as a positional value for another command (for example, `openclaw config set some.key --update`). This silently corrupted user input.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteUpdateFlagArgv` used `argv.indexOf("--update")`, which matches `--update` anywhere in the argument list. The intended behavior is to preserve the legacy root-level `--update` spelling only when `--update` is the first non-root-option token and appears before `--`. The fix scans past root options (`--profile`, `--log-level`, `--container`, `--dev`, `--no-color`), stops at `--`, and only rewrites the first matching `--update`.

## User Impact

Users can now safely pass `--update` as a literal value to CLI commands or after `--` without it being rewritten to the `update` subcommand. Root-level `openclaw --update` and `openclaw --profile p --update` continue to work as before.

## Evidence

### Real CLI behavior (after fix)

Using an isolated state dir on the PR branch (`08abe64`):

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof pnpm openclaw --update --help
OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (08abe64) — All your chats, one OpenClaw.

Usage: openclaw update [options] [command]

Update OpenClaw and inspect update channel status
```

Root-level `--update` is still routed to the `update` subcommand.

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof pnpm openclaw config set env.vars.TEST -- --update
Updated env.vars.TEST. Restart the gateway to apply.

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof pnpm openclaw config get env.vars.TEST
--update

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof cat /tmp/openclaw-proof/openclaw.json
{
  "env": {
    "vars": {
      "TEST": "--update"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "lastTouchedVersion": "2026.7.2",
    "lastTouchedAt": "2026-07-13T05:44:33.088Z"
  }
}
```

`--update` passed after `--` is preserved as the literal string value instead of being rewritten to `update`.

### Automated tests

Focused tests added to `src/cli/run-main.test.ts`:

- `does not rewrite --update after the -- terminator`
- `does not rewrite --update when it is a positional value for another command`

Before the fix:

```ts
rewriteUpdateFlagArgv(["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "foo", "--", "--update"]);
// => ["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "foo", "--", "update"]

rewriteUpdateFlagArgv(["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "update.channel", "--update"]);
// => ["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "update.channel", "update"]
```

After the fix:

```ts
// both leave --update unchanged
```

### Validation run

- `pnpm test src/cli/run-main.test.ts --run` → 38/38 passed
- `pnpm test src/cli --run` → 157 files, 2924 tests passed
- `pnpm format:check src/cli/run-main-policy.ts src/cli/run-main.test.ts` → clean
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cli/run-main-policy.ts src/cli/run-main.test.ts` → 0 warnings, 0 errors

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's main process-execution wrapper manually coordinated spawn, timeout, abort, output, and close races, while several production call sites bypassed that behavior with raw `node:child_process` calls.

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHeartbeatPreflight` in `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` read the workspace `HEARTBEAT.md` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, allowing an arbitrarily large file to be loaded into memory and processed by the heartbeat pipeline.

## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown; 1 MiB is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IDENTITY_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` covering normal load and an oversized file that exceeds the cap.

target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. Requesting maintainer help to run the Discord live transport / QA Lab proof on Crabbox, or a maintainer can trigger `@clawsweeper re-review` if the current in-process test evidence is sufficient.

target.title: fix(chat): preserve explicit current-source sends in Control UI history
target.body:
Related: #104544
Related: #83494

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent could explicitly send a successful `message` tool reply to the exact current source conversation, while Control UI history omitted that delivered reply and showed only a later, different assistant final.

This PR addresses the explicit current-source `message` send slice of #104544. It does not address missing subagent lifecycle announcements, which are tracked separately in #105517.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit routes were excluded from message-tool history projection even when the resolved channel, account, target, and thread matched the current source conversation. The change adds a structured current-source route marker at the outbound owner and permits marker-backed successful explicit sends in the history projector.

Dry-run, suppressed, and explicit `ok: false` results remain excluded. Existing transcript delivery mirrors remain authoritative and are deduplicated.

## User Impact

Users who receive an explicit agent reply in the current Telegram/Slack source conversation can now see the same reply in Control UI session history. Later assistant output no longer replaces that delivered message in the dashboard.

Cross-channel, cross-account, cross-target, and cross-thread sends remain excluded from the current session history.

## Evidence

- Exact patch head: `8e1a56699c15d27847cf45065bb1305fa4868a11`
- Exact-head Control UI proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29226510248
- Proof artifact: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29226510248/artifacts/8269975305
- Patch CI: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29226510257
- Exact-base upstream comparison: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29226570970

The exact-head proof runs focused gateway/outbound regressions, projects a confirmed current-source tool result through the production history projector, and renders the resulting history in the real Control UI with Playwright. The uploaded screenshot shows the Telegram-delivered reply before a later, distinct final; the JSON artifact records rendered order `sourceIndex=0`, `laterIndex=1`.

Patch-specific checks pass, including formatting, lint, production types, test types, LOC guard, Control UI history proof, gateway, agent tools, embedded agent, and the focused outbound regressions. The full matrix currently has two failures: the exact-base branch already contains a stale dead-export baseline, and the locale-sensitive Control UI approval timestamp test remains flaky. The linked exact-base comparison is included to classify those failures independently of this patch.

## Risk And Rollback

Risk is limited to read-time history projection and the structured result metadata used to prove an exact current-source route. The marker is emitted only after trusted channel/account/target/thread resolution, and projection continues to reject existing non-success indicators.

Rollback is a straight revert of this PR. No config, schema, transcript migration, or persisted data rewrite is introduced.

## Documentation

No documentation change is needed. This restores consistency between an existing channel delivery path and the existing Control UI history surface without changing configuration or user-facing commands.

target.title: fix(slack): add timeout to startup auth.test requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users starting a Slack account could wait indefinitely when the startup `auth.test` call stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack startup now bounds the boot-time `auth.test` wait with the existing shared timeout helper and keeps the current degraded startup path when that identity check fails. The change is limited to startup identity validation and does not alter Slack send, upload, or read lookup behavior.

This is an AI-assisted contribution prepared for Alix-007.

## User Impact

A stalled Slack identity check no longer prevents the Slack provider from reaching the existing degraded startup path and logging the same required-mention warning.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `bd1e78af217d16fcb20124042d896ec23aaf53d5`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/monitor/provider.auth-test-token.test.ts --reporter verbose`
- Result: 1 test file passed, 8 tests passed in 12.34s.
- `git diff --check`
- Result: passed.
- The fake-timer cleanup settles the deliberately stalled `auth.test` promise before aborting and awaiting the monitor, so an early assertion failure cannot freeze in cleanup.
- Autoreview was retried with `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`; the local Codex review engine exited before returning structured findings, so no clean autoreview result is claimed here.

## Proof

### Exact-head controlled Slack WebClient startup proof

- Exact head: `bd1e78af217d16fcb20124042d896ec23aaf53d5`.
- Scope: production `monitorSlackProvider()` -> production `createSlackBoltApp()` -> real `@slack/bolt` App -> real `@slack/web-api` WebClient `auth.test()` -> local HTTP transport. Neither Bolt nor WebClient was mocked.
- Harness: a temporary, uncommitted `node:http` server configured through Slack WebClient's `SLACK_API_URL` endpoint hook. It accepted `POST /api/auth.test`, deliberately withheld response headers, then released the underlying response after OpenClaw reached its degraded startup path.
- Redacted command form actually run:

  ```bash
  PROOF_HEAD=bd1e78af21 \
    HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= \
    NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost \
    /usr/bin/timeout 90s "$(command -v node)" --import tsx \
    scratchpad/slack-startup-local-proof.mts
  ```

- Redacted transcript:

  ```text
  proof: exact-head=bd1e78af21 controlled local Slack transport
  slack-api-root: http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>/api/
  server: accepted POST /api/auth.test
  runtime-log: [default] slack auth.test failed at boot (slack startup auth.test timed out); explicit bot-mention detection will be disabled until restart with a valid bot token; required-mention channels will fail closed without another trusted activation signal
  runtime-log: slack http mode listening at /slack/events
  monitor: degraded startup reached http listener path elapsed=10189ms
  server: released /api/auth.test after 10191ms
  monitor: stopped cleanly after abort
  shellExit=0
  ```

- Observation: a real Slack WebClient request stalled before headers, the production 10-second boundary returned through the existing fail-closed warning path, HTTP-mode startup continued, and the monitor then stopped cleanly. The underlying WebClient request is not canceled by the caller-side timeout, so the harness explicitly released it after observing the fallback.
- Not tested: live Slack credentials, a real workspace, Slack's public API/TLS route, Socket Mode, proxy/custom CA behavior, or a real Slack outage. This is controlled local production-path transport proof, not live Slack behavior.

target.title: fix(doctor): bound AGENTS.md and root-memory file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`shouldSuggestMemorySystem` and `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` read `AGENTS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and archived `memory.md` with unbounded `fs.promises.readFile(..., "utf-8")`. A malicious or runaway workspace file could OOM the doctor repair path before any diagnosis or merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `AGENTS.md` is only scanned for a memory-system reference, so a 1 MiB cap is plenty.
- Root memory files are markdown journals; 8 MiB is generous while preventing runaway files from OOMing migration.
- Existing `catch` behavior is preserved: an oversized/unreadable `AGENTS.md` is treated as missing guidance, and an oversized memory pair is archived but not merged.

## User Impact

- `openclaw doctor` workspace memory checks no longer buffer arbitrarily large files.
- Oversized `AGENTS.md` / memory files are handled gracefully instead of crashing.
- Normal workspace doctor flows work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` calls with `readRegularFile` capped reads in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts` covering an oversized `AGENTS.md` and an oversized legacy memory file.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts --run
  # 5 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created a standalone Node script at `/tmp/proof-101448.mjs` that imports the real helpers from `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` and exercises both the normal and oversized paths in isolated temp workspaces:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101448.mjs
=== OpenClaw PR 101448 real behavior proof ===

Normal AGENTS.md -> shouldSuggestMemorySystem = false
  (expected false because AGENTS.md references MEMORY.md)

Oversized AGENTS.md (2 MiB) -> shouldSuggestMemorySystem = true
  (expected true: oversized file is treated as missing guidance)

Normal split-brain root memory -> migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile:
  changed: true
  mergedLegacy: true
  archiveOnly: false
  (expected changed=true, mergedLegacy=true, archiveOnly=false)

Oversized legacy memory.md (9 MiB) -> migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile:
  changed: true
  mergedLegacy: false
  archiveOnly: true
  archivedLegacyPath: /tmp/proof-101448-VTwxDZ/.openclaw-repair/root-memory/2026-07-07T10-29-48-239Z/memory.md
  (expected changed=true, mergedLegacy=false, archiveOnly=true)
```

Interpretation:

- Normal inputs continue to work: a workspace with a conventional `AGENTS.md` referencing `MEMORY.md` is recognized as already having memory guidance, and a normal split-brain `MEMORY.md`/`memory.md` pair is merged.
- Oversized inputs are rejected before any downstream processing: a 2 MiB `AGENTS.md` exceeds the 1 MiB cap and is treated as missing guidance, and a 9 MiB legacy `memory.md` exceeds the 8 MiB cap so the legacy file is archived but its content is not merged into `MEMORY.md` (`archiveOnly: true`).

target.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.
- Dreaming/consolidation can be selected separately from ordinary recall where supported.
- Memory Wiki can remain a companion compiled-knowledge layer beside active memory providers.
- Existing configs using `plugins.slots.memory` continue to work as recall selection.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` can migrate/canonicalize non-conflicting legacy memory-slot config while preserving the legacy key for plugin compatibility.

## Linked Context

Closes #60572.

Directly related memory-composition requests and prior proposals:

- #38874: supplementary/additive memory plugins alongside the primary memory slot.
- #2306: earlier closed PR proposing stackable memory plugins.
- #2080: earlier request for multiple simultaneous memory plugins and emerging memory architectures.
- #77714: pluggable persistent memory backend demand.

Dreaming and memory-role separation context:

- #85473: future protocol work for making dreaming implementable by non-`memory-core` memory plugins. This PR adds the `memory.dreaming` slot contract but does not implement that full protocol.
- #63067 and #65411: prior work around keeping dreaming behavior available when another plugin owns the legacy memory slot.
- #62275: previous selected-slot dreaming config behavior.

Runtime/diagnostic slot handling context:

- #76567 and #76495: configured memory-slot runtime checks should load/consult the selected memory plugin.
- #78540: doctor/status memory diagnostics could misreport configured memory providers.
- #76550: stale `plugins.slots.*` references could leave config unrecoverable until doctor cleanup was broadened.

Context-engine compatibility context:

- #77063, #77185, #76576, and #81843: context-engine registration and LosslessClaw-adjacent failures shaped the compatibility review for preserving the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` behavior while rejecting unsupported per-agent `contextEngine` config.

Future API/RFC context:

- #70823: future machine-readable slot ownership/provenance. This PR intentionally keeps scalar plugin IDs and solves the memory role composition layer first.

Memory-plugin interop research: the [supporting research document](https://github.com/kklouzal/rfcs/blob/rfc/multi-slot-memory-role-architecture/rfcs/0009/memory-plugin-interop-research.md) validates this PR as necessary architecture work, not optional extensibility: OpenClaw's own documentation already describes memory as a composable ecosystem where builtin/QMD recall, Honcho user/session modeling, LanceDB recall/capture, Active Memory orchestration, dreaming/consolidation, and Memory Wiki compilation can coexist, but current `origin/main` collapses every `kind: "memory"` provider into one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner, making those documented combinations impossible or dependent on brittle exceptions. PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Adds canonical memory role slots: `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel`.
- Keeps legacy `plugins.slots.memory` as a backward-compatible shorthand for `memory.recall` during an extended migration window.
- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.
- Wires role-slot selection through config schema/types/help/docs, plugin activation, gateway startup preloading, runtime memory resolution, skill publishing, validation, doctor repair/preview, uninstall cleanup, status diagnostics, and SDK-facing aliases.
- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

## Tests / Verification

Current PR branch:

target.title: fix(gateway): preserve accumulatedText on replace:true with empty text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where media-only upstream responses (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) silently erase accumulated assistant text in OpenResponses streaming. The fallback chain degrades to `"No response from OpenClaw."` — users see a wrong error message even though the assistant had already streamed valid text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText`. The sibling delta-emission path at the same function already guarded with a truthy check (`text &&`); but applying a broad truthy guard to the accumulated-text assignment risks masking a potential "clear buffer" signal from a non‑media empty-text replacement.

Following ClawSweeper review (P2), this change scopes the preservation to **media‑only** replacement events by checking `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media‑content signal used by `server-chat.ts:1101`. A `replace:true, text:""` event that also carries a media signal is a proven media‑only update and must not erase previously streamed text. Without the media signal, the existing "clear" behavior is preserved.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with `"No response from OpenClaw."` when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: When an upstream provider sends a media-only replace event (`replace: true, text: ""`, with `mediaUrls` or `mediaUrl`), the old `typeof text === "string"` guard unconditionally resets `accumulatedText = ""`, erasing all previously streamed assistant text. The lifecycle end fallback then outputs "No response from OpenClaw." instead of the actual assistant reply.

**Evidence**: See sub-sections below for redacted live provider streaming output, end-to-end SSE gateway transcript, shipped code evidence, and integration test results.

### Redacted live provider output

Real streaming response from ZTE Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct (multimodal vision model) processing an image + text query through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` SSE endpoint:

```
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":...,
        "choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":""},...}]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"L"},...}]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"ime"},...}]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":" green"},...}]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":""},
        "finish_reason":"stop"},...]}
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","choices":[],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":87,...}}
data: [DONE]
```

The provider successfully streams deltas (`"L"`, `"ime"`, `" green"`) for a multimodal request. These deltas flow through the agent runtime's `emitSplitResultAsBlockReply` path (`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450`) where `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that the fix targets.

### End-to-end SSE stream proof

Terminal output from a local gateway instance started with the fixed code, sending a real HTTP request to `/v1/responses` and capturing the full SSE event stream:

```
=== SSE Event Stream ===
  [SSE] response.created
  [SSE] response.in_progress
  [SSE] response.output_item.added
  [SSE] response.content_part.added
  [SSE] response.output_text.delta → delta: "Hello "
  [SSE] response.output_text.delta → delta: "world"
  [SSE] response.output_text.done
  [SSE] response.content_part.done
  [SSE] response.output_item.done
  [SSE] response.completed → output text: "Hello world"
  [SSE] DONE

=== Verification ===
  Deltas combined:        "Hello world"
  Completed output text:  "Hello world"

  ✅ PASS: Accumulated text PRESERVED after media-only replace event.
```

The event sequence injected after the two text deltas (`text: ""`, `delta: ""`, `replace: true`, `mediaUrls: [...]`) mirrors the exact shape produced by the production agent runtime at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText`. The `response.completed` output text remains `"Hello world"` — the media-only replace event did not erase the accumulated text.

Test run across all three gateway configurations (gateway-core, gateway-server, gateway-client):

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Shipped code evidence

The event contract and guard pattern are already recognized in two existing shipped code paths:

1. **Producer-side guard** (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`). The agent runtime already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check:
   ```
   evt.data.replace === true && snapshotText
     ? snapshotText
     : ...
   ```
   This confirms the producer never treats empty `text` as valid replacement content — it has always skipped empty-text replace events.

2. **Chat-path media signal** (`server-chat.ts:1101-1102`). The existing chat SSE coalesce logic already identifies media-only assistant events via `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl`:
   ```
   !(Array.isArray(evt.data.mediaUrls) && evt.data.mediaUrls.length > 0) &&
   typeof evt.data.mediaUrl !== "string" &&
   ```
   This fix applies the same media-content signal to the OpenResponses path, narrowing preservation to the proven media-only case.

### Integration test

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts -t "preserves accumulated text on media-only replace"
```

```
 ✓ |gateway-server| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-client| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  2 passed | 64 skipped (66)
```

The test sends a media-only replace event (`replace: true, text: "", mediaUrls: [url]`) after two assistant deltas and verifies that `response.completed` still contains the accumulated "Hello world" text.

**What was not tested**: Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Non‑media empty-text replacement semantics (no known producer emits such events, and the existing shipped agent-runner guard already skips them).

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two channel reliability bugs in the Telegram plugin where shutdown paths can produce unhandled promise rejections, which Node.js terminates the process for by default:

1. **Webhook shutdown**: if `bot.stop()` rejected during abort-triggered shutdown, the rejection was unhandled (`void shutdown()`), crashing the process.
2. **Ingress worker stop**: `stop()` was not idempotent, so calling it twice could post a second `stop` message and leak a second 15s terminate timer. If `worker.terminate()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Webhook**: catch shutdown errors in both the pre-aborted path and the abort listener, route them to `runtime.error`, and continue owned cleanup (transport close, status, diagnostics) in a `finally` block even if `bot.stop()` rejects.
- **Ingress worker**: guard `stop()` with a `stopped` flag for idempotency, catch `postMessage` errors for already-terminated workers, and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.

## User Impact

No more unhandled rejection crashes during Telegram channel restart or shutdown.

## Evidence

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
```

### Negative Control Proof

**Webhook shutdown rejection handling**:

```bash
# Step 1: Revert to origin/main version
git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts

# Step 2: Run test - Expected: FAIL with Unhandled Rejection
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled rejections when shutdown throws"
```

Result: ❌ **FAILED** - Unhandled Rejection: Error: bot stop failed

```bash
# Step 3: Restore fix
git checkout HEAD -- extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts

# Step 4: Run test - Expected: PASS
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled rejections when shutdown throws"
```

Result: ✅ **PASSED** - 1 passed

**Ingress worker stop idempotency**:

```bash
# Step 1: Revert to origin/main version
git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts

# Step 2: Run test - Expected: FAIL
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Result: ❌ **FAILED** - AssertionError: expected Promise{…} to be Promise{…} (stop() not idempotent)

```bash
# Step 3: Restore fix
git checkout HEAD -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts

# Step 4: Run test - Expected: ALL PASS
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Result: ✅ **PASSED** - 2 passed

### Changes

- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts`: catch shutdown errors in abort paths, log via `runtime.error`, continue cleanup in `finally`
- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts`: new test for shutdown rejection handling
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts`: idempotent `stop()` with shared stop promise, catch `postMessage` and `terminate` errors
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts`: new tests for stop idempotency and terminate rejection handling

target.title: feat(discord): show subagent progress
target.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in Discord-scoped sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message, including count reactions, durable failure marker behavior, and typing keepalive while tracked work is active.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users currently have little visible feedback when an assistant turn delegates work to tracked sub-agents. Long-running turns can look idle after the initial message even though background sub-agents are still running, and a sub-agent failure is not visible on the original Discord message.

Discord also cannot represent concurrent work by adding the same emoji reaction multiple times from the same bot/user, so progress needs a count-based reaction model instead of repeated identical reactions.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Discord users get immediate, lightweight progress feedback during delegated work without waiting for the final assistant reply:

- `1️⃣`, `2️⃣`, etc. show the current active tracked sub-agent count for the turn
- the count reaction is replaced as the active count changes
- the count reaction disappears when no tracked sub-agents remain active
- `🔴` remains if any tracked sub-agent ends with a non-OK outcome
- typing stays active while tracked sub-agents are still running

Operators can configure the behavior with `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, including reaction progress, count emoji, failure emoji, typing keepalive, interval, and max-duration TTL.

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## Linked Context

No linked issues or external context were listed in the current PR body.

## What Changes

This PR adds Discord-scoped, best-effort sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message. The feature is opt-in with `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`.

When enabled:

- one configurable count reaction shows the number of currently active tracked sub-agents (`1️⃣` … `🔟` by default)
- count changes replace the previous count reaction instead of accumulating multiple ordinal reactions
- zero active tracked sub-agents removes the count reaction
- any non-OK completion leaves a durable configurable failure marker (`🔴` by default)
- Discord typing is kept alive independently while tracked sub-agents remain active, then stops when all tracked work finishes or the safety TTL expires

The implementation threads the source Discord message id through native `sessions_spawn`, tracked ACP spawn, requester origin metadata, and internal Discord progress hook handling so the Discord extension can target the correct parent message. Non-Discord callers and callers without a source message id keep existing behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds source/current message id propagation through delivery context and `sessions_spawn` tool context.
- Carries that id into native sub-agent spawn and tracked ACP registration.
- Keeps public plugin hook/requester metadata narrow while the Discord extension uses an internal Discord-only event shape for source-message progress targeting.
- Emits progress cleanup at run completion even when ordinary `subagent_ended` delivery is deferred.
- Adds a Discord progress tracker keyed by account id, parent channel id, typing/thread target id, and source message id to avoid thread collisions.
- Tracks active run ids and derives the displayed count from current active set size.
- Replaces the displayed count reaction when the active count changes, removes it at zero, and caps counts above the configured emoji list to the final configured emoji.
- Uses `unref` on typing timers where supported so keepalive intervals do not keep Node alive.
- Updates Discord config schema, exported config types, UI hints, generated channel config metadata, and docs.

## Tests / Verification

Focused validation and static/config/docs gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `20a11bf331429ed2fd521636910b4aa07c5dcc24`
- Current PR head: `0f0ea76085d4ddc271aa25bab129f9c518f95992`
- Re-squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.
- Removed invalid/unnecessary delivered-text visibility experiment from `d17f593b4d4428f6ba7318f55eb40d76c3932094`; legitimate Discord sub-agent progress behavior remains.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live Discord proof for source-message progress behavior, not only tests. The requested coverage was: count reaction add/replace/remove behavior, normal channel context, thread/forum context, concurrent tracked sub-agents, typing keepalive while tracked work is active, typing stop/drain and TTL behavior, and durable failure-marker behavior after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle.

The live proof below covers those requested behaviors: normal channel success, thread-bound success, concurrent count replacement/increment/decrement/clear, typing keepalive/stop plus TTL guard logs, and a durable failure marker retained on the original source message after non-OK lifecycle. Private host/path/token/session/network values are redacted; Discord IDs/timestamps shown are included only where they are needed to tie the proof to the source-message behavior.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Live Discord API proof was run from the installed PR stack on Dev-01 using `OpenClaw 2026.6.10-beta.1` at local HEAD `f15c88bd6f9 stack: combine beta memory slots and Discord progress`, with:

- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.reactions.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.typing.enabled=true`

Observed live behavior in Discord:

- **Normal channel success:** a Discord-originated parent turn spawned a tracked sub-agent run (`8c6dbfa0-e021-4c3a-9992-328de22caa13`). The source Discord message showed the active count reaction while the child was running, typing stayed active during child work, and the count reaction was removed after the child completed. Child proof line: `NORMAL_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:48:33Z`.
- **Thread-bound success:** a thread-bound Discord sub-agent run (`01fa6443-4fc1-409d-9cf3-969ce433edbd`) completed successfully while progress was shown from the Discord parent context. Child proof line: `THREAD_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:49:50Z`.
- **Concurrent count replacement:** two overlapping tracked sub-agent runs (`4b2701ef-85b0-41d5-a87f-f72924e21869` and `9a5b1e70-5b3b-4820-bb5f-cb6cb7b2a926`) exercised count add/replace/remove behavior. The Discord source message count reaction incremented while both children were active, decremented as the first child completed, and cleared after the second child completed. Child proof lines: `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_2_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:23Z` and `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_3_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:36Z`.
- **Typing keepalive/stop:** Discord typing was visible while tracked sub-agents were active and stopped after tracked work drained. Earlier long-running proof passes also hit the configured typing safety TTL, with gateway logs showing `[typing] TTL exceeded (60000ms), auto-stopping typing indicator`, confirming the timeout guard executes.

Additional observation: after the final child drains, there can be a brief visual gap before the parent posts its final reconciliation response. That appears to be parent-yield lifecycle behavior rather than this PR's sub-agent progress tracker; it is being tracked separately as a follow-up investigation and is not treated as a blocker for this PR.

Additional durable failure-marker proof was captured from a real Discord source message after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle:

- **Failure marker:** source message `1518528276031602788` in Discord channel `1507934992699756645` retained the configured durable failure reaction `🔴` with count `1` and `me: true` after the non-OK sub-agent lifecycle. The source message timestamp was `2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z`. A later follow-up heartbeat at `2026-06-22T08:29:48.355Z` reported a separate verification pass, confirming the red marker was left on the original source message rather than being ordinary final text delivery.

Redacted observation:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "1507934992699756645",
  "message_id": "1518528276031602788",
  "timestampUtc": "2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z",
  "content": "Extensively check over the branch end-to-end against the recommended fix and prior investigation/research to ensure everything is clean, finalized, and polished.",
  "reactions": [
    {
      "emoji": { "name": "🔴" },
      "count": 1,
      "me": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Compatibility and Risk

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## PR/Commit Surface Breakdown

Source: 29 files, +846 / -81
Tests: 11 files, +1232 / -20
Total: 40 files, +2078 / -101

## Reviewer Checklist

- Confirm Discord progress remains opt-in and best-effort.
- Review source-message id propagation and tracker keying for channel/thread isolation.
- Confirm live Discord proof and focused tests cover add/replace/remove reactions, failure marker, typing, and config behavior.

---
Maintenance update: squashed to `381aa6f701d588adc4f18fd9dffcb84d6b41b953` after test-surface optimization only; behavior coverage and focused validation were preserved.

---

### Rebase/conflict resolution proof (2026-06-26)
- Rebased independently onto upstream `openclaw/openclaw` main `dd0e4f6e61b808fb77a5b85d2773e73c0dee2078`.
- Old head: `381aa6f701d588adc4f18fd9dffcb84d6b41b953`; new head: `265ab6294af01007c10d3c2406fc2494deec41be`.
- Resolved upstream/base conflict in `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` by preserving this PR's Discord subagent progress SDK surface changes and updating the current upstream public SDK budgets.
- Validation: `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`; `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check`; focused Vitest run covering Discord subagent hooks/config schema, agent spawn hooks/tooling, subagent registry completion/lifecycle/store/core tests, plugin boundary invariants, and delivery context tests.


---

### Clawsweeper remediation (2026-06-26)

Head: `7ad738b966ceb66efce0680ef8692210b01ae070`

- Remediated the valid clawsweeper finding in `extensions/discord/src/subagent-progress.ts`: failed count-reaction adds no longer advance `tracker.runningEmoji`, so later progress updates can retry/restabilize the visible Discord count reaction instead of believing the failed emoji is already present.

target.title: improve: speed timing-sensitive tests and fix LOC ratchet CI
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several timing-sensitive tests spend real wall-clock time waiting for debounce, hover, reconnect, and lifecycle windows. The waits add more than 13 seconds to focused Control UI feedback and about half a second to the managed-process test file. Separately, the new TypeScript LOC ratchet reports baseline drift already present in the PR base, causing unrelated PRs to fail `check-guards`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use Playwright's controlled page clock for six browser timing windows, keeping the tested delays intact without sleeping. End the parallel managed-child fixture explicitly once its listener invariant has been observed instead of waiting for natural process exit. Scope LOC violations to the already-detected changed-path set; baseline-file edits still trigger full-repository validation. Carry that set through a temporary JSON file so large changes cannot exceed the process argument limit. For pull requests, derive the LOC base from the checked-out synthetic merge commit's first parent, which remains exact when the event payload is stale and the checkout is shallow. Remove four newly exposed, unused UI type exports so the dependency guard remains green.

## User Impact

No runtime or user-visible behavior changes. Developers get materially faster test feedback with the same assertions and timing semantics, while CI assigns LOC debt to the change that introduces it.

## Evidence

- Same-box before/after profiling for the six optimized UI assertions: 25.38 s -> 12.25 s (51.7% faster).
- Same-box managed-child file profiling: 635.0 ms -> 114.7 ms (82% faster).
- Pre-rebase exact-head proof: managed-child file 9/9 passed in 145 ms (`run_f7e1f8582f6f`); six focused UI assertions 6/6 passed in 13.86 s (`run_f3fee8e10569`).
- Broad changed-surface gate passed (`run_49ead66732aa`).
- Post-rebase tooling proof: 174/174 tests passed on Testbox `tbx_01kxctqfm2ddeqqg347919wksc` ([run 29223304924](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29223304924)); managed-child finished in 89 ms.
- All six optimized UI assertions passed post-rebase. The run also exposed a current-main duplicate-name selector; the intended sidebar control plus the changed chat-flow timing case passed 2/2 after repair.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` matched all 5,512 baseline entries; `pnpm check:workflows` passed.
- Final 16-file `pnpm check:changed` gate passed, including formatting, four affected typecheck lanes, and lint (Testbox command 28.77 s).
- Fresh autoreview is clean after the CI hardening (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.87) and after the final selector/baseline cleanup (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.91).

target.title: fix(nodes): reject malformed camera content lengths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users saving URL-backed node camera, photo, or clip media could accept a malformed `Content-Length` response header and continue as though no size header was present.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node media URL download boundary now parses `Content-Length` with the shared strict media parser before reading the response body, and cancels rejected response bodies on malformed headers. This keeps the change inside the node-hosted media download path used by camera CLI commands and agent node media actions without changing valid downloads, config, provider behavior, schemas, or public APIs.

## User Impact

Malformed node-hosted media responses are rejected before the payload is copied to disk, while valid URL-backed camera media continues to use the existing size limits and stream guard.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` -> `writeUrlToFile` HTTPS download path still accepts missing and valid `Content-Length` headers, and rejects malformed media lengths before opening/copying the output file.
- Current-head runtime proof at `aef555613389229e08cafc57157a415df05f0783`: loopback HTTPS responder called by `writeUrlToFile` via `node --import tsx --input-type=module -`.

```text
HEAD=aef555613389229e08cafc57157a415df05f0783

valid-header: PASS bytes=11 payload=url-content

requests=/missing,/valid,/malformed
```

target.title: fix(fal): apply request policy to media generation requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring FAL provider request policy for media generation would not have that policy applied to FAL image generation HTTP requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

FAL HTTP config now passes `models.providers.fal.request` into the existing provider HTTP request-policy resolver. This keeps FAL on the shared provider request seam and does not change model parameters, generation parsing, or generated image parsing. Explicit private-network opt-in is now honored from the configured request policy instead of being overridden by a hard-coded deny, while the default remains deny.

## User Impact

FAL media generation requests can now honor configured request headers, proxy/TLS transport settings, and explicit private-network request policy through the existing provider request policy mechanism.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.test.ts` passed: 44 tests.

- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/fal/http-config.ts extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Resolver proof: `resolveFalHttpRequestConfig` with configured `baseUrl`, `request.headers.X-Fal-Trace`, and `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` returned `allowPrivateNetwork: true` plus the configured header and redacted Authorization header.

target.title: docs(coding-agent): require fresh project worktrees
target.body:
## Summary

- require the bundled coding-agent launcher to prepare and verify an isolated worktree from freshly fetched canonical upstream state before a delegated worker edits a Git-backed project
- preserve the fetched contributor head and avoid automatic history rewrites for trusted existing PR/shared-branch work
- treat contributor-controlled refs as untrusted: never launch a permission-bypassed worker directly in those checkouts; use the repository-approved untrusted-PR sandbox/review workflow or stop
- keep read-only tasks and non-project scratch scaffolds exempt
- limit the final scope to `skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md`; there are no `AGENTS.md`, workspace-template, system-prompt, runtime/protocol, or skill-availability changes

## Verification

- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- final `$autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` with Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` at high reasoning: clean, no accepted/actionable findings
- pre-push canonical ancestry: `upstream/main` `125ad94d6d4be543a96a8d92b44bcf7869d37b7a` is an ancestor of pushed head `c23f427ef515e1205e26da45dca6d2fda30f4e40`; the fork head was also an ancestor and the update was pushed without force

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Delegated coding workers must start in launcher-prepared isolated worktrees based on freshly fetched canonical state when modifying a Git-backed project.

Real environment tested: OpenClaw source checkout with live canonical `openclaw/openclaw` and fork remotes, including a concurrently updated existing PR branch.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Fetched `upstream`, verified canonical ancestry and fork-head ancestry, integrated both without rewriting history, then pushed the existing PR branch without force.

Evidence after fix: The live PR diff contains only `skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md` and the pushed branch contains both the fetched canonical base and the concurrent fork head.

Observed result after fix: New project work requires a launcher-prepared fresh-canonical worktree; existing trusted branches preserve their fetched head; untrusted contributor refs are blocked from permission-bypassed launch; scratch/read-only work remains exempt.

What was not tested: A live model turn invoking the bundled coding-agent skill.

target.title: improve(ui): friendlier panel load error state with reload prompt for stale chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users hitting a lazy panel load failure in the Control UI (most commonly the stale-chunk "Importing a module script failed" error after a gateway update) would see a giant red callout stretched across the entire panel area, with the raw browser error message as the most prominent text. The state read as a crash rather than a routine, recoverable condition.

## Why This Change Was Made

The router outlet rendered load failures as a bare `callout danger` with no layout styling, so the callout stretched to fill the routed pane. The raw exception text ("Importing a module script failed.") led the copy, and the common stale-chunk case (a background gateway update replacing hashed chunks) was presented identically to a genuine failure.

This change replaces it with a centered panel error state:

- Icon, human title, and short subtitle; the raw error is demoted to a small muted mono line.
- The stale-chunk case is presented as an update prompt ("A new version is available" with a Reload button, accent styling) instead of a red failure.
- Generic load failures keep a danger-styled alert icon with a Retry button.

Recovery behavior (revalidate vs. document-probe reload) is unchanged; only the presentation changed. The unused `lazyView.unknownError` key was dropped and copy trimmed so `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts` stays within the TypeScript LOC ratchet.

## User Impact

Anyone using the Control UI when a panel chunk fails to load — most visibly right after a gateway update. They now get a clear, calm explanation and an obvious Reload/Retry action instead of a full-pane red error box.

Stale-chunk prompt (after gateway update):

![stale chunk update prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/lazy-view-error/lazy-error-stale.png)

Generic load failure:

![generic load failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/lazy-view-error/lazy-error-generic.png)

## Evidence

- Screenshots above captured live against `pnpm dev:ui:mock` with route imports forced to reject (WebKit stale-chunk message and a generic HTTP 500 message).
- `ui/src/app/router-outlet.test.ts` updated: the stale-chunk test now asserts the update-prompt copy; existing assertions for the raw error text, retry-through-latest-context, and offline fallback behavior still pass.
- `pnpm check:changed` (coreTests + ui lanes) green on Blacksmith Testbox, including the TypeScript LOC ratchet.
- Codex autoreview run on the branch diff.

target.title: fix(ai): serialize ChatGPT websocket message decode order
target.body:
Closes #105435

## What Problem This Solves
`parseWebSocket` started an independent async decode task per `message` event. Blob-like frames await `arrayBuffer()` while strings decode immediately, so later frames could enter the parser queue first and reorder Responses stream events.

## Why This Change Was Made
Serialize decode-and-parse on a per-socket promise chain so arrival order is preserved without dropping the accepted binary/Blob path. Codex sibling `responses_websocket.rs` already consumes one WebSocket message at a time before reading the next; OpenClaw now matches that ordering invariant while keeping Blob compatibility.

## User Impact
ChatGPT Responses websocket streams no longer reorder events when a delayed Blob decode races a later text frame. Normal string-only traffic behavior is unchanged aside from the ordered chain.

## Evidence
- Codex contract checked: `../codex/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs:686-808` (sequential `ws_stream.next()`, binary rejected as unexpected).
- Local: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts` — 33 passed, including delayed Blob + string completion ordering regression.
- `git diff --check` clean on touched files.

target.title: improve(gateway): reduce startup work before readiness
target.body:
Closes #105912

AI-assisted: Codex implementation and review.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup performed restart-scoped managed-plugin cleanup and loaded the full worker-environment runtime before the server was ready, including on the common path with no configured or durable workers. This added avoidable cold-start module initialization, filesystem work, and duplicate durable-record scans before the first interactive turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained managed-plugin cleanup now runs as a cancellable post-ready idle task. It resolves the current installed-plugin index at execution time, preserving plugins installed or reloaded during the delay. The Gateway carries the initial worker record snapshot forward, loads the worker service/runtime bundle only when configured or durable records require it, and imports the protocol schema only when preparing an installation.

Worker-provider lookup and reload planning retain their live lifecycle semantics: provider resolution reads the current plugin registry, and reloads recompute durable providers from the current worker store. The startup benchmark also excludes counters and memory fields from its duration ranking.

Final exact-head CI also exposed dead-export drift in newer `main` merge state. The stack keeps the new SMS reset as an intentional test seam, makes an internal transcript target type file-local, and removes a stale baseline entry; runtime behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Gateway restarts perform less work before readiness, with the largest benefit on cold starts and installations carrying managed plugin history. Dormant worker-environment support no longer imposes its full module-loading cost on every boot. No configuration, protocol, data, or plugin SDK contract changes.

## Evidence

- Linux AWS Crabbox focused proof:
  - `run_3e07b71057d3`: 324 tests plus `tsgo:prod` passed after the live-registry fix.
  - `run_717dd41f456d`: 354 behavior tests passed; the only failures were two copies of an obsolete source assertion, updated to require current install-index resolution.
  - `run_1fa34cd26c39`: updated import-boundary tests 8/8 plus `tsgo:prod` passed.
- Fresh Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcw8h5tcq9wwr2rgp282k1g` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29224416442)): `tsgo:prod`, all test typechecks, and dead-export guard passed; the concurrent iMessage baseline repair passed its focused tests 14/14 and is now on `main` via #106022, outside this Gateway-only stack.
- Exact runtime build: Node 24 `cliStartup` production profile passed in 4.80 s. The full AWS build lane was blocked by a temporary `main` lockfile defect and missing hydrated build-only assets; the later `main` ratchet repair is included in the final rebase, and [hosted exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29225663179) passed at `147ba8f2e847`.
- Final five-run startup benchmark after one warmup:
  - default `/readyz` p50 4761 ms
  - skip-channels `/readyz` p50 4641 ms
  - 50 manifest plugins `/readyz` p50 5180 ms
- Same-box cold one-shot from the causal cleanup loop: 9756 ms before, 8721 ms after deferring retained-install cleanup (10.6% faster).
- Live OpenAI-on-Crabbox proof, `run_65f7344f794b`, model `openai/gpt-5.6`:
  - Gateway ready in 4803 ms.
  - Three long, tool-heavy turns completed successfully in 75.2 s, 99.0 s, and 83.2 s.
  - Repeated-turn startup stages fell from 370 ms to 15 ms and 13 ms.
  - Core/plugin tool setup fell from 215 ms to 17 ms and 14 ms; stream preparation fell from 286 ms to 63 ms and 53 ms.
- Fresh structured review found and drove fixes for live registry lookup, current install paths, and reload-time durable provider discovery. The final remaining suggestion referenced fields absent from the worker record contract and was rejected against current `main`, whose canonical implementation uses the same `listForReconcile().map(providerId)` rule.
- Exact dead-export guard passed with all 5,503 intentional entries matched.
- LOC ratchets decrease: `server.impl.ts` 2370 -> 2271, startup benchmark 1035 -> 1026, worker tunnel 558 -> 553.
- Import-boundary regressions verify managed retention, worker service/live/transcript/tunnel/provider-registry, and worker protocol modules remain off the eager server import path.
