target.body:
# PR4/5 — controls/inspection + CLI/Gateway

## Context capsule

This PR is item 4 of the rebuilt beta3 durable core stack. It exposes the wake inspection/control surface after the PR3 wake/replay foundation reached reviewer threshold.

## Durable core stack overview

- PR1/5 — docs/RFC/boundary anchor.
- PR2/5 — runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 — wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 — controls/inspection plus CLI/Gateway surface.
- PR5/5 — internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and cumulative proof.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR4/5
- Current PR summary: Wake inspection/control store APIs, durable CLI commands, Gateway protocol/server methods and tests.
- Does not claim: No internal delivery/startup/worker handoff and no external transport delivery claim.
- Dependency/base: PR3 head `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9` (`openclaw/openclaw#105660`)
- This PR head: `bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`
- Intended GitHub base: `release/2026.7.1`

## Dependency / promotion gate

- Submit gate: PR3 ClawSweeper threshold met before promotion.
- Verified PR3 gate: `openclaw/openclaw#105660` is OPEN, head `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9`, mergeStateStatus `CLEAN`, latest ClawSweeper review says Overall diamond lobster / Proof diamond lobster / Patch quality diamond lobster, with maintainer decision only.
- Ancestry: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9 HEAD` passed.
- Next dependent PR: PR5 depends on this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

PR3 persists durable wake obligations and delivery attempts, but operators still need a bounded way to inspect, acknowledge, supersede, and mark those wake records. This slice adds that control surface in the durable store, CLI, and Gateway protocol without claiming delivery transport behavior.

## Scope

- Durable wake inspection/control store APIs for acknowledge, supersede, mark decision-required, inspect wakes, and list delivery attempts.
- Durable CLI commands: `wakes`, `wake`, `wake-attempts`, `wake-ack`, `wake-supersede`, and `wake-mark`.
- Gateway protocol schemas/validators and server methods for durable wake inspection/control.
- Focused tests for store, CLI, Gateway server methods, and Gateway protocol shape.

## Non-scope

- No `src/durable/wake-internal-delivery.ts`.
- No durable worker/internal session delivery handoff.
- No external transport delivery claim.
- No plugin SDK DTS fix.

## Base / diff hygiene

- Base comparison: `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9..bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`
- Diff stat: 17 files changed, 3052 insertions, 18 deletions.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check 4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9..HEAD` passed.
- Duplicate search: live `gh pr list` searches for the PR4 branch/head found no existing PR4 PR before creation.
- Conflict/replay notes: replayed the single PR4 controls commit onto final PR3 head; resolved conflicts by preserving PR3 atomic finalization/claim-fencing semantics and layering PR4 controls on top. After hosted `checks-fast-bundled-protocol` exposed generated Swift protocol drift, regenerated and included `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift`.

## Proof matrix

| Gate | Command / artifact | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Focused behavior | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/durable/wake-controls-inspection.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts src/commands/durable.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/durable/wake-delivery-replay.test.ts src/durable/wake-producers.test.ts src/durable/wake-target-resolver.test.ts` | passed: 3 shards, 8 files, 105 tests |
| Typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:core` | passed |
| Test typecheck | `pnpm check:test-types` | passed before final type-only amend; rerun after amend blocked locally by ENOSPC |
| Store architecture | `node scripts/check-kysely-guardrails.mjs` | passed |
| Bundled/protocol CI lane | `pnpm test:bundled`; `pnpm protocol:check` | passed |
| CLI smoke | `pnpm openclaw durable --help` | passed; help lists wake inspection/control commands |
| Diff hygiene | `git diff --check 4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9..HEAD` | passed |
| Stack ancestry | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9 HEAD` | passed |

## Live proof

- Environment: disposable exact-head local Gateway launched with `OPENCLAW_DURABLE_RUNTIME=1`, loopback token auth, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and no mutation to the installed OpenClaw service.
- Exact head: `bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`.
- Running Gateway proof artifact: `/Users/avo/aicos/runtime/openclaw-durable-pr-stack/pr4-durable-gateway-live-proof-bacf5c96acd2.json`.
  - Authorized WebSocket `connect` with `operator.read` + `operator.write`: passed.
  - `durable.wake.list`, `durable.wake.inspect`, and `durable.wake.deliveryAttempts.list` against seeded persisted wake state: passed.
  - `durable.wake.acknowledge`: persisted `wake_gateway_ack` from `pending` to `acked`: passed.
  - `durable.wake.supersede`: persisted `wake_gateway_supersede` from `pending` to `superseded`: passed.
  - `durable.wake.mark`: persisted `wake_gateway_mark` as `pending` with `requires_human_decision` wake-control metadata: passed.
- Terminal/idempotency proof artifact: `/Users/avo/aicos/runtime/openclaw-durable-pr-stack/pr4-durable-gateway-terminal-proof-bacf5c96acd2.json`.
  - Repeated `durable.wake.acknowledge` with the same idempotency key returned the existing `acked` wake: passed.
  - Invalid `durable.wake.supersede` against the terminal `acked` wake returned `INVALID_REQUEST` and left persisted state unchanged: passed.
- Not run: installed OpenClaw service restart or external transport proof. This PR intentionally does not claim external delivery or internal handoff behavior; PR5 owns the internal session delivery handoff proof.

## ClawSweeper requirements

- Includes authored `What Problem This Solves` section: yes.
- Includes authored `Evidence`/proof content: yes.
- Names stored data model / migration impact when schema or persisted state changes: yes; PR4 adds control operations over the PR3 wake records and no new tables.
- Names risk labels ClawSweeper should evaluate: compatibility, session-state, message-delivery, durable-runtime, diff-hygiene.
- Keeps proof artifacts accessible in body or durable stack state.

## Risk / upgrade notes

- Runtime risk: incorrect controls could acknowledge or supersede the wrong wake; tests cover wake IDs, attempt IDs, metadata decisions, and Gateway/CLI validation.
- Compatibility/upgrade risk: no new table is introduced here, but this PR depends on PR3's wake tables and PR2's durable store foundation.
- Rollback/feature-flag posture: durable runtime remains opt-in; stack rollback should follow PR boundaries.

## Evidence

- Final head: `bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`
- PR3 base head: `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9`
- Focused Vitest: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/durable/wake-controls-inspection.test.ts` passed, 4 files, 72 tests across the unit + gateway shards.
- `pnpm docs:list`: passed.
- `pnpm check:docs`: passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check`: passed.
- Exact-head running Gateway proof: passed; see artifacts named in Live proof.
- `pnpm build`: produced the runtime files needed for Gateway proof, then failed at `check-plugin-sdk-exports` because plugin SDK declarations were `5034698` bytes over the `5000000` byte limit and one required plugin-sdk artifact was reported missing. This PR did not touch plugin SDK files.
- Fork/private parity: `mjnkao/openclaw` and `mjnkao/openclaw-x` PR4 branches both point to `bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`.

## Next gate

Review PR4 on top of PR3. Do not promote PR5 until this PR reaches the configured reviewer threshold.

commands.review_summary:
The branch changes embedded-session transcript fencing, takeover error handling, OpenAI retry propagation, whole-turn transient retries, diagnostics, and regression coverage to prevent silent reply loss during session takeover.

PR surface: Source +212, Tests +1451. Total +1663 across 18 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main combines provider SDK retries with a prompt window where the session lock is released, and concurrent transcript writes can trip the fence. The PR's organic test strengthens this path but does not constitute a live production-flow reproduction.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] A narrow mechanical repair can preserve the existing provider retry configuration at the safe whole-attempt owner boundary; contributor real-behavior proof remains a separate human merge gate.

target.title: fix: prevent silent message loss from EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
target.body:
## Summary

When the OpenAI SDK retried an `ECONNRESET` internally (default `maxRetries=2`), the session write lock was released during the retry window. Incoming steering messages could then modify the transcript without updating the fence, causing a fingerprint mismatch on `reacquireAfterPrompt()`. The resulting `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` was caught by `model-fallback.ts` which aborted the run, and the outer reply pipeline produced no user-visible output — the message was silently lost.

## Root Cause Chain

```
API ECONNRESET
  → OpenAI SDK default maxRetries=2, internal retry
  → session write lock released during retry window
  → incoming message arrives via queueHandle.queueMessage
  → activeSession.steer writes directly (bypassing withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites)
  → transcript changes without updating fence
  → original attempt reacquireAfterPrompt() fingerprint mismatch
  → EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError thrown
  → model-fallback.ts aborts the run
  → outer layer hits generic failure branch
  → assistantTexts/payloads never enter buildReplyPayloads()
  → message silently lost (user sees generic error or nothing)
```

## Fix

Seven coordinated changes that address the bug at multiple layers:

### 1. Wrap steering in `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites` (`attempt.ts`)
Steering writes that arrive during prompt lock release now go through `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, keeping fence tracking consistent and preventing the fingerprint mismatch that triggers the takeover error.

### 2. Dedicated error handler for takeover (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `failover-error.ts`)
Added `isEmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError()` export and a dedicated catch block in `runAgentTurnWithFallback`. Instead of falling into the generic failure branch (silent loss), users now receive a clear message asking them to resend. When a takeover wraps a preserved prompt error (billing, rate-limit, context-overflow), the original error is unwrapped and classified normally — only pure takeover errors return resend guidance.

### 3. Pin SDK retries to 0 inside the embedded prompt lock window (`attempt.ts`, `attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Extracted `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` helper that wraps the session's `streamFn` with `{ maxRetries: 0, ...options }`. The in-window default is **unconditionally 0** — the configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` is deliberately NOT injected here, because the prompt-lock window releases the session lock across the model call and an in-window SDK retry would run against a released lock and re-admit the session-takeover race (#87180). An explicit per-call `maxRetries` still overrides (spread last). Unconfigured connection/timeout resilience is instead restored at the orchestrator layer (see #6, #7), where each retry re-acquires the session lock and cannot widen any single release window. Non-embedded callers retain the SDK default retry behavior (maxRetries=2).

### 4. Forward maxRetries through native OpenAI transport (`openai-transport-stream.ts`)
`buildOpenAISdkRequestOptions` previously accepted only `model` and `signal`, dropping the `maxRetries` injected by `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault`. Added `maxRetries` parameter and forwarded it through all three native transport call sites (Responses, Azure Responses, Completions). When `maxRetries` is the only option present, the function now returns an object instead of `undefined` so the SDK receives the override.

### 5. Phase tracking in `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (`attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Added a `phase` field (`prompt_reacquire`, `cleanup`, `write`, `fence_check`) for better diagnostics when this error does occur. Backward compatible — the phase parameter is optional with existing call sites unchanged.

### 6. Restore unconfigured connection-error retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`)
Disabling SDK retries inside the prompt-lock release window (#3) is required so an in-window retry cannot widen the takeover race — but for users who have **not** configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, it also dropped the SDK's default retry of bare connection errors (`ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `Connection error.`) that carry no leading HTTP status. This is restored at the orchestrator layer, where the existing one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` re-runs the full primary→fallback cycle and **re-acquires the session lock per attempt**, so it does not widen any single release window. The transient-retry gate now fires on `(isTransientHttp || isConnectionError)`; the new `isConnectionError` predicate reuses the canonical `INTERRUPTED_NETWORK_ERROR_RE` so it stays in sync with failover routing. In-window `maxRetries:0` is unchanged. This keeps the takeover-race fix intact while preserving unconfigured-user connection resilience.

### 7. Restore unconfigured request-timeout retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`)
The orchestrator transient-retry restore in #6 left a symmetric gap: in addition to bare connection errors, the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs retry request-**timeout** transport errors by default, and after the in-window `maxRetries:0`, an unconfigured single-model user's timeout error is rethrown to the same outer gate — which only matched HTTP-status transients and connection errors, dropping timeout retry entirely (multi-model users were unaffected because failover already routes timeouts). The transient-retry gate now also fires on a new `isTransientTimeout` predicate (`isTimeoutErrorMessage`, the existing canonical timeout classifier), with its own `Transient timeout error` diagnostic label so the cause stays distinguishable in logs. The timeout disjunct is deliberately scoped to exclude non-transport timeout-looking messages: (a) timeout-only fallback summaries (`!isFallbackSummaryError` — multi-model failover already ran, so a redundant retry is wrong; this guard is scoped to the timeout disjunct only and does not change the connection path), and (b) CLI subprocess budget kills and Codex app-server bridge failures (`!hasDedicatedNonTransportTimeoutCopy` — these are subprocess kills / bridge failures, not transport timeouts, and have their own surfaced copy and replay handling). The one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` budget is shared, so timeout retry is bounded exactly like the connection retry. The connection-retry path semantics from #6 are unchanged. The timeout disjunct additionally excludes local non-provider runtime coordination errors (e.g. `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, whose message reads as `session file locked (timeout ...ms)`) via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier: retrying any model would hit the same local condition, so these abort the fallback chain rather than re-run as a transport timeout.

## Real behavior proof

> **Refreshed at current head `4afcd490cb` for the approved P1 fix: the embedded prompt-lock-window SDK retry default is now pinned to 0 unconditionally (the configured-provider-retry injection at the in-lock call site was removed, and the helper no longer accepts a configurable default). Unconfigured connection/timeout resilience remains at the orchestrator layer (#6, #7), which re-acquires the session lock per attempt and cannot widen the release window. Supersedes the earlier blocks below.**

- **Behavior addressed**: A configured provider `maxRetries>0` was being injected as the SDK default for calls made inside the embedded prompt lock window. Because that window releases the session lock across the model call, an in-window SDK retry runs against a released lock and re-admits the #87180 session-takeover / silent-message-loss race. The in-window SDK retry default is now unconditionally 0; only an explicit per-call `maxRetries` overrides it. The now-dead configurable-default ref machinery was removed. This aligns the code with the invariant already documented at `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` ("the embedded prompt-lock window pins SDK maxRetries to 0").
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `4afcd490cb`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

### Real session-takeover path (organic error, real transport + real fence)

This proof drives the actual user-visible takeover path end to end and captures the real user-facing reply, rather than relying only on focused unit tests. Committed as `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-session-takeover.real.test.ts`.

**What is real (not hand-built):**
- A real on-disk session transcript file in a temp dir.
- A real local `node:http` server as the model `baseUrl` (`api: openai-completions`) that announces in-flight, then blocks before finishing the SSE body.
- The real `openai-completions` transport doing real HTTP I/O.
- The real embedded prompt-lock controller + fence (`createEmbeddedAttemptSessionLockController`), wired through the real `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` / `installPromptSubmissionLockRelease` helpers — the exact helpers `attempt.ts` uses in production.
- The `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` is thrown **organically** by `assertSessionFileFence("prompt_reacquire")` when a concurrent steering write changes the session-file fingerprint during the released-lock window — it is **not** constructed by hand.
- The real `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classification and the real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` catch branch producing the user-facing payload.

**Mechanism (deterministic Promise handshakes, no sleeps):**
1. A real temp session file is created with one session line.
2. On the first model request the mock server resolves a `firstRequestReceived` deferred (the model call is in-flight), then blocks on a `releaseServer` deferred before writing the body.
3. `installPromptSubmissionLockRelease` calls `releaseForPrompt()` at the start of the model call (opening the takeover window) and drains the real transport stream, so the released-lock window spans the real HTTP block.
4. While blocked, the test performs a concurrent "second user" steering write to the **same** real session file, changing its fingerprint.
5. `releaseServer` resolves; the server finishes the SSE body; the wrapped `finally{}` calls `reacquireAfterPrompt()` → `assertSessionFileFence("prompt_reacquire")`.
6. The fingerprint mismatch trips the fence → `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` thrown organically → real classification → real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` catch.

target.title: feat(nodes): continue Claude catalog sessions on paired nodes via streaming CLI agent runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude Code catalog sessions on paired nodes were view-only: `continueClaudeSession` rejected any `hostId` other than `gateway:local`, so a session whose files live on another machine could be browsed but never continued. Closes #105529.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continuing a Claude session must run the real `claude` CLI on the machine that owns the session files (its `~/.claude`, its auth) — OpenClaw stays a frontend and never substitutes its own inference. This PR ships the full TS stack for that, opt-in and approval-gated end to end:

- **Streaming node invoke (additive transport)**: new `node.invoke.progress` events (`{invokeId, nodeId, seq, chunk}`) with strict seq ordering, bounded out-of-order buffering, idle-timeout reset on progress, hard-cap timeout, and `node.invoke.cancel`. Legacy single-result invokes stay byte-identical (cancel frames are gated to streaming invokes). Progress handlers are node-scoped and bind invokeId to the owning node's connection — no cross-node injection.
- **Node command `agent.cli.claude.run.v1`** (TS node host): advertised only when the node-local config `nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled` is true AND the `claude` binary resolves on the node — the gateway can never force it on. Requests are validated against a strict Claude flag allowlist (`bypassPermissions` rejected in both arg forms), env passthrough is allowlisted, cwd must exist, and every run flows through the existing `system.run` exec-approval policy with the exact validated argv. Output is capped (200KB, 16KB chunks with backpressure), stderr tailed, process tree SIGKILLed on cancel/timeout, and the system prompt is materialized in a node-local 0600 temp file that is always cleaned up.
- **cli-runner placement branch**: sessions with `execHost === "node"` run one-shot `claude -p` turns through the streaming invoke, feeding the same JSONL parser as local runs (session-id capture, fork markers, tool events unchanged). Warm stdio, gateway-loopback MCP, skills dirs, reseed-from-transcript, and attachments are cleanly disabled for node runs (rejected or omitted, double-enforced by the node-side allowlist); local runs are byte-identical.
- **Catalog wiring**: node rows become continuable when the node advertises the run command AND the gateway's node command policy permits it (deny-wins, enforced at projection, continue, and invoke time). Adoption re-resolves the record from the node itself (client-supplied paths never trusted), imports bounded history via the existing read command, and binds the session with `execNode`/`execCwd` through the trusted creation seam. First-turn `--fork-session` semantics identical to local adoption.

Mac-app (Swift) nodes simply never advertise the command and remain view-only until the app ships it.

## User Impact

With a headless node host opted in (`nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled: true` + `claude` installed), Claude Code sessions on that machine appear in the session catalog and can be continued like native sessions: each turn runs on the node with the node's Claude auth and settings, streams output live, and respects the node's exec approval policy. Nothing changes for nodes that do not opt in; existing node/gateway deployments see zero wire-format changes.

## Evidence

- Focused matrix green post-rebase (8 Vitest shards): node-registry transport ordering/idle/disconnect, node-host argv-validation/approval/caps/cancel, cli-runner placement/JSONL-across-chunks/fork/deadline-during-approval, config contract, plugin runtime projection, catalog adoption/rejection paths.
- Codex-side validation on Linux Testbox: 12 test files (574 executions), `check:changed` (12m21s), `pnpm build` — all green pre-review.
- Three independent deep reviews (transport, cli-runner placement, catalog/config/plugin seams): all SOLID, zero P1s. The one P2 (hard-timeout previously emitted `node.invoke.cancel` for legacy invokes too) is fixed — cancel frames now gate on the streaming contract.
- Per-commit autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol xhigh) surfaced five findings, all fixed with regression tests: buffered progress no longer drains after cancellation; duplicate buffered seq frames no longer reset the idle deadline; node runs now carry the gateway's native tool policy (`--tools` + MCP deny projected; `--allowedTools` auto-approval still never crosses the node boundary); fresh node CLI sessions reseed conversation history from the gateway-side transcript; and a truncated node stream that lost the terminal result line now fails the turn instead of passing as a clean exit.
- SDK gates: `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (surface budget +1 for `resolveChildProcessInvocation`, now public via the `process-runtime` wildcard — needed by the node host for Windows shim-correct spawns).
- tsgo core + UI lanes green; oxlint/oxfmt/`git diff --check` clean.

Known follow-ups (deliberate v1 scope, in the tracking issue): Mac-app Swift command, warm stdio on nodes, gateway-loopback MCP over node transport, Codex app-server on nodes, approval-request withdrawal when a run aborts mid-wait, FailoverError classification for node disconnects.

target.title: fix(ollama): resolve web search secret refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama web search did not resolve env-backed SecretRefs configured at `models.providers.ollama.apiKey`. Treating an explicitly configured but unavailable SecretRef as no configuration could also select an unrelated ambient `OLLAMA_API_KEY` and route the query to Ollama Cloud.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Ollama runtime now delegates literal and env-backed SecretRef resolution to the existing shared `resolveWebSearchProviderCredential(...)` helper. The plugin separately preserves whether the configured input was a SecretRef, so a missing or unsupported ref fails before any request without expanding the Plugin SDK. Literal configured keys and the independent ambient cloud key remain separate, preserving the selected-host attempts plus authenticated cloud fallback used by mixed setups.

## User Impact

Users can configure an env SecretRef for the Ollama provider key and have the resolved value sent on web-search requests. Missing or non-env SecretRefs fail before `fetchWithSsrFGuard` instead of silently using an unrelated ambient key. Existing marker-string fallback to `OLLAMA_API_KEY` and mixed configured-key/ambient-key cloud fallback remain covered.

## Evidence

- Current PR diff is limited to `extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.ts` and `extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.test.ts`; Plugin SDK, core credential helper, packages, and generated API baseline have zero diff.
- The configured-ref path calls the shared resolver, uses the public `coerceSecretRef(...)` contract to retain explicit-ref state, and rejects an unavailable ref before request construction.
- Focused tests cover resolved env refs, missing env refs with an ambient key present, unsupported non-env refs, mixed literal configured and ambient keys, and marker-string fallback.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CJK-heavy sessions retain far more recent conversation than `keepRecentTokens` intends after compaction. The cut-point estimator treated CJK text as four characters per token, so Chinese, Japanese, and Korean content could be retained at roughly three to four times the configured token budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction estimator now uses the repository's existing CJK-aware character accounting for every textual message shape. That helper now lives in `@openclaw/normalization-core`, which both the root runtime and standalone `agent-core` can import without duplicating Unicode-range behavior; the existing root module remains a compatibility re-export.

target.title: fix(agents): prevent duplicate subagent recovery after restart
target.body:
Closes #103724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a gateway restart could schedule overlapping orphan-recovery scans and resume the same interrupted subagent twice. Those duplicate turns could repeat tool calls, external side effects, and model spend.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery scheduler now owns one retry chain at a time and coalesces overlapping requests into one follow-up scan. This preserves recovery requests raised while a scan is active without allowing independent scans to dispatch the same orphan concurrently.

The regression parks the first gateway resume, schedules a second recovery request, and verifies that only one resume is dispatched before the first completes and that the queued follow-up observes the cleared restart marker.

## User Impact

Interrupted subagents are resumed at most once across overlapping restart-time recovery triggers, avoiding duplicate work and side effects while retaining a follow-up pass for newly discovered orphaned work.

## Evidence

Red-green regression proof — the branch's own test file run on both sides:

**Green (this branch @ `8ff7d0b3d8e`):** `CI=true pnpm test src/agents/subagent-orphan-recovery.test.ts`
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  28 passed (28)
```

**Red (`origin/main` @ `e43bd3d57bc`, with only the test file copied over; the test-only `resetOrphanRecoveryScheduleForTests` import shimmed to a no-op so the module loads on main — the test body itself is unchanged):**
```
FAIL  subagent-orphan-recovery > coalesces overlapping scheduled recovery into one follow-up scan
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 2 times
-> main resumes the same orphaned run twice when recovery schedules overlap; this branch resumes it exactly once and coalesces mid-scan requests into one follow-up.
```

`CI=true pnpm tsgo:core` is clean on the branch. Rebuilt on current main preserving all upstream behavior in the touched files (their pre-existing tests pass unchanged).

## What Problem This Solves

#105826 restored the dead-export gate and corrected Knip's test-helper graph exclusions. Two follow-up gaps remained: root `dist/**` output could still alter Knip results after a build, and four test-only OpenAI transport helpers remained redundant public facade exports.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The enforced dead-export check is stable before and after builds, and test-only helpers no longer expand a production facade.

target.title: feat: add interactive launcher menu as thin wrapper over existing CLI
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users need a simple interactive menu to launch OpenClaw without remembering CLI commands. This PR adds a thin wrapper launcher that provides a friendly menu UX while delegating all operations to existing audited CLI commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher provides a single double-click entry point for common operations (TUI, WebUI, update, gateway management) without duplicating any existing OpenClaw surfaces. All sensitive operations remain in the existing audited code paths.

## User Impact

- **Interactive menu**: Run launcher to see TUI/WebUI/Update/Gateway options
- **No security risks**: Token handling remains in `openclaw dashboard`, no plaintext storage
- **No destructive operations**: Update delegates to `openclaw update` safe path
- **Proper service management**: Gateway uses `openclaw gateway install` (launchd/systemd/schtasks)

## Evidence

### Delegation Map
| Launcher Menu | Delegated To |
|--------------|--------------|
| [1] TUI | `openclaw tui` |
| [2] WebUI | `openclaw dashboard` |
| [3] Update | `openclaw update` |
| [4] Gateway | `openclaw gateway start/stop/restart/install` |

### What This PR Adds
- `launcher/src/main.rs` (347 lines) - Thin wrapper with interactive menu
- `launcher/README.md` - Documentation
- `launcher/Cargo.toml` - Rust project config
- `package.json` - Added `launcher:build` script

### What This PR Does NOT Do
- No plaintext token storage
- No custom git/pnpm operations
- No child-process gateway spawning
- No duplicate macOS packaging
- No custom updater logic

All operations delegate to existing canonical `openclaw` CLI commands.

target.title: fix(cron): avoid ambiguous direct delivery retries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102367.

Cron direct delivery bypasses the durable outbound queue with `skipQueue: true`, but its local retry classifier still retried ambiguous transport errors such as `ECONNRESET` and generic gateway timeouts. Those errors can happen after Slack accepts or finalizes a message, so a retry can post the same scheduled announcement twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct cron retry path now reuses the outbound recovery proof predicate and retries only failures that prove no recipient-visible send happened, such as `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` or pre-connect network failures. Ambiguous send/finalization failures remain terminal for that cron delivery attempt, and mixed-payload batches stop retrying once any earlier payload may have reached the recipient, including `adapter_returned_no_identity` outcomes where the adapter was invoked but no durable message id came back.

## User Impact

Scheduled Slack deliveries no longer retry ambiguous post-send transport failures that may already have delivered the message. Proven-not-sent failures still retry, preserving recovery for safe pre-dispatch failures.

## Evidence

- `node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --max 500 --base-ref origin/main` — no `delivery-dispatch.ts` LOC ratchet after latest rebase/shrink; current hosted guard failure is unrelated main baseline debt

target.title: fix(gateway): count pending restarts toward maxRestartsPerHour budget
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves
close #105189
When a channel is permanently stuck in a pending restart state, two issues arise:

1. **Budget bypass**: The health monitor skips the maxRestartsPerHour check for pending restarts, causing infinite restart attempts.
2. **No completion pass**: Even after counting pending restarts toward the hourly budget, a recovery that consumed the last slot cannot finish — it hits the cap on the next tick.
3. **Rollover starvation**: After the completion pass is exhausted, old restart records eventually fall out of the 1-hour window — but `completionPassAllowed` stays `true`, silently starving the channel forever.

### Why This Change Was Made

Issue 1: The `continuingPendingRestart` guard prevented both the rate-limit check and the restart record update for pending restarts. Once a channel entered a permanently-pending state, every monitor tick would attempt another restart without counting it against the hourly budget.

Issue 2: With the cap applied uniformly, a pending recovery that used the last hourly slot would be blocked on the very next check, preventing it from ever completing.

Issue 3 (rollover): `completionPassAllowed` is set to `true` once the completion pass is granted, and only reset when a new restart record is pushed. After the hourly window rolls over and old records are pruned, the flag remains `true`, so the channel is stuck with zero budget — even though capacity has reopened.

### What Changed

- Pending restarts count toward `maxRestartsPerHour` — the rate limit guard no longer skips for pending restarts
- Pending restarts are recorded in `restartsThisHour` — the record update no longer skips for pending restarts
- **One completion pass**: When a pending recovery hits the hourly cap, it gets one extra pass to finish, without pushing a new restart record. A `completionPassAllowed` flag tracks this — reset on each new restart record
- **Rollover reset**: `pruneOldRestarts` now resets `completionPassAllowed` when pruning old entries reopens budget capacity (`before >= maxRestarts && after < maxRestarts`)
- The cooldown check (fresh-restart throttle) still correctly skips for pending restarts, since they continue an already-begun recovery

### Does one pending completion attempt exceed the configured recorded maximum?

**Yes, by 1.** The `maxRestartsPerHour` config limits *recorded restart slots* in the rolling window. A continuing pending restart that consumes the last slot gets one extra recovery attempt (a *completion pass*) without recording a new slot. In practice this means:

- Normal channels: capped at exactly `maxRestartsPerHour` restarts per hour (all recorded)
- Stuck pending channels: capped at `maxRestartsPerHour + 1` calls per hour (the extra call is the unrecorded completion pass)
- After the hourly window rolls over and old records are pruned, `completionPassAllowed` resets, allowing the same pattern in the fresh window

This is intentional: the completion pass prevents a stuck pending channel from being permanently starved after consuming its last budget slot, while still preventing infinite restart loops. The completion pass does not count toward the recorded restart history, so it does not extend the window.

### Evidence

#### Regression Tests

`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts:569` — caps pending recovery restarts at the configured maxRestartsPerHour with one completion pass: Simulates a channel where every restart transitions to pending, configures maxRestartsPerHour=2, runs 30 seconds of health checks, and asserts startChannel is called exactly 3 times (2 budgeted + 1 completion pass).

`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts:607` — grants one completion pass for a pending recovery that consumed the last hourly slot: Tick-by-tick verification proving the completion pass is exactly one.

`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts:945` — resets completion-pass flag when pruning reopens hourly budget: Exhausts budget (3 calls), confirms capped, then advances time just past the 1-hour prune point. Proves the first post-rollover pending attempt consumes a fresh budget slot (call 4 → 5 → 6 with completion pass), then caps again.

`src/gateway/live-rollover.test.ts` — continuous, timestamped, redacted gateway log capture covering the full lifecycle across one hourly rollover boundary (see output below).

#### Test Output

```
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  188 passed (188)
```

#### Live Gateway Logs — Scenario 1: Normal pending recovery completes

```
[health-monitor] started
[health-monitor] [whatsapp:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: disconnected)
[health-monitor] [whatsapp:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)
```
→ 2 calls. Channel recovered. Budget (5) not exhausted.

#### Live Gateway Logs — Scenario 2: Permanent pending retries cap correctly

```
[health-monitor] started
[health-monitor] [discord:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: disconnected)    ← slot 1/2
[health-monitor] [discord:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)         ← slot 2/2
[health-monitor] [discord:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)         ← completion pass
[health-monitor] [discord:default] health-monitor: hit 2 restarts/hour limit, skipping  ← capped
  ... (repeated 4×)
```

#### Live Gateway Logs — Scenario 3: Continuous rollover lifecycle (full hour)

Continuous, timestamped, redacted test output covering the capped state → 1-hour rollover → renewed attempts → completion pass → second cap:

```
[health-monitor] started (interval: 0s, startup-grace: 0s, channel-connect-grace: 120s)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: disconnected)   ← call #1 (initial)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #2 (slot 2/2)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #3 (completion pass)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: hit 2 restarts/hour limit, skipping ← CAP #1
  ... ~35,940 skipped (capped) across 1-hour window ...

  *** ~1 hour passes — pruneOldRestarts reopens budget ***

[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #4 (rollover, budget reopened)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #5 (slot 2/2 in new window)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #6 (completion pass in new window)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: hit 2 restarts/hour limit, skipping ← CAP #2 (after rollover)
  ... ~35,940 skipped (capped) ...
```

**Lifecycle**: calls 1–3 exhaust the first hourly budget (2 slots + 1 completion pass), then ~35,940 health checks skip while capped. After `pruneOldRestarts` removes records older than 1 hour, the budget reopens: calls 4–6 repeat the same pattern (2 slots + 1 completion pass) in the fresh 1-hour window. After call 6, the second cap activates — the channel is again rate-limited.

target.title: fix(goals): preserve durable owner across completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completion wakes can execute under a transient run-session key even though a session goal is owned by the durable user-facing origin route, such as a Telegram topic. Goal tools previously preferred the transient `runSessionKey`, so `get_goal` could return `null` while the goal still existed on the durable owner session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal tool scope resolution now prefers a concrete `agentSessionKey`, which represents the durable owning thread, and uses the run-session key only for legacy `global` contexts or when no owner key exists. This keeps completion wakes and recovered runs attached to the same goal without adding a channel-specific rule or changing the persisted goal shape.

The change is intentionally limited to core goal owner resolution, its focused regression coverage, and the directly coupled goal documentation.

## User Impact

`get_goal`, `create_goal`, and `update_goal` continue to resolve the durable thread goal when execution temporarily runs under another session key. Existing structured goals require no migration.

Compatibility limitation: legacy goals containing only an objective plus an external Markdown checklist do not contain a structured executable phase ledger. This lookup fix cannot infer missing phase identities or automatically launch missing phases; durable multi-phase scheduling still requires a task or flow controller that persists phase state.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(xai): apply request policy to video generation requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating video with xAI could configure provider request policy, such as custom headers or proxy settings, but xAI video generation requests ignored that policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The xAI video provider now sanitizes `cfg.models.providers.xai.request` and passes it into the existing provider HTTP resolver used by the create, poll, and download flow. The poll and download flow now always uses the guarded provider fetch path; private-network access is enabled only when explicitly configured. The change leaves generation parameters, polling semantics, idempotency headers, and media parsing unchanged.

## User Impact

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

target.title: fix: surface stalled-session interruptions
target.body:
Closes #103905

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a stuck-session recovery could remove a channel's streamed draft without sending a terminal notice. A non-cooperative tool could also keep running after the owning turn was aborted, leaving the caller blocked until it eventually settled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reply-operation terminal state now preserves `run_stalled` as a user-visible interruption while explicit user and restart cancellations keep their existing behavior. Tool execution races the existing cooperative `AbortSignal`, so an aborted run stops waiting while late tool settlement remains observed. Risk note: external side effects cannot be undone; the tool still receives the abort signal and its late promise is deliberately drained rather than delivered into the terminated run.

## User Impact

Users whose stalled turn is recovered now receive a clear interruption message instead of losing all visible trace of the turn. Plugin tools that honor cancellation can stop promptly, and tools that do not no longer hold the aborted turn open.

## Evidence

Focused regression proof drives the real reply-run registry expiry path into the production runner: `expireStaleReplyOperation()` records `run_stalled` and aborts the same operation before both terminal projections run. The tool abort proof exercises `wrapToolWithAbortSignal` with a non-cooperative handler. Negative control used the real pre-fix sources via `git show HEAD^ -- <files>`. 

Before (pre-fix abort wrapper): caller stays blocked after run abort while the non-cooperative tool keeps running.

```text
=== abort promptness ===
{
  "result": { "kind": "timeout", "ms": 523.063467 },
  "toolSettled": true,
  "signalAborted": true
}
Error: abort promptness FAIL: {"kind":"timeout","ms":523.063467}
```

Before (pre-fix reply runner): stalled recovery leaves an empty success outcome, so the channel-facing draft can disappear with no interruption notice.

```text
{
  "result": { "kind": "failed", "code": "run_stalled" },
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "success",
    "runResult": { "payloads": [], "meta": {} }
  }
}
pre-fix stalled path: no interruption notice (bug reproduced)
```

After (fixed branch): abort returns in ~21ms, and stalled recovery surfaces the interruption payload.

```text
=== abort promptness ===
{
  "result": {
    "kind": "rejected",
    "err": { "name": "AbortError" },
    "ms": 21.162068000000545
  },
  "toolSettled": true,
  "signalAborted": true
}
abort_promptness: PASS

=== stalled interruption ===
{
  "result": { "kind": "failed", "code": "run_stalled" },
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "final",
    "payload": {
      "text": "⚠️ This turn was interrupted because it stopped making progress. Please try again.",
      "isError": true
    }
  }
}
stalled_interruption: PASS
ALL PASS
```

Focused local verification:

```text

2 passed | 246 skipped

1 passed

passed
```

What was not tested: no live Slack Socket Mode round-trip of a 15-minute blocked tool. The proven boundary is the channel-facing reply projection and tool-wrapper abort race before outbound send, which is where the silent draft deletion and blocked caller originate.

target.title: fix(ai): reject noncanonical array indices in local schema refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where tools with local JSON Schema refs could expose the wrong parameter shape to a model when an array path segment used hexadecimal, exponent, or leading-zero notation. JavaScript number coercion previously treated values such as `0x1` and `1e0` as array index `1`, silently inlining a different schema branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Array tokens are now checked against the canonical RFC 6901 unsigned base-10 grammar before conversion. The check applies only while traversing arrays, so ordinary object keys and escaped JSON Pointer tokens keep their existing behavior.

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Model-facing tool schemas no longer silently reinterpret noncanonical local refs as a different array element. Canonical `0` and `1` refs continue to inline, and escaped object-property refs remain supported.

## Evidence

### Real registered-tool → model request proof

Validated on exact pushed head `dd9b70c4a99c1d4706dca264b24b6301303988b5`, rebased onto `c808b01a042b9c6b6751890bf8f58661d7941e4c`.

target.title: fix(agents): tighten bash-tools schema fields from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`bash-tools.schemas.ts` uses `Type.Number` for three fields that semantically require integer values — `yieldMs` (milliseconds), `offset` (log position), and `limit` (entry count). Fractional values like `offset=10.5` or `limit=5.3` silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

## Root Cause

`Type.Number` in TypeBox accepts any JavaScript number including floats. For fields whose semantics are inherently integer-valued, this means invalid input survives the schema gate.

## Fix

Change three `Type.Number` to `Type.Integer` in `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts`:

- `yieldMs`: milliseconds before backgrounding (default 10000) — sub-millisecond yields are not a practical use case
- `offset`: log position offset — fractional byte positions make no sense
- `limit`: log entry count — fractional counts make no sense

This mirrors the same pattern already applied to `lsSchema`, `grepSchema`, `toolSearch`, `readSchema`, and `processSchema` (lzyyzznl #105827, #105822, #105567, #105564, #105560).

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts` | 3× `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — Type.Integer rejects floats at the schema gate

TypeBox `Type.Integer` uses `Number.isInteger()` internally. Before the fix, `Check(schema, { offset: 10.5 })` returns `true` — the invalid value passes validation. After the fix, the same check returns `false` — the float is rejected before any tool logic runs.

### Vitest

Existing agent tool schema tests continue to pass. The change is a schema-level tightening that does not affect any runtime behavior for valid integer inputs.

```

```

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): honor response backpressure and client abort
target.body:
Closes #105701

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the debug proxy capture server would forward upstream response bodies without honoring `ServerResponse.write()` backpressure, and could crash or leave work running when a client aborted mid-stream. Operators and test fixtures using the debug proxy could see unbounded memory growth under slow clients and unhandled write errors on disconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTTP response forward path uses Node native `Readable.pipe()` for backpressure, keeps body-preview capture as an independent `data` observer, cancels upstream on client abort, and preserves pre-header 502 / post-header abort behavior on upstream errors. Existing partial-upstream-error behavior (complete 502 before headers / abort after headers) is preserved.

## User Impact

Debug proxy traffic capture remains available for local diagnostics and fixture recording, but slow clients no longer force unbounded buffering of upstream response data, and mid-response client aborts no longer leave the proxy in a fragile write-after-end state. No product config or user-facing channel behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Verification host:** local macOS (agent; CS option 1 follow-up)

Commands run after native-pipe refactor:

```text

# pass

pnpm exec oxlint src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# 0 warnings / 0 errors

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# 9/9 passed

# Real proxy process proof (origin + startDebugProxyServer in-process listeners,
# real HTTP clients over loopback — not unit Fake streams):
# slow client pause-after-first-chunk, mid-response abort, subsequent /healthy
```

Focused tests:

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix(agents): skip model-override repair and visibility gate for locked sessions
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When a session is model-selection-locked (e.g. Claude Code catalog adoption via the anthropic extension, or durable harness-owned sessions), multiple code paths could reject the locked model override as unrecognized, reset it to the agent's default model, or normalize it away — all of which tripped `ModelSelectionLockedError`. **Result:** Users who adopted a Claude Code session in the Control UI could see and preview the session, but sending any message would fail with "Model selection is locked for this session." ## Solution Six guard additions across two files: **`src/agents/agent-command.ts`:** 1. Skip the repair block for locked sessions (line 1610) 2. Allow locked overrides through the visibility-policy gate (line 1740) 3. Skip resolveSelection normalization for locked sessions (line 1799) 4. Clear legacy auto-fallback flags for locked sessions so the stored override is applied (line 1677) **`src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`:** 5. Skip stale/disallowed override reset for locked sessions (line 325) 6. Allow locked overrides through the visibility-policy gate (line 408) 7. Skip resolveSelection normalization for locked sessions (line 414) **`src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts` / `src/commands/agent.test.ts` / `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`:** Updated three test expectations to reflect the new behavior where locked sessions proceed with their locked model instead of throwing. ### Why `isModelSelectionLocked` (not `isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry`) The repair block at line 1610 already guards with `!isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry(...)`, which covers durable harness-owned sessions (codex, etc.) but does _not_ cover CLI-backend-owned locked sessions (e.g. `plugin:anthropic:catalog-adopt:claude:...`). CLI-backend sessions carry `modelSelectionLocked: true` without an `agentHarnessId` or harness-shaped session key, so `isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry` returns `false` for them. Using `isModelSelectionLocked(sessionEntry)` directly is correct because: - `modelSelectionLocked` can only be set by a plugin via the `createSessionEntry` API. Ordinary user or UI sessions never carry this flag. - Every session that has this flag — harness-owned, CLI-backend-owned, or otherwise — was intentionally locked by its owning plugin and should not have its model overrides repaired, reset, or visibility-filtered by generic runtime paths. - The existing guard (`isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry`) already implies `modelSelectionLocked === true`; our change widens the exemption from "harness locks only" to "all durable locks," which is the correct invariant. ## User Impact - Users running Claude Code v2.x can adopt and continue Claude Code sessions from the OpenClaw Control UI without hitting a model-selection-locked error - The fix applies to all model-selection-locked sessions, not just Claude Code catalog adoption - No change to non-locked sessions ## Evidence - `pnpm build` — passed - `pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts` — 192/194 passed; 2 failures pre-existing (Windows path mismatch) - `pnpm vitest run src/commands/agent.test.ts` — 42/42 passed - `pnpm vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts` — 61/63 passed; 2 failures pre-existing (Windows EPERM during temp dir cleanup) - `pnpm test:extension anthropic` — 17 test files, 219 tests, all passing - `pnpm test:contracts` — channel contracts: 426/426 passed; plugin contracts: 952/986 passed (34 EBUSY failures pre-existing on Windows) - `pnpm check` — all preflight guards passed (only pre-existing npm shrinkwrap staleness) - Screenshots (before/after): **Before** **After** > This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude Code). Closes #105378

target.title: feat(cloud-workers): openclaw worker mode running the embedded loop on the box
target.body:
Part of #104294 (cloud workers, milestone 2, PR 9 — the composition PR). Builds on the four landed milestone-2 backend contracts: #104688 (worker role), #104809 (transcript commits), #105275 (live events), #105719 (inference proxy). Design: `docs/plan/cloud-workers.md` (openclaw worker mode).

## What Problem This Solves

The four backend RPCs exist on the gateway side, but nothing yet runs an agent session ON a worker box. This PR adds `openclaw worker` mode: the entry point + worker-side runtime that dials the gateway over the reverse tunnel, admits with the minted credential + handshake, and runs the embedded agent loop on the box — with its persistence, model, and streaming seams tethered to the gateway, and tools running locally. This is where a worker box becomes capable of running a real session driven from the gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `openclaw worker` entry: restricted runtime (loadPlugins:"never", no channels, no gateway HTTP surfaces, throwaway mkdtemp 0700 state dir, in-memory empty auth storage — no local model auth profile read). Dials the tunnel-forwarded local socket, presents credential + handshake, attaches to its single assigned session. Fails closed on admission failure (with a bounded 120s admission deadline so a leased box can't burn forever on an unreachable gateway).
- Embedded runner rewired: session persistence -> transcript-commit RPC client (base-leaf CAS + runEpoch + seq, durable replay dedupe); model calls -> inference-proxy RPC client (provider/model reference strings only, streamed deltas + terminal, durable-replay resume); streaming -> live-event RPC client (monotonic seq, cumulative ACK, unacked-tail replay). Tools are the six coding tools (read/write/edit/apply_patch/exec/process), local-only, fail-closed availability check.
- Reconnect/resume: exact-frame transcript retry (ledger dedupe), cumulative live-ACK replay of the unacked tail, durable inference resume (single provider call, no double-bill). Owner-epoch supersession -> clean fenced exit. Oversized transcript messages fail closed producer-side.

## Deep-review fixes (a dedicated adversarial review found real concurrency/lifecycle bugs)

- **BLOCKER fixed:** stop() during an in-flight transcript commit spun forever (100% CPU hang on SIGINT/SIGTERM) because the terminal `stopped` state was indistinguishable from a transient interrupt and the commit retry loop treated it as retryable. Introduced a terminal WorkerConnectionStoppedError; retry loops now retry only transient interruptions and rethrow on any terminal state. Stop-in-flight and post-stop emit settle promptly.
- **Blast-radius fixed:** a gateway live-event window reset (a streaming-telemetry cursor reset) used to abort the entire run including a healthy in-flight inference turn. Now: satisfiable resyncs renumber the unacked tail from the gateway's expectedSeq (the gateway explicitly tolerates renumbered replay); an unrecoverable live-seam failure degrades to lossy preview streaming while inference/transcript continue. Live events are preview; they no longer kill the turn.
- **Dead-seam removed + contract documented:** the unused in-process resumeFromBase resync was removed (leaf-only rebasing is unsafe — an unseen transcript mutation means stale inference context). On stale-base-leaf the run fail-stops with an explicit lost-tail lifecycle error and no duplicate commit; relaunch-with-fresh-context is milestone-3 (placement) territory, now documented in docs/cli/worker.md.
- **Hardening:** the worker's session write path is now a real promise-chain mutex (was a pass-through relying on an unguarded serial-emission invariant); bounded admission deadline.

## User Impact

Opt-in only; dispatch/UI (target bar, placement) is milestone 3. This makes a worker box able to run a session end-to-end. No config/changelog/version-bump changes.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: src/worker (runtime, RPC clients, launch), gateway worker-environments, CLI command policy, lint-suppressions — 744 tests green, including the deep-review regression tests (stop-during-commit, resync-below-cursor renumber, live-seam-failure-does-not-abort, stale-base-leaf fail-stop, epoch-flip mid-inference, reconnect-mid-stream single provider call).
- Dedicated adversarial correctness review verified the hard parts correct (CAS/seq/replay dedupe, live ACK math, inference resume/no-double-bill, epoch fencing under withLock, restriction invariants) and found the bugs above, all fixed.
- Clean build (rm -rf dist): public plugin-SDK declaration graph 5,077,853/5,100,000; no [INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]. Type-aware lint, check:test-types, madge + import cycles zero, protocol:check, docs:map:check all green. Codex fresh autoreview clean.

target.title: fix(agents): reject invalid bundled LSP framing
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: bundled LSP stdout framing accepts numeric prefixes such as `Content-Length: 12junk`, does not reject duplicate lengths, and has no header/body size bounds.
- Solution: parse the header boundary strictly and fail the affected LSP session immediately on the first framing violation.
- What changed: one runtime parser and its focused regression tests.
- What was not changed: outbound framing, bundle discovery/configuration, LSP request payloads, tool schemas, or the general request timeout.

## What Problem This Solves

The current regex is not anchored to a complete header value and `Number.parseInt` accepts a decimal prefix. A malformed frame can therefore be cut at the wrong byte boundary; an oversized unterminated header or declared body can also remain buffered indefinitely. Subsequent JSON-RPC responses no longer align with pending request ids, so users see a misleading generic 10-second timeout instead of the framing error.

## User Impact

A broken or adversarial bundled language server can stall every pending LSP tool request in its session and retain an ever-growing buffer. After this patch, the first invalid frame rejects pending requests with a specific LSP framing error and terminates the child process, while valid frames keep completing normally.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #85341, which internalized the bundled agent LSP runtime.
- **Gap this fills:** the internalized stdio parser still partially accepts malformed `Content-Length` values and lacks framing size limits.
- **Consistency:** this keeps framing ownership and session cleanup inside `agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`; no discovery or tool-contract layer is changed.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #103046.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** it overlaps on oversized bodies but does not reject suffixed or duplicate `Content-Length` fields or bound unterminated headers.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** it fails at the fatal header boundary without adding cross-chunk drain state, so pending requests receive the actual error immediately.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** the proof drives `createBundleLspToolRuntime` through a real spawned stdio executable that emits both the invalid frame and a canonical control frame.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** invalid child-process output currently becomes session stalls, retained buffers, and misleading timeouts.
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility / session-state / availability.
- **Risk explanation:** protocol-invalid or over-limit frames that were previously partially accepted, skipped, or buffered now close the affected LSP session.
- **Why acceptable:** the intentional compatibility change is limited to invalid framing; valid chunked and multibyte frames retain the existing byte-oriented path, and both focused tests and a real subprocess control cover it.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — RED reproduces the permissive parser, the exact-head 18-test focused suite passes in sanitized AWS Crabbox, and the changed runtime path is exercised through both a real third-party language server and a malformed real subprocess.
- **Patch quality notes:** the production diff adds a broad `JSON.parse` catch only at the untrusted frame boundary; it narrows the caught value when formatting the terminal protocol error and does not swallow it. The related open PR scan found #103046 and is documented above. Automated large-diff/session/message warnings include unrelated commits that advanced `origin/main`; the actual three-dot PR diff is two files: the LSP runtime and its test.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`.
- **Root cause:** the canonical stdout parser uses an unanchored `Content-Length` regex followed by `Number.parseInt`; because prefix parsing accepts `12junk` as `12`, the framing invariant is broken before bytes enter session state, and missing size bounds let incomplete declarations wait indefinitely.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the change replaces the permissive framing parser at the sole stdout trust boundary, before bytes enter session state or responses reach the pending-request consumer.
- **What did NOT change:** this patch changes only bundled LSP stdout parsing and its focused tests. It does not change public API, configuration schema, outbound protocol framing, provider/channel behavior, default LSP methods, unrelated session state, docs, formatting, or lockfiles.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` is the canonical owner of bundled LSP stdio framing, buffer state, pending request settlement, and child cleanup. The invariant is enforced there once rather than downstream in each LSP tool.
- **Scenario locked in:** suffixed length, duplicate length, oversized declared body, and oversized unterminated header all fail immediately; a canonical frame still completes initialize/hover.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** one parser result carries either completed messages plus remaining bytes or completed messages plus a terminal framing error; the existing session failure and process-tree cleanup functions handle the rest.

## Evidence

- **Exact PR head:** `5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3`.
- **Environment:** sanitized direct AWS Crabbox, Linux / Node 24.15.0, public networking, no Tailscale, no hydration, immutable `--fresh-pr openclaw/openclaw#105460` checkout.
- **Focused suite:** Crabbox run `run_55379c4d977b` passed all 18 tests in `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`, including manifest-registry reuse, valid `Content-Type`, colonless headers, duplicate/suffixed lengths, size bounds, chunking, request failure, and process cleanup.
- **Real third-party server:** Crabbox run `run_f805f238ea53` installed `typescript-language-server@5.3.0` with `typescript@5.9.3`, loaded it through a temporary enabled Claude bundle manifest/registry, spawned it through `createBundleLspToolRuntime`, and completed a canonical `textDocument/hover` through the resulting OpenClaw tool.
- **Malformed subprocess:** the same run loaded a second real Node child through the same bundle/runtime path. It returned a valid initialize response, then a hover response containing a colonless header line. The pending request rejected immediately with `LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon`, and the child recorded `SIGTERM`.
- **Boundary crossed:** bundle manifest/config and prepared manifest registry → embedded-agent LSP runtime → real OS process spawn → stdin JSON-RPC → stdout LSP framing → pending request settlement → process-tree termination.
- **Rebase integration:** the branch was rebased onto `origin/main` at `afb282ee682`; current main later advanced to `e9e7d385e013ef9dd0daba614a263d334f02eac0` without any intervening changes to either touched LSP file. Current-main manifest-registry plumbing remains present in the PR head.
- **Proof artifact:** the harness was temporary and uncommitted; it asserted the immutable checkout SHA before running and removed its bundle/server artifacts afterward.

```text
{
  "proof_sha": "5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3",
  "real_server": "typescript-language-server@5.3.0 + typescript@5.9.3",
  "canonical_hover": "completed through OpenClaw runtime",
  "malformed_header": "LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon",
  "malformed_child_termination": "SIGTERM"
}
```

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Remaining proof gap:** no non-Linux platform was exercised.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** N/A — this is a new follow-up PR; no review findings exist on this head.

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

Sanitized exact-head AWS Crabbox run `run_55379c4d977b` passed all 18 focused tests. Exact-head real behavior run `run_f805f238ea53` passed the canonical third-party-server and malformed-subprocess scenarios above.

## Risk / Compatibility

Medium compatibility/availability risk at a narrow protocol boundary. Standards-compliant positive safe `Content-Length` frames at or below 64 MiB are unchanged. Invalid values, duplicate fields, headers above 8 KiB, bodies above 64 MiB, and invalid JSON bodies now terminate only the affected bundled LSP session instead of being accepted or left pending.

## What was not changed

- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: no outbound or public contract changes.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: no changes.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: none in the three-dot PR diff.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** the framing boundary used an unanchored regex plus prefix-tolerant integer parsing and had no header/body bounds.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** strict line parsing and size invariants are applied before bytes can alter session framing state or pending-request matching.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — failing reproduction, exact-head focused GREEN, and exact-head real-server/malformed-subprocess proof all bind commit `5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3`.
- **Patch quality notes:** the change reuses existing session failure and process cleanup paths; it adds no new mutable drain/session mode and no unrelated refactor.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** the guard is located in the canonical bundled LSP stdout parser, not in downstream hover/definition tools or generic timeout handling.


Fixes #105675

target.title: fix(agents): tighten lsSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105827

**Problem**: `lsSchema.limit` uses `Type.Number`, which accepts fractional values (e.g. `10.5`) that are semantically invalid for an entry count. This can silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

**Solution**: Change the schema field to `Type.Integer` so the TypeBox schema validator rejects floats before tool logic ever sees them. Export `lsSchema` from the module so tests can validate against the production schema instead of a reconstructed copy.

**What changed**: One character in `src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.ts:28` — `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer`. The test file `ls.limit-schema.test.ts` now imports the production `lsSchema` and validates both valid integers and invalid floats against it. Also exported `lsSchema` (previously module-private `const`) to enable production-schema testing.

**NOT changed**: Tool execution behavior, default limit value (500), `normalizePositiveLimit` clamping logic, any other schema field, the tool registration path, or the tool's runtime behavior. Existing `ls.test.ts` tests continue to pass unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Schema-level rejection of float `limit` values in the production `lsSchema`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
**After-fix evidence**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` → 4/4 passed (see terminal output in Tests section)
**Observed result after the fix**: `Check(lsSchema, { limit: 10.5 })` returns `false`; `Check(lsSchema, { limit: 100 })` returns `true`. Float values are rejected at schema level.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end tool execution with mocked filesystem is covered by existing `ls.test.ts`. Real OpenClaw agent runtime integration is out of scope for this schema-level gate.

## Tests and validation

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw

 ✓ |unit-fast| src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts > ls tool limit schema > rejects float limit — validates against production lsSchema
 ✓ |unit-fast| src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts > ls tool limit schema > accepts various valid integer limits through the full tool path

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Start at  11:00:51
   Duration  568ms

$ pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.test.ts
   (existing tests continue to pass)
```

Validated cases against the production `lsSchema` via `Check()` from `typebox/value`:

| Input | Expected | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `{ path: "/tmp", limit: 100 }` | ✅ accept | passed |
| `{ path: "/tmp", limit: 0 }` | ✅ accept | passed |
| `{ path: "/tmp" }` (optional omitted) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `{ path: "/tmp", limit: 10.5 }` | ❌ reject | passed |
| `{ path: "/tmp", limit: "abc" }` | ❌ reject | passed |
| `{ path: ".", limit: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER }` | ✅ accept | passed |

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — integers previously accepted by `Type.Number` remain accepted by `Type.Integer`
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — production schema validated directly
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — schema is self-documenting via TypeBox types
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

---
