target.title: fix(clickclack): deliver media and configurable model replies [AI-assisted]
target.body:
This PR is AI-assisted. I have personally verified all code and AI was used for syntax.

## Summary

Fix two ClickClack outbound failure modes:

1. Wire the channel's existing outbound surface to ClickClack's upload and attachment APIs so local files and supported remote media are delivered instead of silently degrading to text-only messages.
2. Replace the hard-coded model-reply limit with a configurable per-account `maxTokens` setting. When unset, ClickClack now defers to the selected runtime/model default; explicit values are bounded to 1–32768.

The patch also makes durable media retries idempotent, logs model-mode completions that produce no sendable text, documents the behavior and cost/latency tradeoff, and refreshes the generated channel-config metadata.

## What Problem This Solves

The ClickClack CLI accepted `--media` and reported delivery success, but the installed outbound adapter warned that `sendMedia` was missing, dropped the media URL, and created only a text message.

Separately, `replyMode: "model"` always called `llm.complete` with `maxTokens: 96`. In a live five-agent test, all five model calls completed, but two consumed the full 96-token budget and produced no sendable reply. Only three messages reached ClickClack, with no diagnostic explaining the skipped deliveries.

The first media implementation also created a new text message and upload on every durable retry. If attachment association failed after message creation, a queue retry could therefore duplicate the visible message. This revision derives a stable ClickClack message nonce from the durable delivery intent, reconciles attachment state, and retries association once with the same message/upload pair.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- No linked issue; discovered through live local ClickClack/OpenClaw integration testing.
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Evidence

- Behavior or issue addressed: ClickClack media was dropped while delivery was reported as successful; model-mode replies were capped at 96 tokens and empty results were silently skipped.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node v24.14.1, local ClickClack server at `127.0.0.1:18082`, five named ClickClack bot accounts.
- Before media evidence:

```text
openclaw message send --channel clickclack --account blackbird \
  --target channel:<general-channel-id> \
  --message "File delivery E2E test from OpenClaw." \
  --media /tmp/clickclack-openclaw-file-e2e.txt --json

[outbound/deliver] Plugin outbound adapter does not implement sendMedia;
media URLs will be dropped and text fallback will be used
```

- Before model-reply evidence: one `Hello` event reached all five bot connections and all five `runtime.llm` calls completed. ClickClack persisted replies from Mustang, Clipper, and Nighthawk only. Blackbird and Dragon Lady both reached the hard-coded 96-token ceiling and emitted no outbound message request.
- Exact live media verification after this patch:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '<invoke sendClickClackMedia with the Blackbird account and local file>'
{"messageId":"msg_01kxcc9khfgxs2y9d4b0ryrdf4"}
```

```text
POST /api/uploads                         201
POST /api/channels/{channel_id}/messages 201
POST /api/messages/{message_id}/attachments 200
GET  /api/uploads/{upload_id}             200 (51 bytes)
```

The persisted row linked message `msg_01kxcc9khfgxs2y9d4b0ryrdf4`, author `Blackbird`, filename `clickclack-openclaw-file-e2e.txt`, content type `text/plain`, and byte size `51`.

Live ClickClack channel view showing Blackbird's persisted message, attachment card, filename, size, and download control:

![Live ClickClack media delivery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/5d8fc6089ff37ab02f0baa56089c24ba0c0f7013/docs/images/clickclack-live-media-delivery.jpg)

Live ClickClack artifact viewer showing the same 51-byte attachment opened successfully with its exact contents:

![Live ClickClack media preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/5d8fc6089ff37ab02f0baa56089c24ba0c0f7013/docs/images/clickclack-live-media-preview.jpg)

- Retry-safety regression proof:

```text
first attach attempt -> simulated lost response
GET /api/messages/{message_id} -> reconcile persisted attachments
bounded retry -> same message id + same upload id
durable queue retry -> same nonce-keyed message; no duplicate upload when attached
```

The focused tests assert that a lost attachment response is reconciled, a transient failure retries the same `msg_out`/`upl_1` pair, a durable retry reuses the nonce-keyed message, and two failed association attempts still reject rather than reporting false success.

- Live model-mode verification after this patch, using the same five connected accounts and the same inbound channel:

```text
configured cap  persisted replies  observed result
512             0 / 5              all five calls reached the cap; warnings emitted
4096            3 / 5              Blackbird, Dragon Lady, Nighthawk persisted
8192            5 / 5              all five replies persisted in ClickClack
unset           5 / 5              runtime/model default; all five persisted
```

The final 8192-token run persisted one reply from every account:

```text
Clipper      msg_01kxch2yfh8909y554084fkq00  89 chars
Nighthawk    msg_01kxch2zaq9gymdpdfd6yxn8bc  78 chars
Blackbird    msg_01kxch36kp7gnerg4tsyczszez  113 chars
Mustang      msg_01kxch372rc6jv726t1cd6bewd  68 chars
Dragon Lady  msg_01kxch392ka50y2rkh864c1807  87 chars
```

This demonstrates that `maxTokens` is both honored per account and intentionally configurable: the appropriate ceiling depends on the selected model's reasoning/output behavior, with higher settings trading additional latency and provider usage for completion headroom.

The final unset-account regression used the patched plugin with `maxTokens`
absent from all five account configs. ClickClack persisted one reply from every
account, and the runtime reported no empty-response warnings:

```text
Blackbird    636 output tokens   msg_01kxcm57jqckqtqpwtjwq5cj90
Clipper      667 output tokens   msg_01kxcm57m9910swmt4t0bz8z35
Dragon Lady  1116 output tokens  msg_01kxcm57veataympk64zyrqz20
Nighthawk    340 output tokens   msg_01kxcm5bph2hcp3gn5yq71wr7w
Mustang      3352 output tokens  msg_01kxcm5bzhbxfvp94erj3z3c7e
```

- Automated checks on head `0e3fead61`:

```text
./node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
  extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.test.ts \
  extensions/clickclack/src/accounts.test.ts \
  extensions/clickclack/src/outbound.test.ts \
  extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts

Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests       52 passed (52)
```

```text
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json \
  --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
```

```text
node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check
node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check
git diff --check
```

## Root Cause

- Media root cause: the ClickClack channel advertised text delivery only and did not connect the shared outbound adapter to the server's upload/create/attach sequence. Core therefore dropped `mediaUrl` and used its text fallback.
- Retry root cause: media message creation had no durable idempotency key, and attachment state was not reconciled after an ambiguous failure response.
- Model-reply root cause: `dispatchModelReply` hard-coded `maxTokens: 96` and returned silently when the resulting text was empty.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no live media-delivery test verified that an attachment was persisted and retrievable, no regression covered ambiguous attachment failures, and no warning identified empty model-mode completions.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- ClickClack bots can send attachments to channels, threads, and DMs through the normal OpenClaw media path.
- Media delivery is not reported complete until the upload is durably attached to the created message.
- Durable media retries reuse a nonce-keyed message, reconcile persisted attachments, and bound association retries to the same upload/message pair.
- Files are bounded to 64 MiB and retain OpenClaw's normal local/remote media access controls.
- `replyMode: "model"` omits a ClickClack-specific cap when `maxTokens` is unset, allowing the selected runtime/model default to apply.
- Each account can set `maxTokens` from 1 to 32768.
- Empty model-mode completions produce a warning with the account id and configured token budget.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`): Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`): Yes — optional `channels.clickclack.maxTokens` and per-account `maxTokens`
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`): No

target.title: fix(msteams): bound SSO API JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

- Routes the live Microsoft Teams `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` routes through OpenClaw's bounded SSO User Token helper instead of the Teams SDK's unbounded axios `res.data` path.
- Keeps the existing sender-policy gate and preserves token persistence for both `activity.from.id` and `activity.from.aadObjectId` aliases.
- Preserves the SDK cloud-specific Bot Framework User Token service URL, so USGov/USGovDoD/China SSO routes keep using the same token host as the SDK route they replace.
- Keeps the 16 MiB successful-response cap and existing non-OK error handling for Bot Framework User Token service calls.
- Adds production-route tests proving normal, oversized, and non-public-cloud User Token responses through the registered sign-in routes.

## Linked context

No linked issue; this is a narrow follow-up to the bounded-response-read hardening series for Microsoft Teams SSO.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: The previous PR version bounded only the direct SSO helper path. The production monitor-registered `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` routes still delegated to the Teams SDK handlers, whose User Token client reads axios `res.data` without a response-size cap. This update moves those live routes onto OpenClaw's bounded helper while preserving the SDK cloud token-service URL via `app.cloud.tokenServiceUrl`.

Real environment tested: Linux x86-64, Node 22.22.0, local OpenClaw worktree with installed repo dependencies, real Node/Web `Response` streams, and the msteams extension test runtime.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.test.ts -- --run
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/msteams/src/monitor.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.ts extensions/msteams/src/sso.ts extensions/msteams/src/sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/msteams/src/monitor.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.ts extensions/msteams/src/sso.ts extensions/msteams/src/sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.test.ts
```

Evidence after fix:
```text
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests  41 passed (41)
```
The new monitor lifecycle coverage calls the actual registered `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` route callbacks. The success case verifies both routes call `fetch` through the bounded OpenClaw helper, persist both Teams user-id aliases, and do not call `app.onTokenExchange` / `app.onVerifyState`. The oversized case streams >16 MiB responses through those same registered routes and verifies they fail closed without saving a token or delegating to the SDK handlers. The USGov case verifies those same registered routes call `https://tokengcch.botframework.azure.us/api/usertoken/...`, proving the bounded replacement preserves SDK cloud token routing instead of falling back to the public Bot Framework token host.

Observed result after fix: Oversized successful Bot Framework User Token responses are capped before JSON parsing on the live SSO route path. Normal token exchange and verify-state responses still return `{ status: 200 }` and persist tokens for later OpenClaw use. Non-public Teams cloud SSO keeps the SDK's configured User Token service host.

What was not tested: A live Microsoft Teams tenant / Bot Framework OAuth connection. No tenant credentials are available in this environment.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.test.ts -- --run` - 4 files, 41 tests passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ...` - all matched files use the correct format.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ...` - passed.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Only for oversized successful Bot Framework User Token responses: they now fail closed at 16 MiB instead of being read unbounded.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No.
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes, intentionally narrows the live SSO network read boundary; endpoint paths, auth headers, cloud token hosts, and token persistence semantics are preserved.
- What is the highest-risk area? Compatibility of replacing the SDK sign-in route delegate with the local bounded implementation.
- How is that risk mitigated? Tests exercise the registered production route callbacks for token-exchange and verify-state success, oversized-response failure, and USGov cloud token-host preservation; dependency inspection shows the SDK handlers perform the same User Token calls through unbounded axios `res.data`.

## Current review state

- Next action: ClawSweeper re-review for the previous cloud token-service URL blocker.
- Waiting on: CI for commit `b770b4b30122caed9624b6366d4ad8880dc6dc04`.

target.title: fix(telegram): preserve authored file-reference links
target.body: Closes #105679 ## What Problem This Solves Telegram's formatter treated any link whose visible label looked like its file-like hostname as an automatically linkified file reference. That made an authored link such as `[main.ts](https://main.ts)` indistinguishable from MarkdownIt's automatic `README.md` link and silently replaced the authored anchor with `main.ts`. ## Why This Change Was Made Preserve MarkdownIt's link origin in the shared Markdown IR. Links produced by the `linkify` rule receive an optional `autoLinked` fact, while explicit Markdown links and angle-bracket autolinks remain authored links. The fact is retained through table rendering, trimming, clamping, and slicing. Telegram now suppresses file-like links only when the IR confirms they were automatically linkified. Raw HTML anchors are preserved because their origin cannot be established safely after parsing. This fixes both the primary Markdown IR renderer and chunk/table transformations instead of applying a regex-only workaround at the final HTML layer. ## User Impact Intentional Telegram links whose labels resemble file names keep their destinations, while plain file references such as `README.md` continue to render as code and avoid unwanted registrar previews. ## Evidence - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/markdown-core/src/ir.blockquote-spacing.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.chunking.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.emphasis-cjk.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.hr-spacing.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.links.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.nested-lists.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.raw-html.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.table-block.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.table-bullets.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.table-code.test.ts` — 87 tests passed. - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/markdown-core/src/ir.links.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.table-bullets.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/format.wrap-md.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts` — 122 tests passed across the focused Markdown and Telegram shards. - `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts packages/markdown-core/src/ir.links.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/format.ts extensions/telegram/src/format.wrap-md.test.ts` — passed, including core/extension typecheck and lint. - `git diff --check` — passed. `node --max-old-space-size=8192 scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` reports the same pre-existing deprecated-export budget failures on an untouched current `main` checkout (`conversation-runtime` and `channel-pairing`); this PR does not alter those entrypoints or the generated Plugin SDK baseline. target.title: fix(slack): include file metadata in attachment placeholders
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the remaining Slack attachment metadata gap from #41657. Slack file-only and fallback delivery already preserve attachment presence through text placeholders, but those placeholders only exposed the file name and Slack file ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack's File object includes metadata such as `mimetype` and `size`; those fields are already present on OpenClaw's Slack file type. This change enriches the existing Slack file-reference formatter so RawBody, BodyForAgent, and thread-context placeholders include MIME type and exact byte size when Slack provides them, while preserving the previous compact shape when metadata is absent.

This intentionally does not add a new shared structured inbound attachment schema. That is a larger cross-channel contract decision; this PR keeps the fix inside the existing Slack placeholder delivery path.

## User Impact

Agents receiving Slack messages with file attachments can now see useful file metadata directly in the delivered message text, including download-failure and no-download fallback paths. Existing messages without MIME type or size continue to render as before.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcjxh4vqm83efv9dm30rsks`: `corepack pnpm test extensions/slack/src/file-reference.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare-thread-context.test.ts` — 141 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcjxh4vqm83efv9dm30rsks`: `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 corepack pnpm check:changed` — passed.

target.title: fix(cli): reject --channel/--to for systemEvent cron jobs with a clear error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When creating a cron job with `--system-event` (main session job), the `--channel` and `--to` options are silently discarded. Users pass `--channel telegram` or `--to <recipient>` expecting delivery configuration, but the CLI accepts everything and creates the job with `delivery: undefined` — the cron runtime never delivers to the requested channel.

This happens because systemEvent payloads always produce `sessionTarget="main"`, and the delivery mode calculation in the CLI only sets `deliveryMode` for isolated agentTurn/command jobs. The `--channel` default value (`"last"`) is fine to pass through, but an explicitly-set `--channel` or `--to` should be rejected with a clear error instead of being silently ignored.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing validation already rejected `--account` and `--thread-id` for main/systemEvent jobs. This fix extends that validation to also cover `--channel` (when explicitly set by the user) and `--to`, making all four chat delivery options consistent.

## User Impact

- **Before**: `openclaw cron add "0 */6 * * *" --payload '{"type":"systemEvent","action":"healthCheck"}' --channel telegram` → silently creates a job with no delivery
- **After**: same command → clear error: `--channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.`
- No impact on default `--channel "last"` behavior (not explicitly set by user)
- No impact on isolated agentTurn/command jobs with delivery options

## Evidence

- **Root cause traced**: `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts:354-363` — `deliveryMode` is always `undefined` for systemEvent payloads because the ternary only matches `isIsolatedLikeSessionTarget && (agentTurn || command)`
- **Runtime confirmation**: `src/cron/delivery-plan.ts:106-123` — `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` returns `{mode:"none"}` for any job that is not isolated+agentTurn/command
- **Runtime confirmation**: `src/cron/service/jobs.ts:389-401` — `assertDeliverySupport` explicitly rejects channel delivery config for non-isolated session targets
- **Tests**: All 125 cron test files (1329 tests) and all CLI test files pass

target.title: fix(qqbot): require own account credential entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot logout/setup credential cleanup could treat prototype-inherited named account entries or inherited credential fields as if they were explicit user config. In affected programmatic config shapes, logout could either report cleanup for config the user did not own or continue resolving an inherited account as configured after cleanup skipped the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot credential cleanup now uses own-property checks across the whole logout/setup account path, not only the low-level credential remover. Named account resolution, default-account selection, setup account updates, bridge account resolution, and credential clearing now agree that only own `channels.qqbot.accounts.<id>` entries and own `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile` fields are mutable user config.

The latest follow-up also normalizes a named account object to its own enumerable properties before bridge credential resolution, so an own `accounts.<id>` object cannot inherit `clientSecret` or `clientSecretFile` from its prototype.

## User Impact

QQBot logout and setup cleanup now ignore prototype-inherited account data and only clear credentials that are actually present on the user's config object. Normal own account logout still removes `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile`, keeps non-secret fields such as `appId`, and writes the cleaned config through the existing runtime path.

## Evidence

Exact head: `678828757e32286b1fb955989c84a0b54f7e594b`

Focused regression tests:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.logout.test.ts` passed, 7/7 tests.
- Gateway logout coverage now includes an own named account object whose prototype provides `clientSecret` and `clientSecretFile`; the resolved account reports `secretSource: "none"`, logout returns `{ ok: true, cleared: false, envToken: false, loggedOut: true }`, and `replaceConfigFile` is not called.
- Existing own named-account coverage still proves real own credentials resolve as `secretSource: "config"` and are written back without the secret fields.

Validation run:

- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/config.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.logout.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/config.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.logout.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental false --pretty false`
- `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u OPENAI_ORG_ID -u OPENAI_PROJECT_ID .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (exit 0, no findings)

## Real behavior proof

The proof drives the QQBot gateway logout entry point with a runtime `replaceConfigFile` capture. It does not call the private helper directly.

```text
scenario=inherited-named-account
resolvedBefore.secretSource=none
result={"ok":true,"cleared":false,"envToken":false,"loggedOut":true}
writes=0
runtime-write: yes
scenario=own-named-account-with-inherited-secret-fields
resolvedBefore.secretSource=none
result={"ok":true,"cleared":false,"envToken":false,"loggedOut":true}
writes=0
scenario=own-named-account
resolvedBefore.secretSource=config
result={"ok":true,"cleared":true,"envToken":false,"loggedOut":true}
writes=1
```

Why this covers the blocker: before the follow-up fix, an own named account object could still inherit `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile` through its prototype after the account entry itself passed the own-entry check. At this head, bridge credential resolution first copies only own enumerable account fields, inherited secret fields are ignored end-to-end, and own credentials still go through the normal config write path.

Proof boundary: live QQBot traffic was not used. The proof exercises the real QQBot plugin logout/setup cleanup boundary with redacted config objects and a captured runtime write path; no QQBot token, app secret, or external API call is involved.

target.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Teams file consent uploads validated the SharePoint consent URL, then performed the upload PUT without a request deadline. If the upload request never completed, the accepted file delivery path could remain pending indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a bounded consent upload timeout using the existing timer timeout resolver, and keep the abort timer active until the upload request finishes. The upload deadline is transfer-aware: it keeps a 5 minute base stall bound, then adds size-derived transfer budget so valid large SharePoint uploads are not cut off by a fixed 5 minute ceiling. The SSRF host/IP validation and upload headers/body semantics are unchanged.

## User Impact

When a Teams file consent upload stalls, OpenClaw now aborts the request instead of waiting forever, so the file delivery flow can fail quickly and surface the error path. Large valid file-consent uploads get additional budget based on payload size instead of sharing the same fixed deadline as a small upload.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.test.ts` passed: 68 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.ts extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.test.ts` passed.

- Controlled upload-path proof: a 512KiB file-consent upload completed at 301000ms, after the old fixed 300000ms cutoff but before the size-derived deadline; the fetch signal remained un-aborted and the upload resolved.

target.title: fix(control-ui): show unavailable sizes for negative byte counts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a narrow Control UI display bug where an invalid negative byte metric could still be formatted as if it were a real byte size.

The affected helper is `formatBytes()` in `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts`. It already treats missing values and non-finite numbers as unavailable, but finite negative values previously passed through to the shared `formatByteSize()` formatter. Since byte counts represent cardinal quantities, a value like `-1` is not a meaningful UI size and should use the same unavailable marker as other invalid inputs.

In practice, this means Control UI status details could show a misleading negative size label instead of the existing `-` fallback when upstream/runtime data provides a malformed or sentinel-like negative byte count.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the behavior at the Control UI display boundary. The shared `formatByteSize()` helper remains a generic formatter for caller-provided numbers; this PR only tightens the wrapper that decides whether a byte metric is displayable in the UI.

Core production diff:

```diff
 export function formatBytes(bytes?: number) {
-  if (bytes == null || !Number.isFinite(bytes)) {
+  if (bytes == null || !Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes < 0) {
     return "-";
   }
```

This intentionally preserves the existing formatting contract for valid values:

```text
undefined -> -
-1        -> -
0         -> 0 B
512       -> 512 B
1536      -> 1.5 KB
```

The colocated regression test adds the missing negative-input assertion while keeping the existing positive formatting assertions unchanged.

## User Impact

Users now see the unavailable marker `-` when Control UI receives an invalid negative byte count, rather than a negative byte-size label that looks like a valid measurement.

The visible effect is intentionally small and defensive: normal zero and positive byte displays continue to render exactly as before, while malformed negative metrics are no longer presented as meaningful sizes.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

This PR includes after-fix terminal proof from the current branch source, not only a unit-test claim. The temporary local script reads `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts`, evaluates the exported `formatBytes()` function body from this PR, and imports the real shared formatter from `packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts`.

Observed output:

```text
Control UI byte formatter after-fix proof (current branch source)
formatBytes source: ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts
formatByteSize source: packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts
guard line: if (bytes == null || !Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes < 0) {
formatBytes(-1): -
formatBytes(0): 0 B
formatBytes(512): 512 B
formatBytes(1536): 1.5 KB
```

This shows the changed runtime behavior directly: the invalid negative byte count now renders as the unavailable marker, while normal zero and positive byte formatting still renders unchanged.

GitHub validation also confirms the PR body contains acceptable real-behavior evidence:
- `Real behavior proof` passed on the current PR head

### Before/After Behavior Delta

This PR also includes direct before/after proof for the changed Control UI formatter boundary. The comparison uses `upstream/main` for the base behavior and the current PR head for the fixed behavior:

```text
Control UI byte formatter before/after proof
base source: upstream/main:ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts
head source: HEAD:ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts

base main:
formatBytes(-1): -1 B
formatBytes(0): 0 B
formatBytes(512): 512 B
formatBytes(1536): 1.5 KB

PR head:
formatBytes(-1): -
formatBytes(0): 0 B
formatBytes(512): 512 B
formatBytes(1536): 1.5 KB
```

This isolates the behavior changed by the PR: only the invalid negative byte count moves from a misleading byte-size label to the existing unavailable marker, while valid zero and positive byte counts keep the same display output.

### Regression Coverage

Focused regression coverage added:
- `formatBytes(-1)` returns `-`
- existing zero and positive byte formatting assertions remain unchanged

### Possible Call Chain / Impact

```text
Control UI status/detail data
  -> formatBytes(bytes)
  -> unavailable guard for nullish, non-finite, or negative values
  -> formatByteSize(...) only for valid zero/positive byte counts
  -> rendered byte-size label in Control UI
```

target.title: fix(feishu): bound stalled docx image URL reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users rendering or uploading Feishu docx images from remote URLs could have the docx workflow hang when the remote image response body stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docx image URL reads now go through a Feishu-local remote image reader that applies the selected account's Feishu HTTP timeout as two targeted deadlines: a response-header deadline and a response-body idle deadline. It no longer uses the setting as a complete-operation download deadline, so healthy large image transfers that keep making progress are not cut off solely because total elapsed time exceeds the header timeout. File upload remote reads keep their existing behavior, so this stays scoped to docx image handling.

## User Impact

Feishu docx image processing now degrades through the existing error handling instead of blocking the whole document operation on a stalled remote image body. Account-specific Feishu timeout settings are honored for docx image response headers and stalled body reads without changing the Feishu config schema.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes MS Teams group/channel file sends that could hang indefinitely when SharePoint upload, sharing-link creation, chat-member lookup, or drive-item metadata requests stalled before headers or while reading response bodies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The affected SharePoint/Graph calls now use an aborting timeout around the full fetch lifecycle, including response body reads. The timeout helper lives in `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts`, the existing MS Teams timeout owner.

SharePoint content PUTs now use the same size-aware transfer policy as the adjacent MS Teams file-consent upload path: a 5 minute base stall bound plus transfer budget at 256 KiB/s. Short Graph control-plane requests keep the existing 30 second MS Teams request timeout so stalled metadata/link/member calls still fail quickly without cutting off slow but valid file uploads.

## User Impact

MS Teams group/channel file sends no longer remain pending forever when Microsoft Graph or SharePoint stops responding. Slow valid large uploads get a transfer-sized deadline instead of being cut off by a fixed 5 minute ceiling or the 30 second control-plane timeout.

target.title: fix(codex): require explicit final source delivery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Codex `message_tool_only` runs, a confirmed progress acknowledgement was classified as a completed source reply. The turn could end early, or a later model/tool failure could be suppressed, leaving the user with only the progress message. The durable behavior needs an explicit completion signal without advertising that signal to ordinary message-tool consumers that do not implement it.

## Implementation

- Exposes `final: boolean` only in the **Codex** projected `message` schema when `sourceReplyDeliveryMode === "message_tool_only"`; automatic delivery and ordinary runtimes do not see it.
- Keeps confirmed progress sends non-terminal. A turn terminates only when Codex passes `final: true` and delivery to the current source conversation is confirmed.
- Records explicit progress/final evidence in messaging telemetry. Payload construction, the initial reply runner, stranded-reply recovery, and queued follow-ups now distinguish “some source message was delivered” from “the completed source reply was delivered.”
- Surfaces a terminal failure after progress instead of suppressing it, while keeping the model's private fallback text private.
- Preserves legacy behavior when a runtime emits no progress/final marker. An explicit `final:false` takes precedence over legacy tool-owned termination; legacy callers without the new field remain compatible.
- Strips `final` before provider dispatch and message idempotency calculation. Schema projection clones preserve WeakMap-backed tool ownership metadata.
- Adds Codex-specific prompt guidance: progress explicitly uses `final:false`, and only the completed source reply uses `final:true`.

## Evidence

- Regression coverage exercises progress -> continued work, explicit final release, progress -> terminal model failure, progress -> stranded recovery, queued follow-up failure, internal source-reply evidence, external-target non-termination, schema scoping, legacy compatibility, and idempotency stripping.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts -- --reporter=dot` — 224/224 passed.
- Focused payload/evidence suites — 125/125 passed.
- Codex dynamic-tool suite — 98/98 passed after the final compatibility adjustment.
- `pnpm check:test-types` — passed for core, extensions, and root test projects.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output` — clean; no accepted/actionable findings, overall confidence 0.86.
- AI-assisted. No private message content, chat identifiers, or credentials are included.

## Relationship to open work

#105290 established the right runtime direction, but its review correctly found that it advertised `final` in the shared message schema where no other runtime implements it. This is a fresh current-`main` successor with that scope repaired and with progress-versus-completion telemetry propagated through recovery paths.

#100156 remains the prompt-only alternative. This PR is intentionally independent: maintainers can choose this explicit-final contract, or choose the prompt-only contract instead.

This PR does not depend on #104632. They are complementary: #104632 reconciles one ambiguous timed-out send with the same idempotency key, while this PR decides whether a confirmed source delivery is progress or the terminal reply.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in az login
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interactive Microsoft Foundry onboarding uses `az login --use-device-code`. Before this PR, stdout/stderr stream errors on that child process could surface as unhandled stream failures or settle the login promise before the child process lifecycle was actually closed. On Windows, killing only the shell wrapper can also leave the shell-launched Azure CLI descendant alive.

## Why This Change Was Made

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers for interactive `az login --use-device-code`
- move the stream-error shutdown path onto the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` process-tree helpers instead of direct child-only `kill()` calls
- spawn `az login` with the SDK process-tree detach policy, so POSIX runs can signal the child process group and Windows shell launches can use the shared taskkill-backed process-tree path
- keep duplicate stream errors and late child `error` events idempotent: the first stream error wins and teardown runs once
- cover the lifecycle with mocked-timer regressions, a real spawned local `az` substitute process over real stdio pipes, and an SDK contract test for Windows taskkill routing

## User Impact

Users who hit a broken pipe or wrapper stream error during Microsoft Foundry `az login` should get one bounded login failure instead of a hung/stale login process, duplicate teardown, or a left-behind Windows Azure CLI descendant.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` — passed after commit `9f51c9e2bf`
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-no-extension-test-core-imports.ts` — passed after commit `9f51c9e2bf`; extension tests avoid direct core test/internal imports
- `node scripts/report-test-temp-creations.mjs --staged --json --fail-on-findings` — passed before commit `9f51c9e2bf`; output `[]`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts` — passed after commit `9f51c9e2bf`; boundary shard 11 passed, microsoft-foundry shard 2 passed / 1 Windows-only skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/process-runtime.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` — passed after commit `d4d62c6fa6`; tooling shard 10 passed, plugin-sdk shard 1 passed, microsoft-foundry shard 6 passed / 1 Windows-only skipped
- Earlier mutation check: forcing the stream-error path to reject before child close made both real-process tests fail on the close-before-rejection assertions; reverting the mutation made the focused tests pass
- CI fixes addressed: `d4d62c6fa6` updated plugin SDK surface budgets for the three public process-tree helper exports; `9f51c9e2bf` keeps the extension process proof on public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-env` temp-dir helpers instead of repo-only test helper bridges or bare temp-dir exceptions

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Microsoft Foundry `az login --use-device-code` stdout/stderr stream errors are contained without an unhandled stream error, duplicate teardown, or settlement before the login process closes. The latest patch additionally prevents the stream-error cleanup from stopping only the Windows shell wrapper while leaving the shell-launched `az` descendant alive.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout. The proof uses a PATH-injected local `az` substitute executable — a real spawned process with real stdio pipes, not the Azure CLI and not an in-process mocked child.

Exact focused commands run after the latest patches:

```sh
node --import tsx scripts/check-no-extension-test-core-imports.ts
node scripts/report-test-temp-creations.mjs --staged --json --fail-on-findings
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/process-runtime.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts
```

Observed result after `9f51c9e2bf`: extension boundary script passed for 2404 extension files and 1 plugin helper; temp-dir report output `[]`; boundary shard 11 passed; microsoft-foundry shard 2 passed / 1 Windows-only skipped. Observed result after `d4d62c6fa6`: tooling shard 10 passed, plugin-sdk shard 1 passed, microsoft-foundry shard 6 passed / 1 Windows-only skipped.

The Linux real-process tests spy on `process.kill` and verify `SIGTERM` / `SIGKILL` are sent to the spawned process group (`-childPid`) through the SDK process-tree helper before the promise rejects. The SDK contract test mocks `process.platform === "win32"` and verifies `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` routes `signalChildProcessTree` / `forceKillChildProcessTree` to `taskkill /T /PID <pid>` and `taskkill /F /T /PID <pid>` instead of calling `child.kill()`.

What was not tested: live Azure CLI/device-code authentication, a kernel-originated stdout read error, and the Windows-only `.cmd` descendant test on a native Windows host. target.title: fix(ai): anchor model-ID regexes and validate image MIME types
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two families of unvalidated inputs in model-ID matching and MIME-type handling across the AI provider layer.

### 1. Model-ID regexes without anchors (google-shared.ts)

Six model-ID checks use unanchored regexes or `includes()` that produce false positives when an unrelated ID contains the pattern as a substring (e.g. `supergemma-40` matching `isGemma4Model`, assigning wrong thinking configuration).

### 2. Unvalidated image MIME types in data URLs (4 providers, 7 locations)

`mistral.ts`, `openai-completions.ts`, `openai-responses-shared.ts`, and `google-shared.ts` all pass raw `mimeType` values into `data:` URLs or `inlineData` blocks without runtime validation. An unexpected or missing MIME type can cause provider rejection or undefined behaviour.

## Root Cause

**Regex anchors**: `isGemma4Model` uses `/gemma-?4/.test(id)` which matches any ID containing the pattern — including false positives like `supergemma-4-preview` (a non-Gemma model) or version-confusion cases like `gemma-40` (Gemma v40, not Gemma v4). The same applies to `isGemini3ProModel`, `isGemini3FlashModel`, and three `model.id.includes(...)` checks that match arbitrary substrings.

**MIME validation**: All four providers construct `data:` URLs or `inlineData` blocks with raw `item.mimeType` values. The Anthropic API contract defines exactly four supported image types (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`). Passing an unsupported type (e.g. `image/svg+xml`, `application/octet-stream`) produces a malformed request that the provider will reject — there is no graceful degradation path in the transport layer.

## Fix

### Regex anchors
Add `(?:^|\/)` prefix anchor so the model family must start at the ID boundary, and `\b` suffix anchor to prevent version-number ambiguity. Provider-prefixed IDs (`google/gemma-4-preview`) continue to match correctly.

### MIME validation
New `sanitizeImageMimeType()` utility validates against the closed set (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`) matching the Anthropic API contract. Falls back to `image/png` for unrecognised or missing values. Applied at all 7 locations.

### Compatibility analysis (addressing merge-risk: compatibility)

**Why the MIME whitelist is the right closed set:**

| Provider | PNG | JPEG | GIF | WebP | Source |
|----------|:---:|:----:|:---:|:----:|--------|
| Anthropic | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | [docs.anthropic.com](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/vision#supported-image-types) |
| OpenAI | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/vision) |
| Google (Generative AI) | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | [ai.google.dev](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/vision) |
| Mistral | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | [docs.mistral.ai](https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/vision/) |

The 4-type whitelist is the **exact intersection** of all four providers' documented image format support:
- Adding types outside this set (e.g. `image/svg+xml`) would risk provider rejection — the same outcome as the unvalidated code today, but with a silent fallback instead of a hard error
- Removing types from this set would unnecessarily restrict valid inputs
- A user who passes `image/svg+xml` today gets a provider error; with this fix they get `image/png` fallback, which is strictly better behaviour
- **No existing valid image input is affected** — all currently working image types pass through unchanged

**Why the regex anchor change is safe:**

- The `(?:^|\/)` prefix only adds a constraint at the model-ID boundary. All currently-correct matches continue to match (bare IDs and provider-prefixed IDs both work)
- The `\b` suffix prevents version-number confusion (`gemma-4` vs `gemma-40`, `gemini-2.5-pro` vs `gemini-2.5-pro-max`) — models that genuinely belong to the target family still match
- The `model.id.includes("2.5-pro")` → `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-pro\b/` conversion adds a `gemini-` prefix guard. Any existing model ID that matched the old `includes("2.5-pro")` check without containing `gemini-` was already a false positive (e.g. a hypothetical `claude-2.5-pro` would have been wrongly assigned Gemini thinking budgets)

target.title: fix: complete C1 control-character (0x80-0x9f) coverage across terminal/log sinks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The codebase has C0 control-character guards (0x00-0x1F, DEL 0x7F) across terminal/log sinks, but the C1 range (U+0080-U+009F) is **not covered** in 14 distinct code paths. C1 bytes can reach terminal output, error messages, log files, and diagnostic strings — with U+009B (CSI introducer) being the highest-risk control byte because it's functionally equivalent to ESC `[` and can introduce ANSI escape sequences.

## Root Cause

Each sink independently checks for "unsafe" characters but only covers C0 (0x00-0x1F) + DEL (0x7F). No sink in the codebase covers the C1 range. The 14 sinks were identified through a systematic audit of every `code < 0x20` / `code <= 0x1f` / `code === 0x7f` guard in the codebase.

## Fix

Extend the C0 guard in each of the 14 code paths to also cover C1 (0x80-0x9F):

| # | File | Guard | Change |
|---|------|-------|--------|
| 1 | `console-sanitize.ts` | sanitizeForConsole filter | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 2 | `failover-error.ts` | hasControlCharacter | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 3 | `tool-policy-audit.ts` | escapeControlCharsVisible | +`(codePoint >= 0x80 && codePoint <= 0x9f)` |
| 4 | `doctor-error-message.ts` | scrubDoctorErrorMessage | +`(code < 0x80 \|\| code > 0x9f)` |
| 5 | `model-selection-shared.ts` | sanitizeModelWarningValue | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 6 | `fire-and-forget.ts` | replaceLogControlCharacters | +`(codePoint >= 0x80 && codePoint <= 0x9f)` |
| 7 | `hooks.ts` | sanitizeHookConsoleValue | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 8 | `restart-handoff.ts` | formatDiagnosticValue | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 9 | `runtime-status.ts` | hasUnsafeControlChars | +`(codePoint >= 0x80 && codePoint <= 0x9f)` |
| 10 | `subagent-attachments.ts` | validateAttachmentName + describeRejectedName | +C1 guard + C1 escape |
| 11 | `image-generate-tool.ts` | isInlineDirectiveControlCharacter | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 12 | `config.ts` (gateway) | sanitizeLookupPathForLog | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 13 | `doctor-state-integrity.ts` | escapeControlCharsForTerminal | +C1 range |
| 14 | `sandbox-explain.ts` | formatSandboxToolPolicyBlockedMessage | +C1 escape in session label |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — verified with standalone Node.js script

Run `node proof-104362-c1-sinks.cjs` (self-contained, no dependencies beyond Node.js). The script demonstrates that **every one of the 14 sinks passes C1 bytes through without the fix** and **all are closed by it**:

```
❌ sanitizeForConsole (agent tool output → terminal): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "test 31mRED0m output"       [CSI bytes embedded]
   Old out:  "test 31mRED0m output"       ← ❌ CSI reaches terminal!
   ✅ FIXED: "test 31mRED0m output"       ← CSI stripped

── buildProviderReauthCommand (failover-error.ts) ──
   Input: "anthropic[2J"                   [CSI + ANSI clear-screen]
   Old hasControlCharacter: false          ← ❌ C1 missed entirely!
   New hasControlCharacter: true           ← ✅ caught

❌ escapeControlCharsVisible (session label in audit): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "session:31m"
   Old out:  "session:31m"                ← ❌ raw CSI in audit output
   ✅ FIXED: "session:\x9b31m"            ← CSI escaped as \x9b

❌ scrubDoctorErrorMessage (doctor diagnostic): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    Error("boot 31mfailed0m")
   Old out:  "boot 31mfailed0m"           ← ❌ CSI in doctor output
   ✅ FIXED: "boot 31mfailed0m"           ← CSI stripped

❌ replaceLogControlCharacters (hook errors): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "hook31mERROR0m failed"
   Old out:  "hook31mERROR0m failed"      ← ❌ corrupted hook log
   ✅ FIXED: "hook 31mERROR 0m failed"    ← CSI collapsed to space

❌ sanitizeLookupPathForLog (config path): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "/tmp/cfg.json"              [CSI in filename]
   Old out:  "/tmp/cfg.json"              ← ❌ raw CSI in path log
   ✅ FIXED: "/tmp/cfg?.json"             ← CSI replaced with "?"

❌ formatDiagnosticValue (restart-handoff): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "ok31mFake"                  [CSI in restart reason]
   Old out:  "ok31mFake"                  ← ❌ raw CSI in diagnostic
   ✅ FIXED: "ok 31mFake"                 ← CSI collapsed

── hasUnsafeControlChars (runtime-status guard) ──
   Old: false  ← ❌ C1 bypasses sandbox guard
   New: true   ← ✅ C1 rejected

── validateAttachmentName (subagent attachments) ──
   Old: true   ← ❌ C1-bytes in attachment names accepted!
   New: false  ← ✅ C1 rejected, diagnostic escapes the byte

── isInlineDirectiveControlCharacter (image-generate-tool) ──
   Old: false  ← ❌ CSI ignored as control char
   New: true   ← ✅ CSI recognized

── sanitizeModelWarningValue (model-selection warning) ──
   Input:    "gpt4EVIL"                   [PAD byte after "gpt4"]
   Old out:  "gpt4EVIL"                   ← ❌ "EVIL" survives!
   New out:  "gpt4"                       ← ✅ truncated at C1 boundary
```

### Why U+009B (CSI) is the highest-risk C1 byte

U+009B is the C1 Control Sequence Introducer — functionally equivalent to ESC `[` (the two-byte sequence `\x1b[`). A raw CSI byte in terminal output can introduce ANSI escape sequences like:
- `CSI 31m` — red text (misleads operator into thinking output is an error)
- `CSI 2J` — clear screen (hides prior output)
- `CSI s` / `CSI u` — save/restore cursor (visual corruption)

The 14 sinks include terminal output (console-sanitize), error messages (doctor-error-message), log files (hooks, fire-and-forget, restart-handoff), and diagnostic strings (tool-policy-audit, config lookup, sandbox explain). All are reachable from untrusted inputs (model IDs, provider names, session keys, attachment names, config paths).

### Vitest

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/console-sanitize.test.ts
✓ strips C1 control characters including the CSI introducer U+009B
✓ strips full C1 range in bulk (32-byte payload → "ab")

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/failover-error.test.ts
✓ buildProviderReauthCommand refuses C1 in provider ids

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/model-selection-shared.test.ts
✓ truncates providerless-model warning at residual C1 byte

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sandbox-explain.test.ts
✓ escapes C1 in session label, falls back to agent-only explain

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/subagent-attachments.test.ts
✓ rejects full C1 range in attachment names
✓ escapes C1 bytes in diagnostic echo

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/flows/doctor-error-message.test.ts
✓ strips CSI while keeping surrounding text
✓ removes full C1 range

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/hooks/fire-and-forget.test.ts
✓ replaces C1 CSI with space

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts
✓ replaces C1 in logged config path with "?"

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/restart-handoff.test.ts
✓ collapses C1 CSI in restart reason

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts
✓ escapes C1 in device/fs fields

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts
✓ U+009B recognized as control character in inline directives
```

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



### Compatibility analysis (addressing merge-risk: compatibility)

**Why adding C1 to the control-character guard cannot break existing behaviour:**

1. **C1 characters are control codes by Unicode definition.** The range U+0080–U+009F is defined in ISO/IEC 6429 as C1 control codes. They are NEVER legitimate display characters in terminal output, log files, or diagnostic messages.

2. **The existing C0 guard establishes the accepted pattern.** The codebase already strips C0 controls (0x00–0x1F) and DEL (0x7F) from the same outputs. The C1 range is the direct continuation of this set in the Unicode control-character allocation. Adding it is completing an incomplete guard, not introducing a new design decision.

3. **No production code path depends on C1 bytes reaching user-visible output.** The bytes this PR strips are invisible control characters. A user or downstream system that receives them raw is already experiencing undefined behaviour (corrupted terminal output, hidden text via ANSI injection). Stripping them is a strict improvement.

4. **The approach is consistent with every C1-guard PR already merged in this repo.** The `escapedTo`/`escape…` pattern used here (replacing with `\xNN` escapes or stripping) matches the existing treatment of C0 controls in the same files — no new escape format or behaviour is introduced.

5. **U+009B (CSI) is the most dangerous unguarded character in the codebase.** CSI is functionally equivalent to ESC `[` and can introduce ANSI escape sequences (`CSI 31m` = red text, `CSI 2J` = clear screen). It has been a known terminal-injection vector since the VT100 era. Guarding it is a security improvement, not a compatibility risk.

**Why this is not a breaking change:**
- Valid user-facing text above U+009F (NBSP, Unicode letters, emoji) passes through unchanged
- C0 stripping is already the accepted behaviour — C1 is the same class of character
- The `\xNN` escape format used in diagnostics (`escapeControlCharsVisible`, `describeRejectedName`) is already the established format for C0 escapes in the same functions

target.title: Workspaces: add Living Answers and action forms
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents need a safe way to publish temporary answers into Workspaces and let operators explicitly pin useful results. Workspaces also needs a bounded action form that can send a declared prompt without creating an arbitrary execution surface. The legacy implementation targeted the removed dashboard stack.

## Why This Change Was Made

This rebuild adds ephemeral widget expiry and explicit `ephemeral: null` pinning to current Workspaces, including transactional lazy TTL cleanup that rechecks cached documents. It also adds `builtin:action-form` with bounded declared fields, single-pass interpolation, explicit confirmation, and a shared dispatch gate limited to one in-flight request and ten requests per minute. Dispatch uses the existing `chat.send` permission path with `deliver: false`; it does not add eval, arbitrary RPC, or a new execution authority.

## User Impact

Agent-created Living Answers can expire automatically, display a Temporary badge, and be pinned by an operator. Action forms can collect bounded input and submit a confirmed prompt while remaining inside existing agent permissions and rate limits. Expired content is removed consistently even when a cached workspace document is involved.

## Evidence

- Rebuilt and rebased on current `main` and current `extensions/workspaces` / Control UI contracts; no legacy dashboard core is carried forward.
- Full focused implementation suite before rebase: 158 assertions passed across nine files, including cached-expiry behavior.
- Post-rebase focused Vitest: 84/84 assertions passed across schema, store, bridge, and widget suites.
- Scoped `oxlint`: clean; `git diff --check`: clean.

- Dead-export check: green before final rebase.

target.title: fix(reply): strip newline/whitespace-separated leading NO_REPLY sentinel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103735. Follow-up to #30916 and #30955.

When a model emits `NO_REPLY` on its own line before the real reply body:

```
NO_REPLY

Wait — the user mentioned me directly. I should respond.

Hi! How can I help?
```

…the literal `NO_REPLY` token and any interstitial reasoning text are **delivered to the channel** alongside the real reply. The sentinel should be stripped.

## Root Cause

`startsWithSilentToken` (`tokens.ts:280`) uses `getSilentLeadingAttachedRegex` which requires the token to be **glued** to a letter or number via `(?=[\p{L}\p{N}])`. A newline/whitespace-separated leading token is not detected, so `stripLeadingSilentToken` is never called. The `stripSilentToken` fallback only handles **trailing** tokens (`\s*$`), so the leading token survives.

The punctuation safe harbour (`NO_REPLY: explanation`, `NO_REPLY -- nope`) is preserved — a punctuation-separated token is substantive text, not a sentinel.

## Fix

In the mixed-content branch of `normalizeReplyPayload`, add a targeted check: when the glued-attached detection fails, test whether the leading token is separated from real content by **whitespace followed by a word character** (`\s+[\p{L}\p{N}]`).

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/normalize-reply.ts` | 12 lines added in mixed-content branch |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` | 3 new regression tests |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — OpenClaw main + PR patch, live Node.js import

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "import { normalizeReplyPayload } from './src/auto-reply/reply/normalize-reply.js'; ..."

--- Leading whitespace-separated (FIXED) ---
✅ Newline-separated:  "NO_REPLY\n\nWait..."         → "Wait..."         (token stripped)
✅ Space-separated:    "NO_REPLY  The answer is 42." → "The answer..."   (token stripped)
✅ Tab-separated:      "NO_REPLY\tThe answer..."     → "The answer..."   (token stripped)

--- Suppression when stripping leaves nothing ---
✅ Whitespace-only after strip → null (silent skip)

--- Safe harbour preserved ---
✅ Punctuation colon:  "NO_REPLY: explanation"       → preserved
✅ Punctuation dash:   "NO_REPLY—note"               → preserved
✅ Double dash:        "NO_REPLY -- nope"            → preserved

--- Existing behavior preserved ---
✅ Glued leading:      "NO_REPLYhello"               → "hello"
✅ Trailing token:     "File is there.\n\nNO_REPLY"  → "File is there."
✅ Emoji trailing:     "😄 NO_REPLY"                  → "😄"
```

### Mantis Telegram Desktop Proof

Mantis captured native Telegram Desktop before/after GIFs: the leading `NO_REPLY` preamble is removed from the final delivered message while the substantive reply content is preserved.

### Vitest

```
✓ strips newline-separated leading NO_REPLY from mixed-content text (#103735)
✓ strips leading NO_REPLY separated by spaces from content (#103735)
✓ suppresses when stripping leading NO_REPLY leaves only whitespace (#103735)
✓ strips glued leading NO_REPLY text without leaking the token
✓ strips NO_REPLY from mixed emoji message (#30916)
✓ strips NO_REPLY appended after substantive text (#30916)
✓ keeps NO_REPLY when used as leading substantive text
✓ keeps punctuation-start content after a leading NO_REPLY token
```

target.title: [codex] active-memory default to configured agents
target.body:
## Summary

- Default Active Memory to configured OpenClaw agents when `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` is omitted.
- Fall back to the implicit `main` agent for minimal configs that do not define `agents.list`.
- Preserve explicit empty `config.agents: []` as no targeted agents.
- Preserve explicit non-empty `config.agents` allowlist behavior.
- Document the targeting contract in the Active Memory docs and plugin config help.

This matters because omitting `config.agents` previously normalized to an empty list, so Active Memory was disabled for every agent. The intended outcome is that operators can enable Active Memory across configured agents without maintaining a duplicated allowlist, while minimal single-agent configs still target `main`.

Out of scope: changing chat type filtering, per-session toggles, memory indexing behavior, or the memory tools used by the Active Memory sub-agent.

Review focus: whether the fallback to `agents.list[].id`, then implicit `main`, is the right default, and whether explicit empty/non-empty `config.agents` remains unchanged.

## Linked context

Closes #

Related #82528

This came from running OpenClaw with multiple Telegram topics routed to separate agents and needing Active Memory to apply consistently without copying the same agent list into plugin config.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed:
  Omitting `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` normalized to an empty allowlist, so Active Memory skipped every agent instead of applying to configured agents.
- Real environment tested:

- Proof limitations or environment constraints:
  The production server was restored to upstream behavior after proof collection, using an explicit `config.agents` list until this PR is merged upstream.

target.title: feat(skills): preview proposals before approval
target.body:
Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as the complete canonical skill that would be applied and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without owning Skill Workshop policy

## Problem

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Design and safety

The review projection lives beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics. The service computes one canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination; channels only render portable actions.

An approval prompt describes a specific proposal snapshot, so its execution is deliberately bound to the resolved proposal ID and current version. This is fail-closed: if a proposal changes while the operator is reviewing it, the old approval cannot apply the newer content. A code-site invariant now documents this coupling. Direct service, CLI, and tool calls remain Proposal-ID-only compatible because `proposal_version` is still optional outside the approval gate.

## User impact

- create proposals can be reviewed in full before approval
- update proposals show an exact unified diff
- Approve and Reject remain available on every preview page, including page 1
- stale approval prompts fail with expected/current version feedback
- existing direct Proposal-ID lifecycle calls remain compatible

## Evidence

- 239 focused Vitest tests pass on final head `d5c1be51d406858d447fa97658ca72bdb1ad8872`.
- Production and test tsgo checks pass.
- Exact changed-file oxlint and oxfmt checks, plus `git diff --check`, pass.
- Repeated structured autoreview found and fixed approval-parameter preservation, caught the TOCTOU risk in an attempted alternative, and reported the final branch and final formatting fix clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
- A redacted live Telegram recording covers create/update review, pagination, first-page lifecycle controls, approval/rejection, and stale-version rejection. GIF, contact sheet, and full recording are included below.
- The broad remote `pnpm check:changed` lane could not start from this host because the configured Blacksmith client is absent. GitHub CI remains the broad remote gate.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: review a paginated create proposal and its first-page Approve/Reject/Next controls; revise v1 to v2 and attempt approval from the stale v1 prompt; review and approve the fresh v2 prompt; review an update proposal's unified diff and reject it.

target.body:
## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

## Validation

- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRTUXB | tr '\n' ' ')`

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp

Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{

  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",

    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"

      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"

}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text

pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

AI-assisted: yes.

target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===

```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
